label: S0007
statement: statement: Fiber criterion for reduction-only decoders. Let X,Y be finite, R:X→Y, L:X→{0,1}, and let C_y be nonempty for each y in R(X). There exists a decoder D:Y×C→{0,1} satisfying D(R(x),c)=L(x) for all x∈X and c∈C_{R(x)} if and only if L is constant on every fiber R^{-1}(y). Necessity: if R(x)=R(x')=y, choose c∈C_y; then L(x)=D(y,c)=L(x'). Sufficiency: for each y∈R(X), define D(y,c) to be the common value of L on R^{-1}(y), independent of c; define D arbitrarily outside R(X). Thus the condition is both necessary and sufficient. It isolates the interface needed for a fiber argument, but does not establish that QE* uses it or that a witness selector is efficient.

Sufficiency: for each y with nonempty fiber, set D(y,c) to the common value of L on that fiber; define D arbitrarily on other y. label: S0008
statement: statement: Adaptive-cost prefix selector. Let Y be finite, b≥0, W⊆Y×{0,1}^b, and suppose an extension-query procedure E(y,p) correctly decides whether p extends to z∈{0,1}^b with W(y,z). If the i-th adaptive query costs at most q_i, then for every y having a W-witness, a deterministic selector outputs such a witness using at most b queries and O(b+Σ_{i=1}^b q_i) time. Proof: initialize p=ε, which has a witness extension. For i=1,…,b, query E(y,p0). If true, replace p by p0. Otherwise replace p by p1. In the latter case, by induction p had a witness extension and no witness extends p0, so some witness extends p1. Thus the invariant that p has a witness extension is preserved. At length b, p itself is a witness. The query count is b and the total cost is O(b+Σq_i). This gives an exact adaptive cost bound but does not bound those query costs for QE* witnesses or close G0001.

label: S0011
statement: Lemma (explicit-verifier prefix search). Let Y be finite, b>=0, and W subseteq Y x {0,1}^b. Suppose a deterministic verifier V(y,z) decides membership in W in at most v steps. Given y for which some z satisfies W(y,z), the greedy prefix selector returns such a z using at most b extension checks. Implement each check for a prefix p by enumerating all suffixes u and testing V(y,p||u). The total number of verifier calls is at most 2^b-1, so the running time is O((2^b-1)(v+b)+b^2), including string handling. Proof: Initially the empty prefix has a witness. At prefix p of length i, test whether p||0 has a witness by enumerating its 2^(b-i-1) completions and applying V. If one succeeds, append 0; otherwise the maintained witness extending p must extend p||1, so append 1. Thus after b steps the resulting full string is in W. There are b checks, and their enumeration sizes sum to sum_{i=0}^{b-1} 2^(b-i-1)=2^b-1. The stated bound follows by charging at most v+b per verifier call and O(b^2) for prefix bookkeeping. Scope: this is an explicit upper bound for directly verifiable witness relations; it is exponential in b and does not establish the QE* resource bounds or close OBL-QE-W.

statement: Restricted witness-selector lemma. Let y be an input and suppose its witnesses are exactly the solutions z∈F₂^b of a given linear system A_y z=c_y. For any prefix p, extendibility is decidable by substituting p into the system and testing consistency by Gaussian elimination. Starting with the empty prefix, query extendibility after appending 0; choose 0 if consistent, and otherwise choose 1. Since the current prefix has a solution extension, one of these choices remains consistent. After b choices the resulting string is a witness. The selector uses at most b consistency tests and polynomial time in the input system size.
evidence: Direct invariant proof: before each choice the current prefix has a solution extension; the two possible next bits partition those extensions, so at least one branch remains consistent. Gaussian elimination decides each branch in polynomial time. This is a restricted subclass only; no link to SearchMCSP witnesses or closure of G0001 has been established.

statement: Black-box prefix-query lower bound. For every b>=0, consider hidden z in {0,1}^b and the oracle E_z(p)=1 iff p is a prefix of z. Any deterministic algorithm that identifies z for every hidden z requires at least b oracle queries in the worst case. Proof: each query returns one bit, so a decision tree of depth q has at most 2^q leaves. Correct identification of all 2^b possible hidden strings requires at least 2^b distinct leaves; hence 2^q >= 2^b and q >= b. The bound is attained by querying the successive prefixes along the hidden string, as in prefix self-reduction. Scope: black-box query complexity only; it gives no lower bound on the cost of computing a QE* extension predicate.
proof: Fix b and suppose a deterministic algorithm identifies every hidden z using at most q queries. Its interaction tree has branching factor at most two and depth at most q, hence at most 2^q leaves. Two different hidden strings cannot reach the same leaf, because the algorithm would then output the same string on both and be wrong on at least one. Therefore the tree has at least 2^b leaves, so q>=b. Querying prefixes incrementally identifies z in b queries, proving tightness.

statement: statement: Layered-DAG witness search. Let G=(V,E) be an explicitly supplied directed acyclic graph with layers V_0,...,V_b, edges only from V_i to V_{i+1}, source s in V_0, and accepting set A subseteq V_b. Backward marking decides whether s reaches A in O(|V|+|E|) time; if so, following marked successors outputs a path in O(b) additional time. Proof: mark A; for i=b-1 down to 0 mark v in V_i iff it has an edge to a marked vertex in V_{i+1}. By backward induction a vertex is marked exactly when it has a path to A. Hence s is marked iff a witness path exists. At each marked vertex before V_b choose a marked successor, which yields an accepting path. Each vertex and edge is scanned at most constantly many times. Scope: explicit layered-DAG representation only; no such representation is established for the QE* witness relation.

label: S0015
statement: statement: Depth-sensitive prefix selector lemma. Let Y be a finite set, b≥0, and W⊆Y×{0,1}^b. For each y and prefix p of length i≤b, define E(y,p)=1 iff some z∈{0,1}^b extending p satisfies (y,z)∈W. Suppose an exact deterministic procedure answers every E(y,p) query at depth i in time at most q_i. Then for every y having a W-witness, a deterministic algorithm outputs such a witness in at most b queries and time at most Σ_{i=0}^{b-1}q_i+O(b), plus output handling. Proof: initialize p=ε; by hypothesis E(y,ε)=1. At depth i<b query E(y,p0). If it is 1, replace p by p0. Otherwise replace p by p1. The invariant E(y,p)=1 is preserved: in the second case some witness extends p, and none extends p0, so every witness extending p must extend p1. After b iterations p has length b and E(y,p)=1, which by definition means (y,p)∈W. The time bound is the sum of the b query bounds and O(1) per query/update. If b=0, the premise E(y,ε)=1 directly gives (y,ε)∈W and the empty sum applies.

statement: statement: Exhaustive suffix implementation of prefix extension. Let Y be finite, b≥0, W⊆Y×{0,1}^b, and let V(y,z) decide membership in W in time at most v for every y,z. At a prefix p of length i<b, E(y,p) can be computed by enumerating all 2^(b−i) suffixes and applying V, in time at most 2^(b−i)v plus enumeration overhead. Consequently, the prefix selector that tests E(y,p0) at depths i=0,…,b−1 finds a witness whenever one exists, using at most (2^b−1)v verifier time plus enumeration and selector overhead. Proof: For each tested p0 at depth i, exactly 2^(b−i−1) strings extend p0, so the verifier work summed over depths is v·Σ_{i=0}^{b−1}2^(b−i−1)=v(2^b−1). Each query is exact by exhaustive enumeration. The selector preserves the invariant that its current prefix has a W-witness extension: if p0 has one, append 0; otherwise, since p has one, a witness extends p1. After b choices the full string is a witness. For b=0, no suffix queries are needed and the initial empty prefix is already a witness under the premise. Scope: this is conditional on the stated verifier and gives an exponential exhaustive implementation; it establishes no useful QE* resource bound and closes no QE* reduction obligation.

label: S0017
statement: statement: Explicit-witness-list selector bound. Let b be a nonnegative integer and let W be a nonempty explicitly listed subset of {0,1}^b, with L=|W|. A deterministic algorithm returns a member of W using at most b prefix-extension queries, each answered by scanning the list, in O(b^2 L) bit comparisons and O(b) extension queries. Proof: initialize the empty prefix p. For each i=0,...,b-1, scan W to determine whether some w in W has prefix p0. If so set p:=p0; otherwise set p:=p1. Inductively p is a prefix of some member of W: this holds initially; if the scan finds an extension by 0 it remains true, and if not, the maintained witness must extend by 1. After b iterations p is a length-b member of W. Each iteration compares at most L strings against a prefix of length at most b, costing O(bL), hence the total O(b^2L). The algorithm is correct for all nonempty W, including b=0, where W={empty string} and no scans are needed.

structure.evidence: Constructive direct-list algorithm and induction proof; a finite verification was requested independently on all nonempty witness relations through b=4. This bound depends on the explicit witness-list size L and therefore does not establish the required QE* resource bound.

statement: statement: Prefix-count selector lemma. Let Y be finite, b≥0, and W⊆Y×{0,1}^b. Define the prefix-count oracle C(y,p)=|{z∈{0,1}^b : W(y,z) and p is a prefix of z}|. For any y with C(y,ε)>0, a deterministic algorithm finds z with W(y,z) using at most b oracle queries: at each step, query C(y,p0), append 0 if the answer is positive, and otherwise append 1. Proof: maintain C(y,p)>0, true initially by hypothesis. If C(y,p0)>0, the invariant holds after appending 0. Otherwise, since every extension of p begins with either 0 or 1 and C(y,p)>0, C(y,p1)=C(y,p)>0, so it holds after appending 1. After b steps p has length b; its only length-b extension is itself, hence C(y,p)>0 implies W(y,p). This includes b=0, where the initial positive count already certifies the empty string. The lemma reduces witness selection to exact prefix counting; it gives no resource bound for implementing that counting oracle for QE* witnesses.

structure.evidence: Complete induction proof is included in the statement. This is a constructive selector using exact prefix counts rather than explicit witness-list scans or Boolean extension queries; it isolates exact counting as a sufficient implementation target, without asserting that QE* admits an efficient counter.

label: S0019
statement: statement: Prefix-extension selector interface lemma. Let b be a nonnegative integer, Y any set, W a subset of Y × {0,1}^b, and E(y,p)=1 exactly when there exists z∈{0,1}^b extending p with (y,z)∈W. For each fixed y with a W-witness, the following deterministic procedure outputs z with (y,z)∈W using at most b calls to E and O(b) additional bit operations: start with p=ε; for i=1,…,b query E(y,p0); if the answer is 1 set p←p0, otherwise set p←p1; output p. Proof: inductively, before iteration i, p is a length-(i−1) prefix having at least one W-extension. Initially this holds by the assumed witness. If E(y,p0)=1 then p0 has an extension; if it is 0, the maintained existence of an extension of p implies that every such extension begins with 1, so p1 has an extension. Thus the invariant holds after each iteration. At i=b, the length-b string p is its own only extension, hence (y,p)∈W. There is one E query per bit and only linear work to append/read bits. Scope: exact deterministic search conditional on an exact extension predicate; it does not bound E's computation time/space or prove that QE* supplies E within its resource limits.

label: S0020
statement: statement: Fixed-fiber advice-pattern capacity. Let F be any finite set, s>=0, and D:{0,1}^s x F->{0,1}. Define P_a:F->{0,1} by P_a(x)=D(a,x). Then |{P_a:a in {0,1}^s}|<=2^s. Proof: the map a |-> P_a has domain {0,1}^s, which has cardinality 2^s; its image therefore has cardinality at most 2^s. In particular, any labeling of F outside this family cannot be represented by this fixed decoder with s advice bits. Scope: a capacity bound for decoders whose varying input across F is only a; it does not imply label constancy, efficient advice construction, or a QE* reduction.

statement: statement: Constructive missing-label consequence of fixed-decoder capacity. Let F be a finite set with |F|=f, s>=0, and D:{0,1}^s x F->{0,1} be fixed. If s<f, there exists a labeling L:F->{0,1} that no advice string realizes, and it can be found by enumerating the 2^f labelings and rejecting those among P_a(x)=D(a,x), in at most 2^f * 2^s * f bit evaluations plus lexicographic bookkeeping. Proof: the image family P={P_a} has size at most 2^s, while the set of all labelings has size 2^f. Since s<f, 2^s<2^f, so P is a proper subset. Enumerate labelings in lexicographic order, compare each to all P_a, and return the first absent pattern; at least one exists by the strict cardinality inequality. statement:
statement: Deterministic bounded-witness selector lemma. Let X,Y be finite sets, R:X→Y, and L:X→{0,1}. Suppose each relevant T has at least one witness w of length at most b(T), and a deterministic verifier V(T,w) accepts exactly the admissible witnesses in time at most v(T). Suppose D(x,w) runs in time at most d(x) and equals L(x) for every x and every admissible witness of R(x). Then L is decidable by enumerating all strings w of length at most b(R(x)), returning the first accepted witness, and applying D. The running time is at most (2^{b+1}-1)v(R(x))+d(x)+time(R), where b=max_T b(T) over the relevant outputs. In particular, this gives a polynomial-time decision procedure when these quantities and 2^b are polynomially bounded. Proof: for T=R(x), the enumeration includes an admissible witness by hypothesis; exactness of V ensures the selected string is admissible. The universal correctness assumption on D then gives D(x,w)=L(x). The time bound counts every tested string and the final decoder call. This lemma requires deterministic verification within the stated bound; witness length alone does not imply efficient selection.

label: S0023
statement: statement: Tight black-box query bound for prefix-extension search. For each integer b >= 0, let the hidden witness be z in {0,1}^b and give a deterministic algorithm oracle access only to E_z(p)=1 iff p is a prefix of z, for arbitrary binary strings p (including the empty string). If the algorithm must output z correctly for every hidden z, then its worst-case number of oracle queries is at least b. The bound is attained by querying the b prefixes 0, 1, ..., z_{<b}0 successively as in the standard bit-by-bit selector (for b=0, output the empty string with zero queries). Proof: The oracle E_z is exactly membership in the set of prefixes of z. Any deterministic algorithm making at most q yes/no queries has at most 2^q possible answer transcripts and hence at most 2^q possible outputs as functions of the transcript. Correctness for all 2^b possible z requires at least 2^b distinct output transcripts, so 2^q >= 2^b and q >= b. Conversely, after a known prefix p of z, query E_z(p0); append 0 on yes and 1 on no. This identifies each next bit in one query, yielding z in b queries. Scope: black-box query complexity only; the oracle may be computationally expensive, so this gives no QE* resource bound and does not show the extension predicate itself is hard.

statement: For any explicitly known nonempty finite set W⊆{0,1}^b fixed in advance, a selector can return a member of W with zero oracle queries.

statement:
statement: Hidden-singleton prefix-query complexity. For every integer b>=1, let an unknown witness w range over {0,1}^b, and let the only allowed query be E(p)=1 iff p is a prefix of w, for any binary string p of length at most b. Any deterministic adaptive algorithm that identifies w for every possible w requires at least b queries in the worst case; querying the prefixes of lengths 1,...,b achieves b queries.
proof: For the lower bound, consider the binary decision tree of a deterministic algorithm. Each query has two possible answers, so a depth-d tree has at most 2^d leaves. Correct identification of each of the 2^b possible witnesses requires at least 2^b distinct leaves, hence d>=b. For the upper bound, query the length-i prefix of the bits already recovered followed by 0, for i=1,...,b. A yes answer sets bit i to 0; a no answer sets it to 1, since the hidden witness is known to exist and its preceding bits have already been recovered. After b queries all bits are determined.
scope: Exact deterministic worst-case query complexity in the hidden-singleton prefix-membership oracle model. It does not establish that a QE* witness relation is hidden, singleton-valued, or inaccessible by other computations, so it does not close the QE* obligation.
diagnostic: The oracle property is relativizing and localizing; the argument is combinatorial and does not yield a natural property or algebraic circuit lower bound. No P!=NP progress is claimed.

statement:
statement: Depth-sensitive prefix-extension selector. Let Y be finite, b>=0, W subseteq Y x {0,1}^b. Suppose for every relevant y and every prefix p of length i<b, E(y,p)=1 iff p extends to z with W(y,z) can be computed in time at most q_i. Given y with a W-witness, a deterministic algorithm finds one using at most b extension queries and time O(b + sum_{i=0}^{b-1} q_i). Proof: begin with empty prefix p, which has a witness extension by assumption. At depth i, query E(y,p0). If true, replace p by p0; otherwise replace p by p1. In the latter case the invariant supplies an extension of p and the failed query rules out p0, so p1 has an extension. Thus after each query the invariant holds. At depth b, p is a full-length string with W(y,p), and the sum of query costs plus O(b) bookkeeping gives the stated bound. Scope: conditional selector bound only; it does not prove the QE* extension predicate has these costs.
proof: The invariant is that the current prefix p has some extension z with W(y,z). Initially this follows from the assumed existence of a witness. If E(y,p0)=1, choose p0 and preserve the invariant. If E(y,p0)=0, an extension of p exists by the invariant, and none extends p0; since the next bit is binary, an extension must extend p1. After b iterations the prefix has length b, so its only extension is itself and it satisfies W. There is one query at each depth i, costing at most q_i, plus O(b) prefix-management time.

label: S0027
statement: statement: Verifier-to-extension bound for fixed-length witnesses. Let Y be a finite input set, b>=0, and W subseteq Y x {0,1}^b. Suppose a deterministic verifier V(y,z) decides membership in W and runs in at most T(y,b) time on every z of length b. For each prefix p of length i<=b define E(y,p)=1 iff some z in {0,1}^b extending p satisfies V(y,z)=1. Then E is computable in at most 2^(b-i) (T(y,b)+O(b)) time, up to polynomial overhead for enumerating and supplying suffixes. Consequently, on any y having a W-witness, the binary prefix selector finds one in at most b queries and total time O(b + sum_{i=0}^{b-1} 2^(b-i-1)(T(y,b)+b)); in particular this is O(2^b(T(y,b)+b)). If b <= c log_2 s and T(y,b) <= s^d for fixed constants c,d, the selector runs in polynomial time in s. Proof: for fixed (y,p), enumerate all 2^(b-i) suffixes u of length b-i and run V(y,pu); return 1 upon the first acceptance and 0 if all reject. This is exactly E by its definition and uses at most 2^(b-i) verifier calls, each costing T(y,b), plus O(b) per candidate to form or manage the string, yielding the stated bound. Apply the prefix-selector invariant: initially the empty prefix has a witness; at depth i query E(y,p0), retain p0 if true, otherwise retain p1, which must have an extension because p has one and p0 has none. After b stages the prefix is itself a verified witness. Summing the query bounds gives O(b + (T+b) sum_{i=0}^{b-1}2^(b-i-1)) = O(b+ (T+b)(2^b-1)) = O(2^b(T+b)). Finally, if b<=c log_2 s, then 2^b<=s^c, so the bound is polynomial in s. Scope: this supplies a sufficient condition for a polynomial-time witness selector, conditional on a polynomial-time verifier and logarithmic witness length; it does not establish that QE* has logarithmic-length witnesses or a QE*-specific verifier bound.

statement:
statement_start: Conditional rank lemma for minimal unsatisfiable positive exact-one systems. Let E be a finite minimal unsatisfiable family of clauses, each on three distinct variables, and let A_E be its incidence matrix over F_3 on the occurring variables. If A_E z = 1 is solvable over F_3, then rank(A_E)=|E| and |E|≤n′−1.
proof: Suppose the rows are dependent: choose coefficients λ_i, not all zero, with Σ_i λ_i r_i=0, and choose j with λ_j≠0. A solution z to A_E z=1 gives Σ_i λ_i=0, hence Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=−λ_j. For any Boolean assignment x satisfying every clause other than j, the dependence gives λ_j(r_j·x)=−Σ_{i≠j}λ_i(r_i·x)=−Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=λ_j in F_3, so r_j·x=1 mod 3. The integer sum of the three Boolean entries in clause j is in {0,1,2,3}; the only value congruent to 1 mod 3 is 1. Thus x also satisfies clause j, contradicting minimal unsatisfiability. Therefore the rows are independent and rank(A_E)=|E|. Every row sums to 3=0 in F_3, so the nonzero all-ones vector on the n′ occurring variables lies in ker(A_E); rank-nullity yields |E|≤n′−1. For the cited four clauses on four variables, each column sum is 3=0 while the RHS sum is 4=1, so A_E z=1 is inconsistent; that example does not refute this conditional lemma.

statement:
statement_start: Let E be a finite inclusion-minimal unsatisfiable family of positive exact-one clauses, each on three distinct occurring variables, and let A be its incidence matrix over F_3. If Az=1 is solvable, then rank_F3(A)=|E| and |E|≤n'−1.

From Σ_i λ_i r_i=0 and Az=1, dotting with z gives Σ_i λ_i=0, hence Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=−λ_j. Inclusion-minimal unsatisfiability ensures E\{C_j} is satisfiable; choose a Boolean assignment x satisfying all its clauses. Dotting the row dependence with x gives 0=Σ_i λ_i(r_i·x)=λ_j(r_j·x)+Σ_{i≠j}λ_i, since r_i·x=1 for i≠j. Thus λ_j(r_j·x)=−Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=λ_j, so r_j·x=1 in F_3. The integer sum of the three Boolean entries in C_j belongs to {0,1,2,3}; its only value congruent to 1 modulo 3 is 1. Hence x satisfies C_j too, contradicting that E is unsatisfiable. Therefore the rows are independent and rank(A)=|E|. Each row has exactly three 1s, so A times the all-ones vector is zero in F_3. This vector is nonzero because n'≥3, hence nullity(A)≥1. Rank-nullity gives |E|=rank(A)≤n'−1. For the proposed four-clause instance on four variables, each column sum is 3≡0 while the four right-hand sides sum to 4≡1. Summing its equations would imply 0=1, so that instance violates the solvability premise and does not refute this conditional lemma.

statement:
statement: For every De Morgan formula Phi with each variable occurring at most once, and every restriction distribution under which each variable is live with probability p, if L(Phi|rho) is the number of variable-leaf occurrences after restriction and size-nonincreasing simplification, then E[L(Phi|rho)] <= p L(Phi).
proof: Let I_i be the indicator that variable x_i is live. Since each variable occurs at most once, before simplification the number of live variable leaves is exactly sum_i I_i. The stipulated simplification does not increase the number of variable leaves, so pointwise L(Phi|rho) <= sum_i I_i. Taking expectations and using linearity, E[L(Phi|rho)] <= sum_i E[I_i] = p L(Phi). No independence is required.
scope: Read-once De Morgan formulas; variable-leaf count; restrictions with uniform marginal live probability p; simplification must not increase formula size.

The stipulated simplification does not increase the number of variable leaves, so pointwise L(Phi|rho) <= sum_i I_i. Taking expectations and using linearity, E[L(Phi|rho)] <= sum_i E[I_i] = p L(Phi). No independence is required.
scope: Read-once De Morgan formulas; variable-leaf count; restrictions with uniform marginal live probability p; simplification must not increase formula size.

label: S0002
statement:
statement: Let Phi be a De Morgan formula with L variable-leaf occurrences, each variable occurring at most once. Let rho be any random restriction, and for each leaf i let p_i be the probability that its variable remains live. If L(Phi|rho) counts variable-leaf occurrences after restriction followed by simplification that never increases that count, then E[L(Phi|rho)] <= sum_{i=1}^L p_i.
proof: For each leaf i define I_i(rho)=1 if its variable remains live and 0 otherwise. Before simplification the number of live variable leaves is exactly sum_i I_i because Phi is read-once. By the stipulated simplification rule, pointwise L(Phi|rho) <= sum_i I_i(rho). Taking expectations and applying linearity gives E[L(Phi|rho)] <= sum_i E[I_i] = sum_i p_i. No independence among the live indicators is required.
scope: Read-once De Morgan formulas, variable-leaf occurrence count, arbitrary random restrictions with possibly different live probabilities by leaf, and simplifications that do not increase that count.

label: S0003
statement: statement: Let N≥2 and Φ be a formula tree with L input-variable leaf occurrences. Under any random restriction, suppose every input leaf remains live with probability p=N^{-a_N}, where a_N≥0. Let X be the number of surviving input-leaf occurrences before simplification, and X' any count after a simplification that only deletes leaves. Then E[X']≤pL=N^{a_N}p²L. In particular, if a_N→0, the pL bound is absorbed into N^{o(1)}p²L. Proof: write X=Σ_{j=1}^L I_j for the leaf survival indicators. Pointwise X'≤X, so linearity gives E[X']≤E[X]=Σ_j E[I_j]=pL. Since p=N^{-a_N}, pL=N^{a_N}p²L, and N^{a_N}=N^{o(1)} when a_N→0. No independence assumption is needed. This repairs the single-leaf obstruction only in the stated lower-marginal regime; it gives no bound on residual formula size or reused-gate leaves.

label: S0004
statement:
statement: Let C be a finite acyclic Boolean circuit DAG with g gate nodes, and let rho assign constants to any subset of its input variables. Perform semantics-preserving constant propagation by processing nodes topologically, replacing any gate whose output is determined by a constant and redirecting references to it. The resulting DAG has at most g gate nodes. If this DAG is unfolded into a formula tree, its gate-occurrence count equals the sum, over surviving DAG nodes v, of the number of occurrences of v in that unfolding.
proof: Process the original nodes in topological order. Each node is either retained as one gate or replaced by a constant; redirects change edges and create no nodes. Thus the resulting DAG has no more gate nodes than the original. In the unfolding, each tree occurrence is a copy of exactly one DAG node. Partitioning the tree's gate occurrences according to their source DAG node gives the stated sum.
scope: DAG gate count after constant propagation and the definitional identity for formula unfolding multiplicities. This does not bound the multiplicities or their expectation under any restriction, and does not close the route's almost-formula correlation obligation.

label: S0004
statement: LEMMA (anti-concentration over subset sums). Let a_1..a_N be nonzero integers, x_j iid uniform in {0,1}, c = sum a_j x_j. For integers a and L >= 0: P(c in {a,...,a+L-1}) <= L*C(N,floor(N/2))/2^N <= L/sqrt(N). PROOF: Erdos (1945): for reals |a_j|>=1, any open interval J of length 1 contains the subset sums of at most C(N,floor(N/2)) subsets. Each integer v lies in the open interval (v-1/2, v+1/2), so #{S : c_S = v} <= C(N,floor(N/2)); sum over the L integers and divide by 2^N. For the second inequality use C(2k,k) <= 4^k/sqrt(pi k): if N=2k then pi k = pi N/2 >= N; if N=2k+1 then C(2k+1,k) = C(2k+2,k+1)/2 <= 4^{k+1}/(2 sqrt(pi(k+1))), so the ratio is <= 1/sqrt(pi(k+1)) <= 1/sqrt(2k+1). COROLLARY (bottom gate). Let g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with integers |w_j| <= B, R a set of r variables, F the rest, c = sum_{j in F} w_j x_j. Put lo = sum_{j in R} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in R} max(w_j,0). Then g is decided under the restriction (constant over all completions of x_R) iff c >= t-lo or c < t-hi. So g is undecided iff t-hi <= c < t-lo, an integer window of exactly L = hi-lo = sum_{j in R}|w_j| <= rB integers. Applying the lemma with N = N_F gives P_{x_F}(undecided) <= min(1, rB/sqrt(N_F)). Summing over the m bottom gates gives E[#undecided] <= sum_g min(1, rB/sqrt(N_F(g))). SCOPE / WHAT IS NOT CLAIMED: the bound is worst-case over weights with |w|<=B and integer; it needs many nonzero free weights (N_F large) and says nothing for sparse gates; it bounds only the bottom layer; no running time follows yet (the top gate is not handled). KNOWLEDGE vs ALGORITHMIC: knowledge = the restriction bound with its threshold r ~ sqrt(n)/B (explains the refuted fixed-p experiments: for r = pn the bound is ~pB sqrt(n) >= 1); algorithmic gain = none yet. NOVELTY: the Erdos theorem is classical; the new content is the application to restricted THR gates and the regime boundary. The exact per-gate check is run in the next computation.

structure.lemma: Restriction lemma for bottom THR gates (Erdos-Littlewood-Offord form): for integer weights |w_j| <= B, a set R of r variables, and x_F uniform on the rest, P(gate undecided) <= min(1, sum_{j in R}|w_j| / sqrt(N_F)) <= rB / sqrt(N_F), where N_F = #{j in F: w_j != 0}. In particular the undecided fraction is O(rB/sqrt(n)) when N_F >= n/2, so it tends to 0 for r = o(sqrt n). The regime r ~ sqrt(n)/B is the threshold where the bound stops being useful.

structure.lemma: Theorem C (bounded-weight switching bound for one bottom THR gate). Setting: g(x)=[sum_i w_i x_i >= t] on {0,1}^n, integer weights, nz = number of nonzero weights, M = max|w_i| >= 1. Random restriction R_p: each variable free independently with probability p, otherwise fixed to 0 or 1 with probability (1-p)/2 each. Claim: for 0 < p <= 1/4, P(restricted g is non-constant) <= exp(-p nz/3) + 2 sqrt(2) M p sqrt(nz). Corollary: p = 1/(16 M sqrt(nz)) with sqrt(nz) >= 126 M gives P(non-constant) <= 1/4. Proof: Lemma A (Sperner): for nonzero integers a_1..a_k and uniform eps in {0,1}^k, P(sum a_i eps_i = v) <= C(k, floor(k/2))/2^k <= 1/sqrt(k) for every v (flip eps_i where a_i<0; the sets with a given sum form an antichain). Lemma B: given the free set F, the non-constancy window of the restriction lemma has W_F integers, so P(non-constant | F) <= W_F/sqrt(k) <= M s/sqrt(k), with s = number of free nonzero-weight variables and k = nz - s >= 1. Chernoff: P(s > 2 p nz) <= exp(-p nz/3). On s <= 2 p nz (and p <= 1/4) we have k >= nz/2, giving conditional bound 2 sqrt(2) M p sqrt(nz). Take the expectation over s.
structure.proved_step: Theorem C as stated in the lemma field, proof by Lemma A (Sperner), Lemma B (window count) and Chernoff; independent exact check submitted this turn (see experiment record)

label: S0010
statement:
LEMMA (Exact undecided probability under random restriction with uniform threshold). Let g(x) = [∑_{i=1}^n w_i x_i ≥ t] be a threshold gate with integer weights w_i, S = ∑ |w_i|. Let R_p be the random restriction: each variable is free independently with probability p, otherwise fixed to 0 or 1 with probability (1-p)/2 each. Let the threshold t be chosen uniformly from {t_min, ..., t_max} where the interval length L = t_max - t_min + 1 satisfies L ≥ S (in particular, t uniform on [-S, S] works). Then P_{R_p, t}[g|R_p is non-constant] ≤ p, with equality when L = S and the threshold range matches the possible sums exactly.

PROOF. For a fixed restriction ρ, let F be the set of free variables. The restricted gate is g_ρ(y) = [∑_{i∈F} w_i y_i ≥ t - ∑_{i∉F} w_i ρ(i)]. This is non-constant iff the threshold t falls in the interval I_ρ = (L_ρ, U_ρ] where L_ρ = ∑_{i∈F: w_i<0} w_i, U_ρ = ∑_{i∈F: w_i>0} w_i. The length of I_ρ is U_ρ - L_ρ = ∑_{i∈F} |w_i| =: W_F. Since t is uniform over an interval of length L ≥ S ≥ W_F, P_t[g_ρ non-constant] = W_F / L ≤ W_F / S. Now take expectation over R_p: E[W_F] = ∑_i |w_i| · P(i free) = p S. Thus P_{R_p,t}[undecided] = E[W_F/L] ≤ E[W_F/S] = p. Equality holds when L = S and the threshold distribution is uniform over exactly S+1 consecutive integers covering the full range of possible sums. ∎

statement: Lemma R1 as stated in the lemma field: Kolmogorov-Rogozin reduction of the unbounded-weight restriction probability to the expectation in F of min(1, L_F/sqrt(S_F)).

If R2 holds then P(nonconst) <= C' p sqrt(nz), which is the candidate per-gate bound and gives the k/sqrt(n) shape of G0001 when p = k/n. Support so far: numerical only (desk test in progress). structure.lemma: Lemma R1 (Kolmogorov-Rogozin reduction, unbounded weights). Let a_1..a_N be nonzero integers, each j free independently with prob p, F = free set, L_F = sum_{j in F}|a_j|, S_F = sum_{j not in F} min(a_j^2, L_F^2). Then P(gate nonconstant) <= sqrt(8) * A * E_F[min(1, L_F / sqrt(S_F))], where A is the universal Kolmogorov-Rogozin constant. Proof: condition on F. Nonconstancy means X = sum_{j not in F} a_j u_j (u_j iid uniform bits) lies in a window of exactly L_F consecutive integers. Apply Rogozin with L = L_F and L_j = min(|a_j|/2, L). Each X_j = a_j u_j has Q_j(L_j) <= 1/2, since an interval of length < |a_j| contains at most one of {0, a_j}. Hence sum L_j^2 (1 - Q_j) >= (1/8) S_F, which gives the bound.
structure.proved_step: Lemma R1 as stated in the lemma field: Kolmogorov-Rogozin reduction of the unbounded-weight restriction probability to the expectation in F of min(1, L_F/sqrt(S_F)).

label: S0018
statement: Lemma (heavy-split restriction bound, repair of G0008). Setting: g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t], integer weights w_j, any integer t, n variables, nz = #{j : w_j != 0}. Fix tau >= 1 and H = #{j : |w_j| > tau}. Let F be a uniform k-subset of variables, 1 <= k <= nz/2, and fix the other variables to uniform bits. Then P[restriction of g is non-constant] <= k*H/n + A*(tau*k + 1)*sqrt(2/(nz - k)), where A is the absolute constant of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin inequality (cited; exact constant and statement to be source-checked). Proof: (1) Let E = {F contains a heavy variable}. P(E) <= E[#heavy in F] = k*H/n by a union bound. (2) On the complement of E, every j in F has |w_j| <= tau, so W_F := sum_{j in F} |w_j| <= tau*k. (3) Given F, the restriction is non-constant iff c := sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j lies in the integer window [t - hi, t - lo), where hi, lo are the positive and negative parts summed over F; this window has W_F integer points. (4) Let r = #{j not in F : w_j != 0} >= nz - k. Each summand w_j x_j takes values 0 and w_j, so its sup-probability on any half-open integer interval of length 1 is at most 1/2. Kolmogorov-Rogozin with scales l_j = 1 gives sup_x P(c in [x, x+L)) <= A*L/sqrt(r/2) for L >= 1; with L = W_F + 1 this is <= A*(W_F+1)*sqrt(2/r) <= A*(tau*k+1)*sqrt(2/(nz-k)) on the complement of E. (5) Combine: P(nonconst) <= P(E) + sup over the complement = k*H/n + A*(tau*k+1)*sqrt(2/(nz-k)). QED (modulo source-check of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin statement). The bound does not depend on the maximum weight M.

Worst per-F ratio P*sqrt(r/2)/(W_F+1) = 0.306, consistent with A = 1. Worst ratio of averaged P(nonconst) to the full bound (capped at 1) = 0.875. Zero violations of the full bound. Finite evidence only; it does not establish A.

label: S0021
statement: Lemma (exact unit-weight average, lane C). Let g(x) = [x_1 + ... + x_n >= t] with all weights 1. Let F be a fixed k-subset of the variables, 0 <= k <= n, and let the other m = n-k variables be uniform bits. Let t be uniform on the 2n+1 integers -n..n. Then the average over t of P[restriction of g to F is non-constant] equals exactly k/(2n+1). Proof: let c = sum of the m free bits, so 0 <= c <= m. Let s = number of ones in F, 0 <= s <= k. The restriction is non-constant iff c < t <= c+k, i.e. c in [t-k, t-1]. For each c in [0, m], the number of integers t in [-n, n] with c+1 <= t <= c+k is exactly k, because c >= 0 and c+k <= m+k = n. Summing over t and averaging over c gives k/(2n+1). QED. Consequence: for k = pn the average tends to p/2, not p, so the uniform-t value in S-4c7647ab5f is wrong by a factor 2. The lemma is an identity, not a bound. It does not control the worst-case threshold, which at t near the centre gives an undecided probability of order k/sqrt(n), so it does not close G0001 or G0003.

structure.evidence: cm-e2a79221bb204bd9 (EXPLORATORY_COMPUTATION, exact binomial sums): n in {20,40,80,160}, p in {0.25,0.5}; computed average equals k/(2n+1) to machine precision in all 8 rows. Earlier cm-9fb9f1733aeb4dbb: at t=n/2, undecided probability 0.686-0.706 for k=sqrt(n), 1.0 for k=n/4 and n/2. The identity is an exact finite check plus the proof above; the general statement is a claim for the review, not yet a finding of the validator.
structure.gap: G0008 and G0001/G0003 stay open. The averaged quantity is k/(2n+1), which is small only because most thresholds make the gate constant; an algorithm must handle the thresholds where the gate is undecided, so a per-gate count averaged over t is the wrong target for a worst-case running time. The repair must count undecided gates under the threshold distribution the algorithm actually faces (the thresholds of the circuit), or bound the worst-case t at order k/sqrt(n) with heterogeneous weights (G0008).

label: S0023
statement: LEMMA R (window bound, arbitrary integer weights, uniform in the threshold). Let g(x)=[sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with w in Z^n, t in Z, nz=#{j: w_j != 0} >= 2, F a uniform random k-subset with 1 <= k <= nz/2, and the bits outside F uniform. Then for EVERY integer t: P[g restricted to F is nonconstant] <= (k/n) * (sum_j |w_j|) * sqrt(2/nz). PROOF. (1) Fix F. Put lo = sum_{j in F} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in F} max(w_j,0), W_F = hi - lo = sum_{j in F}|w_j|, and c = sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j. The restriction is nonconstant iff t - hi <= c < t - lo, i.e. c lies in a window of exactly W_F consecutive integers. (2) Let r = #{j not in F: w_j != 0} >= nz - k >= nz/2. Replace x_j by 1 - x_j for each j not in F with w_j < 0 (a bijection of bit strings). Then c becomes sum_J a_j y_j over r indices with a_j = |w_j| > 0. For each fixed value v, the sets J with sum_{j in J} a_j = v form an antichain (A strictly inside B forces a strictly smaller sum), so by Sperner P[c = v | F] <= C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r <= 1/sqrt(r). (3) Hence P[nonconstant | F] <= sum over the W_F window values v of P[c=v | F] <= W_F/sqrt(r) <= W_F*sqrt(2/nz). (4) P[j in F] = k/n gives E_F[W_F] = (k/n) sum_j |w_j|. Taking the expectation over F proves the claim. QED. The bound is uniform in t, so it is a worst-case-over-thresholds statement, not an average over t.

label: S0025
statement: LEMMA (exact threshold-averaged restriction count). Let w in (Z minus {0})^n, S_lo = sum_j min(w_j,0), S_hi = sum_j max(w_j,0), L = S_hi - S_lo = sum_j |w_j|. Let F be a uniform k-subset of [n], x uniform in {0,1}^n, and t uniform on the L+1 integers of [S_lo, S_hi], all independent. Let g_t(y) = [sum_j w_j y_j >= t] and let U be the event that the restriction of g_t to the free variables F, with the variables outside F fixed to x, is non-constant. Then P[U] = (k/n) * L/(L+1) exactly. PROOF: fix F and x, put c = sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j, lo = sum_{j in F} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in F} max(w_j,0), W_F = hi - lo = sum_{j in F}|w_j|. The restriction is non-constant iff cfix+lo < t <= cfix+hi, a window of exactly W_F integers. Since c+lo >= S_lo and c+hi <= S_hi, the window lies inside [S_lo, S_hi]. Hence P_t[U | F,x] = W_F/(L+1). Taking E over F with P[j in F] = k/n gives E[W_F] = (k/n) L. SCOPE: averaged over uniform t only. It does NOT bound P_x[c in window] for a fixed adversarial threshold t, so it does not close G0001 or G0002 as worst-case statements; it is an exact distributional count for the uniform threshold law. CONSEQUENCE: at k = c*sqrt(n) the averaged undecided fraction is exactly c/sqrt(n)*L/(L+1), with no anti-concentration input. The Sperner-type bound of Theorem C is needed only for fixed t.

statement: Lemma (truncated Kolmogorov-Rogozin for one THR gate, CLAIMED). Let c = sum_{j in O} w_j x_j with O = [n] minus F, x_j iid uniform bits, nonzero integer weights, and W = hi - lo the window width of the free set F. label: S0030
statement: LEMMA (gcd-refined window bound, one THR gate, per fixed free set). Let g(x) = [sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with integer weights, F a set of variables, and out = complement of F. Let W_F = sum_{j in F} |w_j| (the window width), r_F = #{j in out : w_j != 0}, and g_F = gcd{|w_j| : j in out, w_j != 0} (assume r_F >= 1). Then, for uniform independent bits on out and any fixed assignment of F, P[g restricted to F is non-constant] <= (floor(W_F/g_F) + 1)/sqrt(r_F). PROOF. (i) Non-constancy: let lo = sum_{j in F} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j in F} max(w_j,0). The F-part of the sum takes its minimum lo and maximum hi, so the restriction is non-constant iff t - hi <= c < t - lo, where c = sum_{j in out} w_j x_j. (ii) Sperner: write y_j = x_j if w_j > 0 and y_j = 1 - x_j if w_j < 0. Then c = const + sum_{j in out, w_j != 0} |w_j| y_j with positive integer coefficients a_j = |w_j|. For a fixed value v the set {S : sum_{j in S} a_j = v} is an antichain of subsets of the r_F free positions, so P[c = v] <= C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r <= 1/sqrt(r) (the central-binomial inequality holds for every r >= 1). (iii) Residue: every a_j is a multiple of g_F, so c takes values only in one residue class mod g_F. The window [t-hi, t-lo) contains W_F consecutive integers, hence at most ceil(W_F/g_F) <= floor(W_F/g_F)+1 values of the correct residue. Summing (ii) over these values gives P[nonconst | F] <= (floor(W_F/g_F)+1)/sqrt(r_F). QED. Consequence: for g_F >= 2 the window term is divided by g_F; for g_F = 1 it reduces to the earlier W_F/sqrt(r) bound up to +1.

structure.lemma: L2-window lemma (per gate, conditional on F). Let g(x)=[sum_j w_j x_j >= t] with integer weights, F subset [n] fixed, x_F fixed, x_O uniform in {0,1}^{[n]\F}. Let WF = sum_{j in F}|w_j| >= 1 and Neff(F) = sum_{j not in F, w_j != 0} min(|w_j|, WF)^2. Then P_{x_O}[g|F nonconstant] <= sqrt(2)*A*WF/sqrt(Neff(F)), where A is the absolute constant of the Kolmogorov-Rogozin inequality Q(S;L) <= A*L*(sum_j l_j^2 (1-Q(X_j;l_j)))^{-1/2} (0<l_j<=L). Proof: nonconstancy means the shift c = sum_{j not in F} w_j x_j lies in a window of WF consecutive integers, so the probability is at most Q(c;WF). Take l_j = min(|w_j|, WF) <= WF. The two-point variable X_j = w_j x_j has Q(X_j; l_j) <= 1/2 because an interval of length l_j <= |w_j| contains at most one of {0, w_j}. So sum_j l_j^2 (1-Q_j) >= Neff/2 and the inequality gives the bound. The constant is scale-invariant in w.

label: S0034
statement:
PROOF. Let F be the free set, k = |F|, m = L - k, O the fixed nonzero coordinates, S = sum_{j in O} w_j b_j with b_j iid uniform bits. (1) For fixed F, the free sum V = sum_{j in F} w_j x_j takes every integer in [minV, maxV], with maxV - minV = k (unit weights: toggle one coordinate at a time). So g is nonconstant iff minV + S < t <= maxV + S, i.e. S lies in an integer interval of exactly k integers. (2) Writing -b_j = (1-b_j) - 1 for w_j = -1 gives S = Bin(m,1/2) + const, so max_a Pr[S=a] = q(m) := C(m, floor(m/2))/2^m. Hence Pr[nonconst | F] <= min(1, k q(m)). (3) q(m) <= sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))) for m >= 2: for m = 2r, q = C(2r,r)/4^r <= 1/sqrt(pi r) (Wallis); for m = 2r+1, q(m) = q(2r)(2r+1)/(2r+2) <= q(2r). (4) If L >= 4 and k <= L/2 then m >= L/2 >= 2, m-1 >= L/4, so q(m) <= sqrt(8/(pi L)) <= 2/sqrt(L). (5) Average over k ~ Bin(L,p): E[min(1,k q(L-k)); k <= L/2] <= 2 E[k]/sqrt(L) = 2pL/sqrt(L) = 2p sqrt(L). The event k >= j, j = floor(L/2)+1 >= L/2, has probability <= C(L,j) p^j <= (eL/j)^j p^j <= (2ep)^j. Summing gives the claim. QED.
CONSEQUENCE: with p = delta/sqrt(n) (free set of size o(sqrt n) in expectation) the undecided probability of a bottom gate is <= 2 delta + o(1). For p constant the bound is trivial (>= 1). So this closes the SPARSE regime of G0002 only; the Theta(n) regime (p constant) stays OPEN. This is a sharp-constant version of the standard Erdos/Littlewood-Offord restriction bound, not a new theorem in the field; it is recorded as a proof-book lemma for the algorithmic route.

label: S0042
statement: Proof: The top gate is the OR of the bottom gate outputs. Each bottom gate's output depends only on the sign of W_j·x. The sum S = Σ_{j∈F} W_j·x aggregates these signs; a positive majority (S ≥ t_top) implies the OR is 1, otherwise 0. Computing S needs to read each of the N bottom gates once, i.e., O(N) time.

structure.lemma: For any THR o THR circuit C whose bottom gates are g_j = [W_j·x ≥ t_j] with W_j ∈ {−1,1}^{n−N} of unit magnitude and a free variable set F of size N = c√n, if the top gate is a THR with weight vector W_top = Σ_{j∈F} W_j and threshold t_top, then the top gate output equals 1 iff Σ_{j∈F} W_j·x ≥ t_top. Consequently the top gate can be decided by computing S = Σ_{j∈F} W_j·x, which requires examining at most N bottom gates and runs in time O(N) = O(√n).

statement: Lemma (window bound for random thresholds): for every rho and F as above, P_t[gate j undecided] <= sum_{i in F}|W_ji|/(2R+1), with equality up to clipping at +-R. Proof: undecided iff f_j can be 1 and can be 0 under rho, i.e. mn_j < t_j <= mx_j; the integers in (mn_j, mx_j] number mx_j - mn_j = sum_{i in F}|W_ji| (because mx - mn = sum over free i of |W_ji|); intersecting with [-R,R] and dividing by 2R+1 gives the probability.

statement: LEMMA U (adversarial threshold, unit weights). Let n >= 2, p in (0,1), pn >= 2. Random restriction: each variable is free with probability p, otherwise fixed to 1 or to 0 with probability (1-p)/2 each. Single gate with w_i = 1 for all i and threshold t = ceil(n/2). Let a = number of variables fixed to 1, f = number free. The gate is undecided iff a < t <= a+f. Then P(undecided) >= 1 - 2*exp(-2*(pn/2 - 1)^2 / n). Proof: a is Bin(n, (1-p)/2) with mean (1-p)n/2; a >= t forces a - E[a] >= pn/2 - 1. a+f is Bin(n, (1+p)/2) with mean (1+p)n/2; a+f < t <= n/2 + 1/2 forces (E - value) >= pn/2 - 1. Hoeffding on each event gives the bound. Scope: one unit-weight gate, one threshold; it refutes the adversarial-threshold form of the p-bound (max_t P(undecided) <= p) for p >> 1/sqrt(n). statement: LEMMA (random restriction, +-1 weights, ANY fixed threshold). Let n>=2, w in {-1,+1}^n, 0<p<=1/4. Random restriction: each variable is free (in F) independently with prob p; for i not in F the bit a_i is uniform in {0,1}, independent of F. For a FIXED integer t, let mn = sum_i min(0,w_i a_i) over i not in F plus sum_{i in F} min(0,w_i), and mx analogously with max; gate undecided iff mn < t <= mx. Then P_{F,a}[undecided] <= 3*sqrt(2)*p*sqrt(n) (about 4.24 p sqrt n). PROOF. Fix F, let s=|F|, k=n-s. (1) mx-mn = s, so the set of values of base = sum_{i not in F} w_i a_i that make the gate undecided is a set of s consecutive integers. (2) Substitute b_i = 1-a_i for the k' indices with w_i=-1: base = sum_{w_i=+1} a_i + sum_{w_i=-1} b_i - const, a sum of k independent uniform bits plus a constant. (3) Sperner/Erdos: max_x P(Bin(k,1/2)=x) = C(k,floor(k/2))/2^k <= 1/sqrt(k) for k>=1 (even k: C(2m,m)/4^m <= 1/sqrt(pi m) <= 1/sqrt(2m); odd k: the extra factor (2m+1)/(2m+2) <= 1 and 1/sqrt(pi m) <= 1/sqrt(2m+1) for m>=1; k=1 gives 1/2). Hence P(undecided | F) <= min(1, s/sqrt(k)) for k>=1, and <= 1 for k=0. (4) Average over F. Region A = {s <= n/2}: k >= n/2, so s/sqrt(k) <= s*sqrt(2/n); E[s] = pn gives contribution <= p*sqrt(2n). Region B = {s > n/2}: its probability is <= sum over |F|>=n/2 of p^{|F|} <= 2^n p^{n/2} = p * (2^n p^{n/2-1}) <= p * 2^n * 4^{-(n/2-1)} = 4p (using p<=1/4 and n/2-1>=0). Total <= p*sqrt(2n) + 4p = p*sqrt(n)*(sqrt(2)+4/sqrt(n)) <= 3*sqrt(2)*p*sqrt(n) for n>=2. QED. NOTE: the window bound is for an ADVERSARIAL fixed t; the uniform-t version (proof-state lemma above) is weaker and elementary. The random-a assumption is needed: the OR-gate example with all fixed bits 0 (exact, cm-33cf0317f7794fa7) has P/p ~ 0.79 sqrt(n) at p=1/n, which is consistent with the bound.

statement: CLAIMED S-R26-LEMMA-UNIFORM-THRESHOLD. Proof: fix F and a; let s = sum_{i notin F} w_i a_i, mn = s + sum_{i in F} min(0,w_i), mx = s + sum_{i in F} max(0,w_i). A linear form over the subcube attains its min and max at vertices, so over the subcube min = mn and max = mx. If mn >= t, g is constantly 1; if mx < t, g is constantly 0. Hence non-constant implies mn < t <= mx, and the integers t with mn < t <= mx number mx - mn = W_F := sum_{i in F}|w_i|. Since t is uniform on 2R+1 >= W+1 integers, P_t(nonconst | F,a) <= W_F/(W+1). Taking expectation, E[W_F] = p W, so the probability is at most p W/(W+1) < p. Conversely, if mn < t <= mx then both constant values are attained, so the events coincide. QED. Consequence: for m gates with independent uniform thresholds, E[#nonconstant gates] <= p sum_j W_j/(W_j+1) <= p m, by linearity.

The half-open interval (mn+c, mx+c] contains exactly mx-mn = W_F := sum_{i in F}|w_i| integers. Since t is uniform on 2R+1 integers and independent of F, P_t[undecided | F, a] <= W_F/(2R+1). This bound is uniform in a. Taking expectation over F, E[W_F] = sum_i |w_i| P(i in F) = p W, so P_{F,t}[undecided] <= pW/(2R+1). Since 2R+1 >= W+1 > W (R = ceil(W/2)), the bound is at most p. If W = 0 both sides are 0. QED.

label: S0072
statement: CLAIMED LEMMA (+-1 weights, single THR gate, hand proof). Let w in {-1,0,1}^n have s >= 1 nonzero entries, t in Z fixed, F a random free set (each variable free independently with prob p), and a_i uniform in {0,1} on the non-free nonzero variables. Then P(gate non-constant after restriction) <= sqrt(2s) * p. Proof: (1) Given F, with k = |F cap supp(w)|, m = s - k, the gate is non-constant iff c in [t - kp, t + kn - 1], where kp, kn are the free positive and negative counts; this window has exactly k integers, because the free sum ranges over the contiguous set [-kn, kp] in unit steps. Here c is the fixed contribution. (2) With a uniform on the m non-free nonzero variables, c + m_- ~ Bin(m, 1/2), so max_x P(c = x) = C(m, floor(m/2))/2^m <= 1/sqrt(m) for m >= 1. Hence P(nonconst | F) <= min(1, k/sqrt(s-k)). (3) For k <= s/2, k/sqrt(s-k) <= sqrt2 k/sqrt s. For k > s/2 (s >= 2), sqrt2 k/sqrt s > sqrt(s/2) >= 1, so min(1, .) <= sqrt2 k/sqrt s. This also covers k = s (m = 0). (4) E[k] = sp, so P(nonconst) <= sqrt2 sp/sqrt s = sqrt(2s) p. The case s = 1 is trivial (P <= p). Equivalence: since free-sum steps are unit, nonconstancy is exactly the window event, so the statement is about non-constancy itself.

statement: Window lemma for a fixed threshold, with a uniform completion a on [n] minus F. Let K = the non-free indices with w_i nonzero, k = |K|, and W_F = sum over F of |w_i|. For each integer t, P_a(gate t undecided | F) <= (W_F+1) * binom(k, floor(k/2)) / 2^k <= (W_F+1)/sqrt(k). The point mass bound uses Erdos (1945): if |w_i| >= 1 for all i in K, an interval of length 2 contains at most binom(k, floor(k/2)) of the 2^k subset sums. The union bound over the W_F+1 integers of the undecided window gives the rest. Result: the fixed-threshold step has the same form as G0008 Lemma B, and it is not a new closure.

label: S0075
statement: CLAIMED LEMMA (bounded integer weights, single THR gate; generalises the +-1 lemma S0072 with B = 1). Setting: w in Z^n with s nonzero entries, |w_i| <= B for all i, t in Z fixed. F = free set, each variable free independently with prob p; each non-free nonzero variable gets a_i uniform in {0,1}. Claim: P(gate non-constant after restriction) <= B sqrt(2s) p for s >= 1. Proof. (1) Let k = |F cap supp(w)|, m = s - k, c = sum over non-free i of w_i a_i, X = sum over free i of w_i x_i. Non-constancy is min(c+X) < t <= max(c+X), i.e. c lies in a set of exactly max X - min X = W_F := sum_{i in F}|w_i| consecutive integers. (2) Erdos/Sperner: flip a_i to 1 - a_i where w_i < 0 (uniformity preserved), so c = (sum |w_i| a'_i) - const with |w_i| >= 1. For any half-open interval [y, y+1), the subset sums lying in it form an antichain (if A is a proper subset of B, the sums differ by >= 1), so there are at most C(m, floor(m/2)) of them. Hence max_x P(c = x) <= C(m, floor(m/2))/2^m <= 1/sqrt(m) for m >= 1. (3) So P(nonconst | F) <= min(1, W_F/sqrt(m)). (4) W_F <= B k. If k <= s/2 then m >= s/2 and B k/sqrt(m) <= sqrt2 B k/sqrt(s). If k > s/2 and s >= 2 then sqrt2 B k/sqrt(s) > B sqrt(s/2) >= 1, so the min is at most sqrt2 B k/sqrt(s). If s = 1, P(nonconst) <= P(k=1) = p <= sqrt2 B p. (5) E[k] = s p, so P(nonconst) <= sqrt2 B s p/sqrt(s) = B sqrt(2s) p. Corollary: with p = q/n and s <= n, the bound is B sqrt2 q/sqrt(n), the k/sqrt(n) shape of G0001 (per gate, in expectation, bounded weights only). Scope: single gate, bounded integer weights, fixed t, uniform fixed bits, i.i.d. free set. Does NOT close G0001, G0002, G0004 or G0009: no w.h.p. statement over m = n^1.5 gates, no unbounded weights, no top gate, no decision procedure, no running time. Barrier labels (provisional): not relativizing-relevant; a statement about linear forms under random restriction; not natural in the Razborov-Rudich sense as stated; localizing not checked.

label: S0076
statement: CLAIMED S-R26-LEMMA-UNIT-FIXED-THRESHOLD. Proof: fix F, k = |F|, m = n - k. Put s = sum_{i notin F} w_i a_i and mn = s + sum_{i in F} min(0,w_i), mx = s + sum_{i in F} max(0,w_i). The subcube minimum and maximum of w.x are mn and mx, so non-constancy is equivalent to mn < t <= mx, i.e. s lies in a set I_F of exactly mx - mn = k integers (all |w_i| = 1). (1) Distribution of s given F: s = sum_{w_i=+1} a_i + sum_{w_i=-1} (1-a_i) - N_- where N_- = #{i notin F: w_i=-1}; the terms a_i and 1-a_i are i.i.d. uniform bits, so s is a fixed integer shift of Bin(m,1/2). Hence each point probability is at most C(m,floor(m/2))/2^m <= sqrt(2/(pi m)) (standard central binomial bound, valid for all m >= 1). Therefore P_a(nonconst | F) <= min(1, k sqrt(2/(pi m))). (2) Case k <= n/2: then m >= n/2 >= 1/2, so sqrt(2/(pi m)) <= 2/sqrt(pi n) < sqrt(2/n), giving P_a(nonconst|F) <= k sqrt(2/n). Taking expectation, E[k 1(k<=n/2)] <= E[k] = pn, so this part contributes at most p sqrt(2n). (3) Case k > n/2: bound the conditional probability by 1; by Markov, P(k >= n/2) <= E[k]/(n/2) = 2p. Adding: P <= p sqrt(2n) + 2p. QED. Consequence: for m' gates with the same (F,a) law, E[#nonconstant gates] <= m' p(sqrt(2n)+2), by linearity, with no independence needed.

statement: LEMMA (session R1046, CLAIMED, not self-reviewed). Let a_1..a_k be nonzero integers, x_i iid uniform {0,1}, S = sum a_i x_i. Then for every integer a, P(S=a) <= C(k,floor(k/2))/2^k. Proof: for a_i<0 put y_i=1-x_i, so S = c + sum |a_i| y_i with all coefficients >= 1. If Y is a strict subset of Y' then sum_{Y'} >= sum_Y + 1, so the subsets with a fixed sum form an antichain; Sperner bounds it by C(k,floor(k/2)). Corollary: for a window I of W integers and fixed-part sum S over the k nonzero fixed weights, P(S in I) <= min(1, W*C(k,floor(k/2))/2^k). Applied to a gate with free set F: the gate is undecided iff S lies in a window of W = sum_F |w_j| integers, so P(undecided) <= min(1, sum_F|w_j| * C(k,floor(k/2))/2^k), k = #fixed nonzero weights. This replaces S0004 (refuted twice).

statement: PROOF. (i) flo >= lo, since const >= sum_{j notin F} min(W_j,0), so flo >= sum_j min(W_j,0) = lo. Likewise fhi <= hi. Hence (flo,fhi] lies inside [lo,hi] and contains exactly fhi - flo = W_F integers. (ii) t uniform on S+1 integers gives P = W_F/(S+1). (iii) Each j lies in a uniform k-subset F with probability k/n, so E_F[W_F] = (k/n) S, giving E_F P = (k/n) S/(S+1). The identity sum_F W_F = C(n-1,k-1) S is checked exactly in cm-26d396f198844b29 (276 sum checks, 0 mismatches), and the pointwise identity in 87576 checks, 0 mismatches. With k = c sqrt(n) this gives E_F P <= c/sqrt(n).

structure.lemma: Uniform-threshold restriction identity. Let W in Z^{1 x n} with S_+ = sum_j max(W_j,0), S_- = sum_j min(W_j,0), S = S_+ - S_- = sum_j |W_j|, lo = S_-, hi = S_+. Let t be uniform on the S+1 integers {lo,...,hi}. Fix x in {0,1}^n and a free set F. Let const = sum_{j not in F} W_j x_j, flo = const + sum_{j in F} min(W_j,0), fhi = const + sum_{j in F} max(W_j,0). The gate is undecided under the restriction iff flo < t <= fhi. Then P_t[undecided] = W_F/(S+1) exactly, where W_F = sum_{j in F}|W_j|. Averaging over a uniformly random free set F of size k: E_F[P_t[undecided]] = (k/n) S/(S+1) <= k/n.
structure.proved_step: PROOF. (i) flo >= lo, since const >= sum_{j notin F} min(W_j,0), so flo >= sum_j min(W_j,0) = lo. Likewise fhi <= hi. Hence (flo,fhi] lies inside [lo,hi] and contains exactly fhi - flo = W_F integers. (ii) t uniform on S+1 integers gives P = W_F/(S+1). (iii) Each j lies in a uniform k-subset F with probability k/n, so E_F[W_F] = (k/n) S, giving E_F P = (k/n) S/(S+1). The identity sum_F W_F = C(n-1,k-1) S is checked exactly in cm-26d396f198844b29 (276 sum checks, 0 mismatches), and the pointwise identity in 87576 checks, 0 mismatches. With k = c sqrt(n) this gives E_F P <= c/sqrt(n).

statement: Lemma U (unit-weight fixed-threshold restriction). Let n>=2, 1<=k<=n-1, N=n-k, and let t in Z be ARBITRARY (worst case over thresholds). Let g(x)=[x_1+...+x_n >= t] on {0,1}^n. Fix a set F of k free coordinates and draw the N other coordinates i.i.d. uniform; set c = sum of the fixed coordinates, so c ~ Bin(N,1/2). Then P_c[g restricted to F is non-constant] <= k/sqrt(N). PROOF. The restricted function is c + (sum of the k free bits), which takes values in [c, c+k]. It is constant 1 iff c >= t and constant 0 iff c+k < t, so it is non-constant iff t-k <= c <= t-1, a window of at most k integers. Hence P <= sum over the window of P(Bin(N,1/2)=c) <= k * M_N, where M_N = max_j C(N,j)/2^N. Claim: M_N <= 1/sqrt(N) for all N>=1. Let a_m = C(2m,m)/4^m. (i) For N=2m, M_N = a_m. Put f(m)=a_m^2(3m+1), f(0)=1. Since a_{m+1}/a_m=(2m+1)/(2m+2), f(m+1)/f(m) <= 1 iff (2m+1)^2(3m+4) <= (2m+2)^2(3m+1); the difference RHS-LHS equals m >= 0. So a_m <= 1/sqrt(3m+1) <= 1/sqrt(2m) = 1/sqrt(N). (ii) For N=2m+1, M_N = C(2m+1,m)/2^{2m+1} = a_{m+1} (because C(2m+2,m+1)=2 C(2m+1,m)), so M_N <= 1/sqrt(3m+4) <= 1/sqrt(2m+1) = 1/sqrt(N). Combining, P <= k/sqrt(N). QED. COROLLARY: since N >= n/2 when k <= n/2, the bound is <= sqrt(2) k/sqrt(n); it shrinks with n only when k = o(sqrt n). SCOPE: unit weights only; uniform random fixed coordinates; the bound holds for every threshold t. It does NOT handle general integer weights (the Erdos-Moser/Halasz obstacle of G0002/G0004), the top gate, or running time. It is a special case of the open restriction obligation, not a closure of it.

statement:
statement: For n>=1, 0<=k<n, a fixed k-element set F, and g_t(x)=[sum_{j=1}^n x_j>=t] on {0,1}^n, choose the n-k coordinates outside F independently and uniformly. For every integer t, the probability that the restriction of g_t to F is nonconstant is at most min(1, k*sqrt(2/(n-k+1))).
proof: Put r=n-k and let C be the sum of the random outside coordinates. Given C=c, the restriction is nonconstant exactly when c<t<=c+k. Thus C must lie in a set of at most k integer values. Since C~Binomial(r,1/2), every atom is at most 2^{-r} binom(r,floor(r/2)) <= sqrt(2/(r+1)); summing over at most k values gives the second bound. Probability is also at most 1. For k=0 the interval is empty, so the probability is zero, as the formula states.

label: S0021
statement: LEMMA W (exact, general n, 0<k<n). PM on K_{n,n}, row-major order, top block a = rows 1..k, bottom block b = rows k+1..n. Let F(a) = {T subset of [n], |T|=k : a admits a perfect matching of rows 1..k onto T}, g_a(b) = PM(a,b). Then F(a)=F(a') iff g_a=g_a' as functions of b. Hence the level-kn width equals the number of distinct F(a). PROOF. (1) A perfect matching of K_{n,n} splits into a matching of rows 1..k onto some T with |T|=k and a matching of rows k+1..n onto [n]\T; so g_a(b)=1 iff some T in F(a) has b matchable onto [n]\T. (2) For T, let b_T be the bottom graph whose only edges form one perfect matching of rows k+1..n onto [n]\T. Its rows can only be matched onto exactly [n]\T, so by (1) g_a(b_T)=1 iff T in F(a); hence F(a) is determined by g_a. (3) By (1), g_a(b)=1 iff some T in F(a) has b matchable onto [n]\T, a condition on the pair (F(a), b); hence g_a is determined by F(a). Together (2) and (3) give the claim. QED.

label: S0024
statement:
statement: For n>=2 and 1<=k<=n-1, let X={(i,j): i<k} and Y={(i,j): i>=k} be the edge sets of K_{n,n}. Let M[a,b]=1 iff a (subset of X) union b (subset of Y) is a perfect matching of K_{n,n}. Then rank_F(M)=C(n,k) over every field F. Closes: none. This is a control-failure lemma and does not close G0001.
derivation: (1) In a union a+b that is a perfect matching, each left vertex i<k has degree 1 in a, since b has no edges at i<k, and the right endpoints of a are distinct. So a is valid iff a is an injection f:[k]->[n]; let S(a) be its image, |S|=k. (2) Symmetrically, b is valid iff it is an injection g:{k..n-1}->[n], with image T(b) of size n-k. (3) a+b is a perfect matching iff valid(a), valid(b) and T(b)=[n]\S(a). (4) Row a depends only on S(a). Each k-set S has a nonempty row class R_S (valid a with S(a)=S), and each (n-k)-set T has a nonempty column class C_T (valid b with T(b)=T). The block R_S x C_T is all-ones if T=[n]\S and zero otherwise; invalid rows and columns are zero. (5) Distinct S give distinct T=[n]\S, so the nonzero blocks have disjoint row and column supports. M is therefore a sum of C(n,k) rank-1 blocks with disjoint supports, plus zero rows and columns, so rank_F(M)=C(n,k) over every field. (6) For k=n/2, rank >= 2^n/(n+1). Perfect matching is in P, so this rank measure fails the perfect-matching control.
evidence: Hand proof above, re-checked step by step. Matches cm-40cf2c6f2271450d (GF(1000003), n<=4: 2,3,3,4,6,4) and cm-4a4d1d1af70b4712 (GF(2), n<=6, ALL_MATCH True, including n=5 k=2 -> 10 and n=6 k=3 -> 20). Not a proof of an oracle-free lower bound.

label: S0026
statement:
statement_start: For every deterministic one-pass streaming machine with S state bits and a one-bit input alphabet, each transition stage can be implemented by a Boolean circuit of size O(S 2^S).
statement: Lemma (truth-table transition simulation). Let M be a deterministic one-pass machine whose configuration at each read boundary is encoded by S bits, whose next configuration after reading one input bit is a total function δ:{0,1}^S×{0,1}->{0,1}^S, and whose input length is L. There is a layered Boolean circuit with L transition layers, O(S 2^S) gates per layer, and O(S) wires carrying state between adjacent layers, whose output equals M's final configuration (and hence any Boolean output function of that configuration, if that final decoder is appended). Proof: for each output coordinate j and each pair (u,b) in {0,1}^S×{0,1} with δ(u,b)_j=1, form the minterm that is 1 exactly when the S state wires equal u and the input wire equals b. OR these minterms to obtain output coordinate j. A minterm uses O(S) literals and can be implemented with O(S) fan-in-2 gates; OR of at most 2^(S+1) minterms uses O(2^S) fan-in-2 gates per output coordinate. Summing over S coordinates gives O(S 2^S) gates per layer. Cascade the layers, feeding the initial configuration constants to the first layer and each layer's state outputs into the next; induction on layer index shows the wires equal M's configuration after each read. Appending the decoder preserves the final output. The construction is exact for all input strings of length L. This restricted lemma only gives an upper simulation bound and does not imply a lower bound for Search-MCSP or close G0001.

label: S0027
statement:
statement: Let L be the YES language of an exact deterministic one-pass Search-MCSP machine on inputs of fixed length N. At a cut after t bits, define the suffix residual of prefix u in {0,1}^t by L_u={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: uz in L}, and let R_t be the number of distinct such residuals. If the machine has S state bits and its final output determines membership in L, then 2^S >= R_t, hence S >= ceil(log_2 R_t).
proof: Suppose prefixes u and v reach the same state at the cut. Determinism implies that for every common suffix z, the continuation from that state produces the same final state and output on uz and vz. Exactness and the assumed membership decoder imply uz is in L iff vz is in L for every z. Therefore L_u=L_v. Distinct residuals must reach distinct machine states, so there are at least R_t states. An S-bit state has at most 2^S possibilities, giving 2^S >= R_t and the logarithmic bound.
scope: Fixed-length inputs; deterministic one-pass computation; the entire configuration relevant to future computation is included in the S-bit state; final output determines YES membership. Applies to Search-MCSP when its exact search output is decoded for validity/membership under the specified total-task convention.

label: S0028
statement:
statement: Let F be any subset of {0,1}^N and fix a cut after t bits. For each prefix u in {0,1}^t, define its suffix residual F_u={z in {0,1}^{N-t}: uz in F}. If R_t is the number of distinct residuals, then R_t <= min(2^t, 2^(N-t), |F|+1).
proof: There are at most 2^t prefixes and at most 2^(N-t) possible residual subsets of suffixes, giving the first two bounds. For the third, each distinct nonempty residual contains at least one suffix z. Choose one such z for each distinct nonempty residual, and choose one prefix u realizing that residual. The resulting pairs (u,z) are distinct because distinct residuals cannot be realized by the same prefix, and each pair satisfies uz in F. Thus the number of distinct nonempty residuals is at most |F|. There is at most one empty residual, so R_t <= |F|+1.
scope: Finite fixed-length Boolean language and any fixed prefix cut. For Search-MCSP the lemma applies to F equal to the YES truth tables, but supplies only an upper bound on residual width; it does not prove G0001 or an update-time lower bound.

statement:
statement: Let F be a subset of {0,1}^N, fix a cut after t bits, and put p=2^t, q=2^(N-t), k=|F|. For each prefix u define F_u={z:uz in F}, and let R_t be the number of distinct F_u. Then R_t <= min(p,q,k+1,pq-k+1).
proof: There are p rows, so R_t<=p. Each row is a subset of a q-element suffix set, so R_t<=q. For every distinct nonempty row pattern choose one matrix entry equal to 1 in a row realizing that pattern. Different patterns have different realizing rows, so the chosen entries are distinct; hence there are at most k distinct nonempty patterns, plus at most one empty pattern. Thus R_t<=k+1. For every distinct pattern other than the full pattern, choose a 0-entry in a row realizing it. Distinct patterns have distinct realizing rows, hence these chosen entries are distinct; there are pq-k zero entries. Thus there are at most pq-k non-full patterns, plus at most one full pattern, so R_t<=pq-k+1. Combining the four bounds proves the claim.
scope: All finite fixed-length Boolean languages and every fixed prefix cut. For Search-MCSP this is only a residual-width upper bound; it proves no residual lower bound and no update-time lower bound.

label: S0036
statement:
statement: For every integer n >= 1, the row-major perfect-matching Boolean function on K_{n,n} has exactly 2^n distinct residual functions after the first n edge variables (the edges incident to the first row).
proof: A prefix of the first n variables specifies a subset U of columns adjacent to the first row. For any suffix assignment b to the remaining edges, the full graph has a perfect matching exactly when some j in U can be reserved for the first row and the suffix rows have a matching onto [n]\\{j}. Thus the residual depends only on U, so there are at most 2^n residuals. To distinguish any distinct U,V, choose j in their symmetric difference, and let b contain exactly a bijection from the remaining n-1 rows onto [n]\\{j}. Then the only possible perfect matching uses column j for the first row. The residual accepts precisely when j belongs to the prefix subset, so the residuals for U and V differ. Every subset U is realizable by a prefix assignment. Hence there are exactly 2^n distinct residual functions.

For any suffix assignment b to the remaining edges, the full graph has a perfect matching exactly when some j in U can be reserved for the first row and the suffix rows have a matching onto [n]\\{j}. Thus the residual depends only on U, so there are at most 2^n residuals. To distinguish any distinct U,V, choose j in their symmetric difference, and let b contain exactly a bijection from the remaining n-1 rows onto [n]\\{j}. Then the only possible perfect matching uses column j for the first row. The residual accepts precisely when j belongs to the prefix subset, so the residuals for U and V differ. Every subset U is realizable by a prefix assignment. Hence there are exactly 2^n distinct residual functions.

label: S0037
statement: statement_start: LEMMA (residual distinguishability forces streaming states). Let L be a language over strings split into prefixes and suffixes, and fix a prefix length l.

structure.lemma: LEMMA (residual distinguishability forces streaming states). Let L be a language over strings split into prefixes and suffixes, and fix a prefix length l. Define u ~ v iff for every suffix z, uz is in L exactly when vz is in L. Any deterministic one-pass machine that reads the prefix, stores a state, and thereafter processes the suffix exactly has at least as many distinct states after length-l prefixes as there are ~-classes. Proof: if u and v reach the same state, determinism implies that processing any common suffix z from that state yields the same acceptance outcome. Exactness therefore gives uz in L iff vz in L for every z, hence u ~ v. Thus each ~-class requires a distinct machine state. If the machine uses at most B bits of memory, it has at most 2^B states, so B >= ceil(log2 R_l), where R_l is the number of residual classes at the cut. Scope: deterministic exact one-pass recognition, fixed cut and encoding; this does not establish a large R_l for Search-MCSP or bound update time, and it does not close G0001.

statement: statement: CONSTRUCTIVE RESIDUAL AUTOMATON LEMMA. Let L be a language over a finite alphabet Σ. For each prefix u, define its residual R_u={z∈Σ*: uz∈L}. Let ℛ={R_u:u∈Σ*}. If ℛ is finite, the machine with state set ℛ, initial state R_ε, transition δ(R_u,a)=R_{ua}, and accepting states {R_u: ε∈R_u} recognizes L and is minimal among deterministic exact automata. The transition is well-defined: R_u=R_v implies for every z, uaz∈L iff vaz∈L, hence R_{ua}=R_{va}. Recognition follows by induction on the consumed input: after prefix u the state is R_u, which accepts exactly when u∈L. For minimality, prefixes with distinct residuals are distinguished by some suffix z on which membership differs; any exact deterministic machine must therefore place them in distinct states. Consequently the minimum state count is |ℛ|, and any encoding needs at least ceil(log2 |ℛ|) bits. This gives an exact state lower bound but no transition-circuit/update-time lower bound.

statement:
statement_start: In a Boolean transition circuit with T fan-in-two gates, if every output is driven by a gate, at most 2T distinct input variables can feed those gates.
evidence: Each of the T gates has at most two input slots, so the union of variables feeding gates has size at most 2T. The output restriction matters: free output wires can copy arbitrarily many inputs without gates. This restricted lemma gives no bound for the unrestricted Search-MCSP machine, so it does not close G0001.

statement_start: For every Boolean circuit with n primary input variables and T gates, regardless of fan-out and with arbitrary output wires, the circuit has at most n+T distinct output Boolean functions.

label: S0014
statement: Formalization of S-54f648a904 (inclusion-exclusion for #F). Let F = C_1 and ... and C_m be a CNF over x_1..x_n. For S subset of [m] put L(S) = union of C_i over i in S, and N(S) = #{a in {0,1}^n : every literal of L(S) is false under a}. Then #F = sum over S of (-1)^|S| N(S). Moreover N(S) = 2^(n - |V(S)|) if L(S) contains no complementary pair {x, not-x}, and N(S) = 0 otherwise, where V(S) is the set of variables occurring in L(S). Proof: with f_i(a) = 1 iff C_i is falsified by a, [a satisfies F] = product over i of (1 - f_i(a)). Expanding gives sum over S of (-1)^|S| times product over i in S of f_i(a), and that product is 1 exactly when all literals of L(S) are false under a. Summing over a gives the identity. A consistent L(S) forces the values of V(S) and leaves n - |V(S)| variables free; an inconsistent L(S) has no satisfying-falsifying assignment.

structure.lemma: Reuse-elimination (naive): for an acyclic De Morgan circuit C with S non-input gates and r gates of fan-out >= 2, f_C has a De Morgan formula with at most 2^r * 2S leaves. Proof: order the reused gates topologically; for b in {0,1}^r let term_b = AND_j [g_j(x,b)=b_j] AND [out(x,b)=1], where reused gates are read as constants b. Least-index argument: if b != y(x) (true values), the least j with b_j != y_j(x) fails its check, since g_j reads only inputs with index < j, which agree with y. So exactly one term is consistent and OR_b term_b = f_C. Each term is a fan-out-1 forest with <= 2S leaves (x-literals), so the total is <= 2^r * 2S.

statement:
LEMMA (De Morgan leaf size, general). Setting: formulas are trees with fan-in-2 gates from {AND, OR} and leaves labelled by literals x_i or NOT x_i; L(f) = minimum number of leaves over formulas computing f. Parity_d(x) = x_1 XOR ... XOR x_d.
(A) L(NOT f) = L(f). Proof: for a formula F, let F^d be obtained by swapping AND and OR at every gate and negating every leaf literal. By induction on F, F^d computes NOT of F's function (De Morgan), and F^d has the same number of leaves. Hence L(NOT f) <= L(f), and the reverse follows by applying the same argument to NOT f.
(B) L(f XOR g) <= 2(L(f) + L(g)). Proof: take formulas F, G with leaves L(f), L(g). By (A), F^d and G^d compute NOT f and NOT g with the same leaf counts. The formula H = (F AND G^d) OR (F^d AND G) computes (f AND NOT g) OR (NOT f AND g) = f XOR g and has 2L(f) + 2L(g) leaves (F, F^d, G, G^d are each a copy of a subtree).
(C) For every j >= 0, L(parity_{2^j}) <= 4^j. Proof by induction. j = 0: parity_1 = x_1, one leaf, 1 = 4^0. Step: parity_{2^{j+1}}(x) = parity_{2^j}(x_left) XOR parity_{2^j}(x_right) on disjoint variable sets. By (B), L <= 2(4^j + 4^j) = 4^{j+1}. Since parity_{2^j} is computed by a formula on 2^j variables with 4^j = (2^j)^2 leaves, this gives the exact pattern d^2 at d = 2^j.
NOTE (not a claim): the same recursion for general d gives L(parity_6) <= 2(L(3)+L(3)) = 40 > 36 = 6^2 with L(3)=10, so the bound d^2 is NOT derived for general d by this construction; only the powers of two are proved.
WHAT THIS DOES NOT PROVE: nothing about DAGs with reuse, constant-width state, or the S0001 conversion lemma (a reused DAG of size S with shared state -> formula of size poly(S)). S0001 stays REFUTED-as-stated / OPEN.

structure.closes: None of S0001. It closes the session's own open checkpoint: an exact general upper bound L(parity_{2^j}) <= 4^j, valid for all j, not only j <= 3.

statement:
statement: For every field F, n >= 0, and function f:{0,1}^n -> F, M_f(x)=sum_{a in {0,1}^n} f(a) product_{i:a_i=1} x_i product_{i:a_i=0}(1-x_i) is multilinear, agrees with f on the Boolean cube, and is zero as a formal polynomial iff f is identically zero. Its displayed representation has at most 2^n terms and O(n*2^n) literal factors.
proof: At Boolean input b only the summand a=b survives, so M_f(b)=f(b); multilinearity is immediate. If a multilinear polynomial P vanishes on the cube, induct on n. Write P=A+x_n B with A,B multilinear. The restrictions x_n=0 and x_n=1 vanish on the smaller cube, so induction gives A=0 and A+B=0, hence B=0. Thus P=0. Applying this to M_f proves the equivalence. The displayed sum has 2^n terms of n factors each.

statement: statement: Let R=Z[x_1,...,x_n]/(x_i^2-x_i:1<=i<=n). For every polynomial P in Z[x_1,...,x_n], its class in R is zero iff P(a)=0 for every a in {0,1}^n. Consequently, for any CNF φ, the class of its literal-product satisfaction indicator P_φ=∏_j(1-∏_{literal occurrences ℓ in C_j}(1-ℓ)), where ℓ=x_i for a positive literal and ℓ=1-x_i for a negative literal, is zero in R iff φ is unsatisfiable. Proof: Modulo x_i^2=x_i, reduce each monomial by replacing every positive exponent of x_i by 1; this gives a multilinear representative with the same Boolean evaluations. A multilinear polynomial vanishing on the Boolean cube is the zero polynomial, by induction on n: write it A+x_nB; restrictions at x_n=0 and x_n=1 imply A=0 and A+B=0 on the smaller cube, so induction gives A=B=0. Thus P's class is zero exactly when all evaluations vanish. On Boolean inputs P_φ is 1 precisely when every clause has a true literal, hence it vanishes on the cube iff φ has no satisfying assignment.

label: S0003
statement: statement: For every n>=0 and every multilinear polynomial Q(x)=sum_{S subseteq [n]} c_S product_{i in S} x_i over the integers, the Boolean-cube sum is sum_{a in {0,1}^n} Q(a)=sum_{S subseteq[n]} c_S 2^{n-|S|}. Consequently, if Q is the unique multilinear representative modulo (x_i^2-x_i) of a CNF satisfaction indicator, this weighted coefficient sum equals #SAT of that CNF. Proof: finite-sum interchange gives sum_a sum_S c_S product_{i in S}a_i = sum_S c_S sum_a product_{i in S}a_i. For fixed S, the monomial equals 1 iff all coordinates in S are 1; the remaining n-|S| coordinates are free, so exactly 2^{n-|S|} assignments contribute 1. The n=0 case uses S=empty and has one assignment. This is an identity over integers, not modulo a finite field, and asserts no efficient coefficient extraction from an arithmetic-circuit description.

statement:
statement: Conditional overlap-to-excess lemma. Let k composable systems have excesses e_1,...,e_k and successive overlap subspaces U_1,...,U_{k-1}, with the T52 composition law applying at every composition. If e_i >= a for all i and sum_i dim(U_i) <= b k, then total excess e^* >= k(a-2b). Thus a > 2b implies linear excess in k.
proof: Induct on k using the composition law at each step. Each composition adds the next component excess and subtracts twice the dimension of that step's overlap, so e^* = sum_i e_i - 2 sum_i dim(U_i). The assumptions give sum_i e_i >= ka and 2 sum_i dim(U_i) <= 2bk. Hence e^* >= ka-2bk = k(a-2b), which is linear and positive when a>2b.

structure.gap: Conditional criterion only. COMPRESS-D still requires deriving a positive aggregate margin from f(J)=2r(J)-|J|>=0 and uniqueness of S(x) for actual circuit-evaluation systems. The retrieved question and T52 summary provide no relation establishing that margin; no circuit-specific bound is claimed.

The assumptions give sum_i e_i >= ka and 2 sum_i dim(U_i) <= 2bk. Hence e^* >= ka-2bk = k(a-2b), which is linear and positive when a>2b.
