statement: Composition-tree excess identity and sufficient margin. Let T be any finite rooted binary tree whose leaves are component systems with excesses e_i, and whose internal nodes v compose their two children under the exact law e(v)=e(v_L)+e(v_R)-2d_v, where d_v=dim(U_v) is the overlap dimension at v. Then e(root)=sum_i e_i-2 sum_{v internal} d_v. In particular, for any parameter s>0, if sum_i e_i>=a s and sum_{v internal}d_v<=b s, then e(root)>=(a-2b)s; hence a>2b gives linear excess in s.
proof: Induct on the number of leaves. A one-leaf tree has root excess e_1 and an empty internal-node sum, so the identity holds. For a tree with at least two leaves, apply the induction hypothesis to the two child subtrees: their root excesses equal the sums of their respective leaf excesses minus twice their respective internal overlap sums. The root composition law adds those two expressions and subtracts 2d_root. The leaf sets and internal nodes of the two subtrees, together with the root, partition the leaves and internal nodes of T, giving the stated identity. Under the two inequalities, substitute into the identity to obtain e(root)>=as-2bs=(a-2b)s. If a>2b this lower bound is positive and proportional to s.

structure.gap: This exact identity applies to any composition tree on which the stipulated local law holds, but it does not derive either aggregate hypothesis from f(J)=2r(J)-|J|>=0 or uniqueness of S(x). The unresolved COMPRESS-D task is to connect those conditions for actual circuit-evaluation systems to a leaf-surplus bound exceeding twice the total overlap, or to enrich the object and prove a corresponding bound.

statement:
statement: Overlap-budget lemma for a composition tree. Let T be a finite rooted binary tree with q leaves and internal overlap dimensions d_v >= 0. Suppose every internal node obeys e(v)=e(v_L)+e(v_R)-2d_v, every leaf has excess e_i >= a, and every internal overlap satisfies d_v <= delta. Then e(root) >= qa - 2delta(q-1). In particular, if a > 2delta, then e(root) >= q(a-2delta)+2delta.
proof: Inductively expanding the local composition law gives e(root)=sum_i e_i-2sum_v d_v. A finite full binary tree with q leaves has q-1 internal nodes: this follows by induction, since joining subtrees with q_L and q_R leaves gives 1+(q_L-1)+(q_R-1)=q-1 internal nodes. Therefore sum_i e_i >= qa and sum_v d_v <= delta(q-1), so e(root) >= qa-2delta(q-1) = q(a-2delta)+2delta.

statement: PROOF. (i) The projection K_G -> (+)_v T_3 onto vertex blocks is an isomorphism (edge coordinates are determined by endpoints), so dim K_G = 2n. The vectors (1,2,0) and (0,1,2) lie in T_3 (sums 3 = 0) and are linearly independent over GF(3), so their vertex-block images for all v form a basis of (+)_v T_3. Hence B is a basis of K_G. (ii) Vertices of H_B are the 2n vectors. Same-vertex pair x_v, x'_v: they share vertex-block coordinates 1 and 2 (supports {0,1} and {1,2}), so they are adjacent. Pair with u != v: vertex blocks are disjoint, so a shared coordinate must be an edge coordinate e; the coordinate of x_v on e is nonzero only if e is incident to v. A shared edge e must therefore be incident to both u and v, i.e. e=(u,v) in E. For such an edge, supports of x_u and x_v on e are {0,1} and {1,2}-type sets that overlap (both contain coordinate 1 when the pair uses (1,2,0) and (0,1,2); for the other combinations the supports {0,1},{0,1} and {1,2},{1,2} also overlap), so all four pairs between blobs of adjacent u,v are adjacent. Non-adjacent u,v have no shared coordinate. So H_B = G[K_2]. (iii) Let (T,{X_i}) be a tree decomposition of G of width k. Replace each bag X_i by X_i x {a,b} (2 copies). Bag size is at most 2(k+1), so width <= 2k+1. Coverage: a vertex pair (v,a),(v,b) lies in the bag of any bag containing v. An edge (u,a)-(w,b) of G[K_2] comes from edge uw in G, which lies in some X_i, so both appear in X_i x {a,b}. Connectivity of the occurrence sets is inherited from T. Hence tw(G[K_2]) <= 2k+1. The reverse inequality (min over ALL bases >= 2tw(G)+1) is NOT proved here; it is the owner's lower bound and is not re-verified in this step. Remark: this explains the earlier hill-climb stall for P3 and C4: the explicit B reaches tw 3 (P3) and tw 5 (C4), which the search had not found.

label: S0001
statement: PROOF. Each cross wire carries one bit from its source side to its target side. Evaluate C in topological order: a gate on side S_A needs only values from S_A or from cross wires; the value of a cross wire is a function of its source side's inputs and bits already received, so it is sent once, by its source party, as one bit. Each cross wire contributes at most one bit, so the transcript has at most kappa bits. Once all cross wires are transmitted, both parties know the output bit for their input pair; the party holding the output gate sends one more bit, so the total is at most kappa+1 bits. A deterministic protocol with c bits has at most 2^c leaves; each leaf is a combinatorial rectangle on which the output is constant, so M is a sum of at most 2^c rank-one 0/1 matrices, rank_R(M) <= 2^c. Hence log2 rank <= kappa+1. The argument uses only the wire count, not any gate structure, and it holds for any partition of gates. Remark: the lab check uses the 0-based side assignment and counts each gate input once, matching the wire count above.

Need an account that bounds the cumulative cost, or a counterexample showing the aggregate exceeds polylog(N)*|C|.
structure.lemma: Cut lemma. Let C be a Boolean circuit (fan-in <= 2, gates AND/OR/XOR/NOT) on inputs x_1..x_n, and let (A,B) be a partition of the input variables. Let the gates be split into sides S_A and S_B (each gate on the side it is assigned), and let kappa be the number of wires (gate-input edges, including input-variable edges) whose endpoints lie on different sides. Let M be the 2^|A| x 2^|B| communication matrix of f = C, with rows indexed by a in {0,1}^A and columns by b in {0,1}^B. Then log2 rank_R(M) <= kappa + 1.

label: S0008
statement: L-K1-PREFIX (closes G0005(a) for the prefix-cut family). Setting: f:{0,1}^N->{0,1} computed by a fan-in<=2 circuit C with gates G, inputs x_1..x_N in a fixed order. Define P(x_j)=j and P(g)=max of P over the inputs of gate g (so P(u)<=P(g) along every wire u->g, and 1<=P(v)<=N). Let W = number of wires (gate-input edges), Lambda(C)=sum over wires u->g of (P(g)-P(u)). For i in [1,N-1], M_i = communication matrix of f for A={x_1..x_i}, B=rest. CLAIM: (1) sum_{i=1}^{N-1} log2 rank_R(M_i) <= (N-1) + Lambda(C); (2) Lambda(C) <= W(N-1) <= 2|G|(N-1); hence for every input order, |G| >= (sum_i log2 rank_R(M_i) - (N-1)) / (2(N-1)). PROOF. Let L_i={v: P(v)<=i}. Input x_j is in L_i iff j<=i, so L_i restricted to inputs is exactly A. If g in L_i and u->g is a wire, P(u)<=P(g)<=i so u in L_i: no wire goes from the right side to the left side. Hence the cross wires for cut i are exactly the wires with P(u)<=i<P(g); call their number kappa_i. This is a legal gate split for (A,B), so S0001 (SURVIVED_REVIEW) gives log2 rank_R(M_i) <= kappa_i+1. Summing over i: sum_i kappa_i = sum over wires of #{i in [1,N-1]: P(u)<=i<P(g)} = sum over wires of (P(g)-P(u)), because 1<=P(u) and P(g)<=N. So the sum is <= Lambda(C)+(N-1). (2) holds since 0<=P(g)-P(u)<=N-1 and each gate has at most 2 wires. Corollary (CEILING): rank_R(M_i) <= 2^{min(i,N-i)}, so sum_i log2 rank <= N^2/4 and the bound gives |G| >= (N^2/4-(N-1))/(2(N-1)) = N/8 - O(1) at most. The method cannot give a superlinear bound for any N-input function using prefix cuts.

label: S0012
statement: S0002 (repair of S0001, kind LEMMA). Setting: Boolean circuit C of fan-in at most 2 over AND, OR, NOT, with input nodes x_1..x_(n+m); Alice holds x_1..x_n, Bob holds the rest; f(a,b) is the output. Assign every node (inputs and gates) to a party. Let kappa = number of DAG edges whose endpoints lie on different parties, input edges included. Claim: DCC(f) <= kappa+1 and log2 rank_Q M_f <= kappa+1, where M_f[a,b] = f(a,b). Proof: fix the schedule in topological order; each node is evaluated by its owner once its inputs are known. For every node that has at least one crossing out-edge, its owner sends its value once; the number of such sources is at most kappa. The output owner sends the output bit (at most 1 more). The protocol is deterministic, costs at most kappa+1 and computes f. A protocol of cost c has at most 2^c leaves, each a combinatorial rectangle on which f is constant, so M_f is a sum of at most 2^c indicator rectangles over the 1-leaves and rank_Q M_f <= 2^c. This is an upper bound, not a lower bound, so the barrier check does not apply. Gap: the aggregate G0001 (cut costs over many partitions) stays open. Evidence: cm-5d2f4c68ffda4c45 (exploratory check).

label: S0026
statement: LEMMA (subclass, cut width). Fix a variable order pi and a level l. Call a node prefix-side if its support lies in the first l variables. Let kappa_l be the number of prefix-side nodes with an edge into a non-prefix-side gate. Then the level width K_l (number of distinct residual functions C restricted to rho, for rho in {0,1}^l) satisfies K_l <= 2^kappa_l, because each non-prefix-side gate's value under rho depends on rho only through the constant values of the kappa_l crossing nodes. Hence the OBDD size for order pi is at most sum_l 2^kappa_l. COROLLARY: if kappa_l <= c log n for all l, then #SAT of C runs in poly(n, m) time by building the OBDD. This is the standard cut-width / OBDD-width technique and is not new; it is recorded only as a verified subclass.

structure.gap: G0001 is NOT closed: this is a single-order, log-cut-width subclass. The aggregate over many partitions remains open, and the multiplier family (G0013) shows that no OBDD-size bound can be polynomial for all poly-size circuits.

structure.lemma: Repaired cut width (single order, single level l). P = first l variables in order pi. X = prefix-side nodes feeding a gate whose support is not inside P, k = |X|. o = 1 if the output support is inside P, else 0. Then K_l <= 2^k if o = 0, and K_l <= 2 if o = 1. Proof: prefix-only gates are fixed by rho; by induction every non-prefix node depends only on (c_X(rho), y); so the residual equals F_{c_X(rho)}, giving at most 2^k residuals; if o = 1 the residual is constant in y, giving at most 2.

structure.lemma: Repaired cut lemma (single partition). C is a Boolean circuit over inputs a (Alice) and b (Bob). Every node (input or gate) has an owner in {Alice, Bob}; input nodes belong to their holder. kappa = number of wires u->g whose endpoints have different owners, input wires included. Let M_f be the communication matrix of f with rows indexed by a and columns by b. Then log2 rank_Q(M_f) <= kappa + 1. Proof: the protocol evaluates nodes in topological order. A deterministic protocol of cost c partitions the matrix into at most 2^c monochromatic rectangles, and rank_Q(M) is at most the number of 1-rectangles, so rank_Q(M_f) <= 2^(kappa+1). structure.lemma: Single-order residual-width sum (identity order). C is a fan-in-2 circuit over x_0..x_{n-1} with gates G, output node out, computing f. For a node v let t(v) = bit_length of its support bitmask, so t(v) = 1 + max variable index in the support. Let Lambda(C) = sum over wires u->g of max(0, t(g) - t(u)). For l = 0..n let K_l = number of distinct residual functions f restricted to x_{<l} = rho, over rho in {0,1}^l. Then sum_{l=0}^{n} log2 K_l <= Lambda(C) + #{l : t(out) <= l}. Proof: fix l and P = {0..l-1}. Let X_l be the set of prefix-side nodes (support inside P) that feed a non-prefix gate. By the S0026 argument, if out is non-prefix then K_l <= 2^{|X_l|}; if out is prefix-side then K_l <= 2. Since supports grow along wires, t(g) >= t(u) for every wire u->g. Each w in X_l has a wire w->g with t(w) <= l < t(g), so |X_l| <= #{wires u->g : t(u) <= l < t(g)}. Summing over l, each wire with t(u) < t(g) is counted exactly t(g)-t(u) times, so sum_l |X_l| <= Lambda(C). Adding the at most one bit per level where out is prefix-side gives the claim. Scope: a single fixed variable order; Lambda depends on the order and can be about |C| * N for a bad order.

label: S0042
statement: LOCAL-BOUND-REPAIR (CLAIMED, bookkeeping; does not close G0001). Setting: fan-in <= 2 circuit C on inputs x_1..x_n, prefix split X_l = {x_1..x_l} (rho) versus Y = rest (y), with a gate partition into left and right such that no wire goes right to left. Let kappa = number of left-to-right wires and K = number of distinct residual functions C|rho (functions of y). Claim: K <= 2^(kappa+1). PROOF: left nodes depend only on rho. Case A, output on the right: each right node is a function of y and of the crossing bits, and the crossing bits are functions of rho, so C|rho depends only on the crossing vector in {0,1}^kappa; hence K <= 2^kappa. Case B, output on the left: C|rho is constant in y, so only two residuals occur, K <= 2 <= 2^(kappa+1). Combining, K <= 2^(kappa+1), and so log2 K_l <= kappa_l + [output on left]. Summing over l gives sum_l log2 K_l <= Lambda + #{l : output on left}, which is the corrected S0031 with the output indicator. Tightness: the example above has K=2 with kappa=0. SCOPE: prefix splits, one fixed gate partition, fan-in <= 2 (fan-in is not used beyond the wire count). Indexing caveat: the 'left' set in the lab script is {0..l-1} ∪ {n..t-1}; the output-on-left indicator must be stated in that convention. G0001 (aggregate over many partitions) remains OPEN.

label: S0044
statement: REPAIR of S0001 (single-split cut lemma, input wires counted). Statement: Let C be a fan-in<=2 Boolean circuit on inputs X disjoint-union Y computing f, with communication matrix M_f (rows indexed by assignments to X, columns by assignments to Y). Fix any side assignment of all nodes (inputs included) to {A,B} with every x in X on A and every y in Y on B; gates may be placed freely. Let kappa = number of EDGES (u,g) of C with side(u) != side(g), input nodes included. Then rank_Q(M_f) <= 2^(kappa+1). PROOF: fix a topological order v_1..v_T (inputs first). Alice holds a, Bob holds b. Process v_1..v_T in order: the owner of v (the party of side(v)) computes val(v) from its own input bits and from values already received; every in-neighbour u of v on the other side has a cross edge (u,v), so u has a cross out-edge and was transmitted when processed, hence the owner of v has it. The owner transmits val(v) as one bit exactly when v has at least one cross out-edge. After all nodes, if the output node o was not transmitted, its owner sends val(o) as one final bit. Both parties then know f(a,b). MESSAGE COUNT: each transmitted node has >=1 cross out-edge and out-edge sets of distinct nodes are disjoint, so at most kappa nodes are transmitted; total <= kappa+1 bits. The schedule (order, sender rule) is fixed in advance, so the transcript determines whose turn it is. RECTANGLE: a deterministic protocol with c bits has at most 2^c leaves; the inputs reaching a leaf form a rectangle A_l x B_l (standard, since each message depends only on the sender's input and the transcript); f is constant on each leaf because val(o) is in the transcript (either transmitted or the final bit). So M_f = sum over leaves with f=1 of 1_{A_l} 1_{B_l}^T, a sum of at most 2^(kappa+1) rank-one matrices, hence rank_Q(M_f) <= 2^(kappa+1). QED. SCOPE: one fixed split X|Y, any gate placement, any side assignment (the best bound is min over assignments of kappa). This is the standard circuit-to-communication argument (folklore, not claimed as new); it is bookkeeping, it does NOT close G0001 or G0002 (aggregate over many partitions) or G0005(a). It is not a LOWER_BOUND and does not trigger the barrier check. Consistency check on the refuted case: for IP_2 with all gates on Alice's side the input edges b1->AND1 and b2->AND2 are cross edges, so kappa=2 and the bound 8 >= rank 3; the gate-only count gives kappa=0 and the false bound 2.

label: S0046
statement: MINLA LEMMA (limit of the single-order prefix route; does not close G0001/G0002). Let G be a graph on n vertices with edge expansion h = min over S with 1<=|S|<=n/2 of |boundary(S)|/|S|. For any linear order v_1..v_n let cut_k = number of edges with one endpoint in {v_1..v_k} and the other outside. Then sum_{k=1}^{n-1} cut_k >= h*floor(n^2/4). PROOF: for k <= n/2, S={v_1..v_k} has |S| = k <= n/2, so cut_k >= h*k. For k > n/2, T={v_{k+1}..v_n} has |T| = n-k < n/2 and cut_k = |boundary(T)| >= h*(n-k). So cut_k >= h*min(k, n-k). Summing, and using sum_{k=1}^{n-1} min(k, n-k) = floor(n^2/4) (checked: n=3 gives 2, n=4 gives 4), the claim follows. CONSEQUENCE: for a fan-in-2 circuit C of size s whose underlying graph (all nodes, inputs included, n <= s + #inputs) has constant expansion h, the telescoping sum Lambda_pi = sum_k cut_k of the prefix chain (the identity sum_l kappa_l = Lambda_pi from the prefix cut lemma) is at least h*floor(n^2/4) = Omega(s^2) for EVERY order pi. So min over orders of Lambda_pi, and with it the bound sum_l log2 K_l <= Lambda_pi + n, is Omega(s^2) for such circuits and cannot give O(s polylog s). SCOPE: the lower bound is for any graph; it applies to any circuit family whose underlying graph is an expander, provided the expansion is verified for that family. CORRECTION of S0042: with output on the left, C|rho is constant in y, so K <= 2 (not K = 1); the bound K <= 2^(kappa+1) is unchanged.

label: S0050
statement: PROOF. (1) By induction over a topological order, every node in P has a value that depends only on a, since P is closed under predecessors. (2) Let W be the set of wires leaving P; |W| = w(P). For any node outside P, its value is a function of its own inputs, which are either suffix inputs, outside gates, or wires in W. So for each suffix assignment b there is a function G_b with f(a,b) = G_b(z(a)), where z(a) in {0,1}^W lists the values carried by the wires in W. (3) Therefore f(a,.) = G_(.)(z(a)) is determined by z(a), which takes at most 2^(w(P)) values, so at most 2^(w(P)) distinct subfunctions occur. QED. Consequence: if every level l admits a closed prefix set with w_l <= W, then the OBDD has size at most n 2^W and #SAT of C takes time about n 2^W poly(s). For W = O(log s) this is polynomial.

(d) Expander-like circuits have w_l >= h min(l, n-l) for every closed or non-closed set, so the bound is 2^(Omega(n)) on those families, consistent with S0046. Let w(P) = number of wires u->g with u in P and g not in P. Claim: the number of distinct subfunctions f(a,.), a in {0,1}^l, is at most 2^(w(P)). Hence the OBDD for the order x_1..x_n has size at most sum_l 2^(w_l), where w_l is the boundary of a closed prefix set at level l.

label: S0053
statement: PROOF. Case 1, output on Bob's side. Induction in topological order: every Bob-side node value is a function of (y, z(x)), where z(x) in {0,1}^X is the vector of values of X-nodes (a Bob gate reads Bob nodes or X-nodes only). So row M[x,.] depends only on z(x); there are at most 2^|X| distinct rows, and rank <= number of distinct rows. Case 2, output on Alice's side: f(x,y) = out(x) does not depend on y, so rank <= 1. Hence log2 rank <= |X|. TIGHTNESS: f = AND_i NOT(x_i AND y_i) (disjointness), h = m, Bob reads each x_i, |X| = m, and M_f is the m-fold tensor power of [[1,1],[1,0]] (det -1), so rank = 2^m and log2 rank = m = |X|. The +1 in the earlier statement is slack, not needed.

label: S0055
statement: PROOF OF L1. (i) By induction on topological order, every A-node is a function of x alone: x-inputs trivially; an A-gate's inputs are A-nodes because no B-node feeds an A-gate. (ii) Let S(x) in {0,1}^kappa be the values of the kappa cross nodes (A-nodes with a B-consumer), which are functions of x by (i). By induction every B-node is a function of (y, S(x)): its inputs are y-inputs, B-nodes, or A-nodes, and any A-node feeding a B-node is a cross node, hence a coordinate of S(x). So f(x,y) = G(S(x), y) for some G. If the output node is an A-node, then f = h(x) and M_f has rank <= 1 <= 2^kappa. (iii) For s in {0,1}^kappa let u_s be the indicator vector of {x : S(x) = s} and w_s(y) = G(s,y). Then M_f = sum over s of u_s w_s^T, a sum of at most 2^kappa rank-<=1 matrices over Q, so rank_Q M_f <= 2^kappa. QED.

label: S0056
statement: PROOF OF L2. Fix a topological order v_1,...,v_N of the circuit. Let c_1,...,c_kappa be the nodes of K in that order; each c_i is owned by Alice (A) or Bob (B). Protocol: for i = 1..kappa the owner of c_i sends the bit value(c_i), then the output owner sends f's bit if f is not in K, i.e. at most kappa+1 bits. Well-defined and deterministic: the speaker sequence depends only on the circuit and the side assignment, not on the inputs. Correctness: when the owner of c_i speaks, it knows its own input and all bits sent so far, and it can compute c_i. Induction on the topological order: any input of c_i is either an input node (owned by the speaker, since inputs lie on their own side), a node on the speaker's side (computed by the speaker by induction), or a node on the other side with a consumer on the speaker's side, hence in K, hence earlier in the order and already sent. So value(c_i) is a function of the speaker's input and the transcript so far. Thus the transcript determines all of K and f. Rectangles: for a fixed transcript tau, the set of x with tau consistent is a set X_tau, and similarly Y_tau for y; by the standard induction over rounds the set {(x,y): transcript = tau} equals X_tau x Y_tau. On a leaf f is constant (it is determined by tau). Hence M_f = sum over leaves with f=1 of u_tau w_tau^T with u, w 0/1 vectors, so rank_Q M_f <= number of leaves <= 2^(kappa+1). QED. Note: L2 does not use the one-way hypothesis; L1 (one-way, bound 2^kappa without +1) remains a separate sharper statement.

Note: L2 does not use the one-way hypothesis; L1 (one-way, bound 2^kappa without +1) remains a separate sharper statement.

label: S0061
statement: Proof: Alice and Bob process gates in topological order. Each cross edge carries one bit, sent by the side that owns its source once the source value is determined from that side's inputs and previously received bits. Total communication is at most kappa bits. The output bit adds 1, so the deterministic communication complexity satisfies D(f) <= kappa+1. A deterministic protocol of depth d partitions the matrix into at most 2^d monochromatic rectangles, each of rank at most 1, so rank_R M_f <= 2^d. Hence log2 rank_R M_f <= kappa+1.

label: S0062
statement: Proof: Protocol: each cross edge carries the value of its source gate, sent by the owner of the source once that value is determined. Each gate is evaluated by the side that owns it, using its own inputs and bits received so far. Total communication is exactly kappa bits, so the protocol tree has at most 2^kappa leaves. For each leaf, the set of (a,b) reaching it is a combinatorial rectangle R_l on which f is constant. M_f = sum over 1-leaves of the indicator matrices of R_l. Each indicator of a rectangle has real rank at most 1, so rank_R(M_f) <= number of 1-leaves <= 2^kappa. Hence log2 rank_R(M_f) <= kappa.

label: S0076
statement: L-K1-LOCAL-REPAIR (R1367, claude-haiku-5-5): fan-in<=2 Boolean circuit C over AND OR NOT, fixed topological order, variable order v_1..v_N. For level l let P = nodes with support inside first l variables, kappa_l = number of edges from P into non-P nodes, K_l = number of distinct functions C restricted to rho for rho in {0,1}^l. Claim: K_l <= 2^(kappa_l+1). Proof: if output not in P, each non-P node depends on rho only through the boundary values of P, so C|rho is determined by a vector in {0,1}^kappa_l, giving K_l <= 2^kappa_l. If output in P, C|rho is constant in the remaining variables, so K_l <= 2 <= 2^(kappa_l+1). Corollary: sum_l K_l <= sum_l 2^(kappa_l+1) bounds the OBDD size for this order; #SAT in poly time when kappa_l <= c log N for all l. Scope: one order, one level, fan-in 2. Standard cut-width/OBDD technique, verified subclass only. Does not close G0001.

structure.lemma: One-directional cut bound: if all edges between L and R go from L to R and there are kappa of them, then the rank over Q of the communication matrix of the output (rows x_L, columns x_R) is at most 2^kappa. Proof: by induction on topological order, every R-gate value is a function of x_R and the kappa cross-edge tail values, which are functions of x_L; so f(x_L,x_R)=g(w(x_L),x_R) with w in {0,1}^kappa, giving at most 2^kappa distinct rows.

label: S0006
statement: PROOF. (a) Restricted gate = [R_j(x_A) + S_j >= t_j], R_j = sum_{i in A} w_ji x_i. If A has p positive and q negative weights, R_j takes every integer value in [-q, p] (choose a positive-weight and b negative-weight variables; value a-b covers the whole interval), so the value set is exactly [L_j, U_j] with U_j-L_j = p+q = k. The gate is non-constant iff U_j+S_j >= t_j and L_j+S_j < t_j, i.e. t_j-U_j <= S_j < t_j-L_j; this window contains k integers. (b) Erdos-Littlewood-Offord (Erdos 1945): for reals a_1..a_f with |a_i|>=1 and any real x, #{eps in {0,1}^f : |sum a_i eps_i - x| < 1} <= binom(f, floor(f/2)). Apply with a_i = w_ji (i in F) and x = s an integer: Pr_z[S_j=s] <= binom(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= 1/sqrt(f), using binom(2r,r)/4^r <= 1/sqrt(3r+1) and binom(2r+1,r)/2^(2r+1) = binom(2r+2,r+1)/2^(2r+2) <= 1/sqrt(3r+4). Gate j is non-constant only if S_j lies in one of k integers, so Pr_z[j non-constant] <= k/sqrt(f). Summing over j by linearity gives E_z[N] <= m k/sqrt(n-k). QED. CONSEQUENCE: with k = round(n^delta), delta < 1/2, the expected surviving fraction is <= n^(delta-1/2)(1+o(1)) -> 0 polynomially; at delta = 1/2 it is O(1). Consistency check (not a sharpness test): k/sqrt(n-k) = 1.155 (n=16,k=4), 1.118 (n=25,k=5), 1.080 (n=49,k=7), above the observed fractions 0.74, 0.72, 0.70 in cm-9e6b480beb584cee. SCOPE AND LIMITS: +-1 weights only (the MAJ∘MAJ bottom layer). For general THR weights the window has sum_A|w_ji| integer points and the bound becomes sum_A|w_ji|/sqrt(#(F ∩ supp)), which is useless for large weights, so Chen-Tal-Wang's general THR∘THR count is NOT covered. KNOWLEDGE gain: exact characterisation (a) and an expectation bound (b) for the ±1 case. ALGORITHMIC gain: none yet - the polynomial-approximation step of a CAPP algorithm is still open, and the bound does not yet yield a running time. Erdos-Littlewood-Offord is classical; the new content is the exact characterisation and the application to the restricted MAJ∘MAJ bottom layer.

label: S0012
statement: GENERAL-WEIGHT ALIVE-SURVIVAL LEMMA (integer weights, S0007). Setting: w_ji, t_j integers; A subset [n], |A|=k, F=[n]\A, f=n-k; z uniform on {0,1}^F; L_j = sum_{i in A} min(0,w_ji), U_j = sum_{i in A} max(0,w_ji), S_j(z) = sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i, f_j = #{i in F : w_ji != 0}, N(A,z) = #{j : T_j restricted to x_F=z is non-constant on {0,1}^A}. Then (a) INCLUSION: if gate j is non-constant then t_j - U_j <= S_j(z) < t_j - L_j; the window holds exactly U_j - L_j integers. (b) For f_j >= 1: Pr_z[j non-constant] <= (U_j - L_j)/sqrt(f_j). (c) E_z[N(A,z)] <= sum_{j: f_j>=1} (U_j-L_j)/sqrt(f_j) + #{j : f_j = 0 and t_j - U_j <= 0 < t_j - L_j}. PROOF. (a) The restricted gate is [R_j(x_A) >= t_j - S_j(z)] with R_j = sum_{i in A} w_ji x_i, whose values lie in [L_j, U_j]. Non-constancy gives some x_A with R_j >= t_j - S_j, so U_j >= t_j - S_j; and some x_A' with R_j < t_j - S_j, so L_j < t_j - S_j. These are the two inequalities. Integrality gives the count U_j-L_j. (b) S_j depends only on the f_j coordinates with nonzero weight, which are uniform bits. Each nonzero weight has |w| >= 1, so Erdos (1945) gives Pr[S_j in an open interval of length 2] <= binom(f_j, floor(f_j/2))/2^{f_j} <= 1/sqrt(f_j). Summing over the U_j-L_j integers in the window gives (b). (c) For f_j = 0, S_j = 0 and the gate is non-constant iff the window contains 0; for f_j >= 1 use (b); then linearity. QED. CHECK: for +-1 weights with all F-weights nonzero, f_j = f and U_j - L_j = k, so (c) reduces to S0006. SCOPE AND CAVEAT: the exploratory check cm-9284392501944f05 summed only over gates with f_j >= 1, so it did not test the f_j = 0 term in (c); the term is needed for general weights and is covered by this proof, not by that run. Progress: bookkeeping. The bound is in expectation, costs 2^k per surviving gate, and closes no obligation (G0001, G0002, G0007 stay OPEN).

label: S0017
statement: REPAIR of S0012(b), general nonzero integer weights (CLAIMED, for review). Setting as in S0012, with f_j = #{i in F : w_ji != 0}. Claim: E_z[N(A,z)] <= sum_j (U_j - L_j) * a_j, where a_j = C(f_j, floor(f_j/2))/2^{f_j} <= 1/sqrt(f_j) whenever f_j >= 1. Proof: (1) Window identity from S0012(a): gate j is non-constant iff S_j(z) lies in a set of U_j - L_j consecutive integers. (2) Union bound: Pr_z[S_j in window] <= (U_j-L_j) * max_c Pr_z[S_j(z)=c]. (3) Erdos Littlewood-Offord: S_j is a sum of f_j terms of integer absolute value >= 1, and the number of subsets with sum in any open interval of length 2 is at most C(f_j, floor(f_j/2)); so each point atom is at most a_j. (4) C(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= 1/sqrt(f) for f >= 1. Hence E_z[N] <= sum_j (U_j-L_j)/sqrt(f_j). Scope: this is an expectation bound with the sum over gates; for f_j = 0 the gate is deterministic and the bound must be replaced by an indicator term, so the statement needs f_j >= 1 or a separate count of such gates. Exact check: cm-8dbbae68545b4cff (corrected window bound: 0 violations in 300 instances; worst ratio 0.707). Does NOT close G0007(ii) (deterministic bound) or G0001.

label: S0031
statement: LEMMA D (derandomised window bound, scope: +-1 weights on A and F, A fixed). Setting: disjoint A, F with |A|=k>=1, |F|=f>=1; gates g_j(x,z) = [sum_{i in A} w_ji x_i + sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i >= t_j], w_ji in {-1,+1}, t_j integer, j=1..m. For z in {0,1}^F let N(z) = number of j with g_j(.,z) non-constant on {0,1}^A. CLAIM: a deterministic procedure computes z* in {0,1}^F with N(z*) <= m k / sqrt(f) using O(m f^3) arithmetic operations on integers of O(f) bits. PROOF. (a) Let L_j = sum_{i in A} min(0,w_ji), U_j = sum_{i in A} max(0,w_ji); U_j - L_j = k. g_j is non-constant given z iff L_j + S_j < t_j <= U_j + S_j, S_j = sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i, i.e. S_j lies in an integer window of exactly k integers. (b) By S0006(b) (sign flip y_i = z_i or 1-z_i, Y ~ Bin(f,1/2), central binomial bound), for uniform z: Pr[g_j non-constant] <= k C(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= k/sqrt(f). (c) For a prefix b in {0,1}^p of z, let E(b) = sum_j Pr_{z''}[g_j non-constant | z_{1..p} = b], z'' uniform on {0,1}^{f-p}. Then E(b) = (E(b0)+E(b1))/2, so min(E(b0),E(b1)) <= E(b). The procedure sets b_{p+1} to the minimiser; E is non-increasing along the run; at p=f, E equals N(z*) because each term is then 0/1. E(empty) = sum_j Pr[...] <= m k/sqrt(f) by (b). Hence N(z*) <= m k/sqrt(f). (d) Cost: for a fixed prefix, Pr[g_j non-constant | prefix] = Pr[t_j - U_j - c_j <= S'_j < t_j - L_j - c_j] with c_j the fixed-prefix contribution and S' the free-part sum. S' has a distribution over [-f,f] computed by a DP in O(f^2) operations (exact, with weights 2^{-(f-p)}). Each step evaluates 2 candidates over m gates: O(m f^2) per step, O(m f^3) in total. QED. SCOPE AND LIMITS: (i) +-1 weights only; (ii) A fixed in advance (the adaptive choice of A, G0016, is still open); (iii) the bound m k/sqrt(f) is below m only when k < sqrt(f), so it gives no saving at k = sqrt(n) and m = n^1.5; (iv) no CAPP algorithm follows: the later cost is still 2^k times the surviving count. WHAT IT CLOSES: the deterministic-bound part of G0007(ii) and G0008(i) in the form 'a poly-time computable z with a deterministic surviving-gate bound', for fixed A and +-1 weights. It does not close the adaptive-A question, general integer weights (G0009(b)), or Chen-Williams 2019 (Q-05bce643f5). CLAIM: a deterministic procedure computes z* in {0,1}^F with N(z*) <= m k / sqrt(f) using O(m f^3) arithmetic operations on integers of O(f) bits. PROOF. (d) Cost: for a fixed prefix, Pr[g_j non-constant | prefix] = Pr[t_j - U_j - c_j <= S'_j < t_j - L_j - c_j] with c_j the fixed-prefix contribution and S' the free-part sum. statement: LEMMA D2 (self-contained replacement of S0031 LEMMA D; supersedes it, no CLAIMED premise). Scope: disjoint A, F, |A|=k>=1, |F|=f>=1; w_ji in {-1,+1} for i in A and i in F; t_j integers, j=1..m; g_j(x,z)=[sum_A w_ji x_i + sum_F w_ji z_i >= t_j]; N(z)=#{j: g_j(.,z) non-constant on {0,1}^A}. CLAIM: a deterministic poly-time procedure outputs z* in {0,1}^F with N(z*) <= m k / sqrt(f). PROOF. label: S0034
statement: INTEGER-WEIGHT SURVIVOR LEMMA (G0009(b)). Setting: A, F partition [n], |A| = k >= 1, f = |F| >= 1, integer weights w_ji with |w_ji| >= 1 for i in F (zero weights on A allowed), thresholds T_j in Z, gates g_j(x,z) = [sum_A w_ji x_i + sum_F w_ji z_i >= T_j] on x in {0,1}^A, z in {0,1}^F. Let M_j = sum_{i in A} |w_ji| and N(z) = #{j : g_j(., z) non-constant}. CLAIM: (i) for each j, #{z : g_j(., z) non-constant} <= M_j * C(f, floor(f/2)); hence P_z[non-constant] <= M_j / sqrt(f). (ii) E_z N(z) <= (sum_j M_j)/sqrt(f) <= m k B / sqrt(f) if |w| <= B on A. (iii) The conditional-expectation fixing of Lemma S-DERAND gives z* with N(z*) <= E_z N. PROOF. (1) Window: g_j is non-constant iff min_x (A-sum) + S < T_j <= max_x (A-sum) + S, where S = sum_F w_ji z_i. This holds for any integer weights, with no gap condition. With L = sum_A min(0,w_ji) and U = sum_A max(0,w_ji), non-constancy is equivalent to T_j - U <= S <= T_j - L - 1. This is an integer window with exactly U - L = M_j integers. (2) Point masses: put eps_i = 2 z_i - 1 in {-1,+1}. Then S = s iff sum_F w_ji eps_i = 2s - sum_F w_ji. Since |w_ji| >= 1, Erdos's Littlewood-Offord theorem (1945: for reals |b_i| >= 1, an open interval of length 2 contains at most C(f, floor(f/2)) of the 2^f sums sum eps_i b_i) gives #{z : S = s} <= C(f, floor(f/2)) for every integer s. (3) Union: #{z : S in window} <= sum over the M_j window integers of #{z : S = s} <= M_j C(f, floor(f/2)). Dividing by 2^f and using C(f, floor(f/2))/2^f <= 1/sqrt(f) (f >= 1) gives (i). Summing over j gives (ii). (4) Step (iii) uses only that N is an integer-valued function whose expectation is known; the DP for E_p has integer sums in [-fB, fB], so it costs O(m f^2 B) per evaluation and O(m f^3 B) in total. SCOPE: non-zero integer weights on F, arbitrary integers on A, fixed A. Zero weights on F reduce f to f' = #nonzero F-weights, giving 1/sqrt(f'). The ±1 lemma S0006 is the case M_j = k. The lemma says nothing about all z simultaneously, adaptive A, or Chen-Williams 2019.

structure.lemma: INTEGER-WEIGHT WINDOW LEMMA (extends S0006 from +-1 to integer weights; gap G0007(i)). Fix a gate j with integer weights a_i (i in A, |a_i| >= 1, |A| = k) and b_i (i in F, b_i in Z, f' = #{i in F : b_i != 0} >= 1). Let U = sum_A max(0,a_i), L = sum_A min(0,a_i), B = U - L = sum_A |a_i|. For z in {0,1}^F let S(z) = sum_F b_i z_i and N_j(z) = [g_j(.,z) non-constant on {0,1}^A], g_j(x,z) = [sum_A a_i x_i + S(z) >= T]. Then (i) P_{z uniform}[N_j(z)=1] <= B / sqrt(f'). Proof: (1) Non-constancy needs L + S < T <= U + S, so S lies in an integer window of exactly B integers. (2) Sperner: flip y_i = 1 - z_i for b_i < 0 and y_i = z_i otherwise; then S = sum_{F'} |b_i| y_i + const, y uniform on {0,1}^{F'}. Two subsets T1 strictly contained in T2 have sums differing by >= 1, so the level sets {y : sum |b_i| y_i in an open interval of length 1} form an antichain; hence #{y : S = r} <= C(f', floor(f'/2)) and P[S = r] <= C(f',floor(f'/2))/2^{f'} <= 1/sqrt(f') (central binomial bound, f' >= 1). (3) Union over the B window integers. Hence E_z N_j(z) <= B/sqrt(f'). Summing over j: E_z N(z) <= sum_j B_j / sqrt(f'_j). For |a| = 1 this is k/sqrt(f') and recovers S0006. For weights bounded by W, B_j <= k W, so E_z N(z) <= m k W / sqrt(f_min). Derandomisation: the conditional-expectation fixing of S0006 applies unchanged, since each E_p is an exact DP over integer sums in [-W f, W f] (cost O(m f * W f) per evaluation). Scope: integer weights, A fixed in advance, expectation (not deterministic) bound for all z.

label: S0040
statement: DETERMINISTIC_BOUND_LEMMA

structure.evidence: conditional expectation over DP on sums in [-W f, W f] yields deterministic bound on surviving gates
structure.lemma:
Lemma: For any MAJ o MAJ circuit C with integer weights w_j, thresholds T_j, and any deterministic choice function z: {0,1}^F → {0,1}, let N(z) be the number of bottom gates that are non-constant after fixing the free variables according to z. Then

N(z) ≤ m·(k/√n) + C·m/n,

where k is the number of fixed variables, n is the total number of free variables, m is the total number of bottom gates, and C is an absolute constant (e.g., C=2). Consequently, the total cost of evaluating all 2^k restrictions is at most 2^k·(m·k/√n + C·m/n) = o(2^k·m) when k = o(√n).

Proof sketch: Use a DP over the sum S_j(z) that depends only on the fixed variables; the window indicator is a function of S_j. For each gate j, the DP computes the exact probability that S_j falls in the window. By fixing variables in order, the conditional expectation E_p = (E_{p+1}^{z_p=0}+E_{p+1}^{z_p=1})/2, so the greedy choice of z_{p+1} never increases the expectation. Hence the final expectation E_f = N(z) ≤ E_0 = E_z[N(z)] ≤ Σ_j B_j/√(f'_j) with B_j ≤ m and f'_j ≥ n/k, giving N(z) ≤ m·k/√n + C·m/n. QED.

label: S0054
statement: REPAIR of S0006(b). Setting: n >= 1, 0 <= k < n, f = n-k. Weights w_1..w_n in {-1,+1}; for z in {0,1}^k put a(z) = sum_{i<=k} w_i z_i (integer). Free weights w_j (j > k), lo = sum_{j>k} min(w_j,0), hi = sum_{j>k} max(w_j,0), so hi - lo = f. Threshold T uniform on the 2R+1 integers {-R,...,R}, R >= 0. Gate g(x) = [w.x >= T]. Claim: (a) for every z, the restriction x_{[k]} = z leaves g non-constant iff lo < T - a(z) <= hi, and every integer in [lo,hi] is attained by the free sum; (b) for every fixed z, P_T[g|z non-constant] <= f/(2R+1). Hence for m independent gates with thresholds T_j uniform on {-R..R}, E[N(z)] <= m f/(2R+1) for every z, where N(z) = number of non-constant gates after fixing z. Proof: (a) The free sum S = sum_{j>k} w_j x_j takes each integer value in [lo,hi] (each coordinate moves S by one step in the value set), and g|z = [S >= T - a(z)], which is constant 0 iff T-a(z) > hi and constant 1 iff T-a(z) <= lo. (b) Non-constancy means T - a(z) is an integer in (lo, hi]; there are exactly hi - lo = f such integers, so the number of T in {-R..R} with this property is at most f, giving the bound f/(2R+1). Linearity of expectation gives the count bound.

structure.gap: This repairs S0006(b) but does not close G0007(ii) or G0008(i). (1) It is an expectation over a uniformly random threshold for each fixed z, not a deterministic bound for adversarial thresholds: an adversary choosing T_j in the window makes every gate survive. (2) The bound m f/(2R+1) gives the k-free form m k/sqrt(f) only when R >= f^{3/2}/(2k), so the claimed k/sqrt(f) scaling is not a consequence of the window. Numerical check: (n,k,m)=(10,3,40) bound 18.7 vs observed 17.9; (20,3,60) bound 53.7 vs observed 50.3; (30,5,100) bound 108.7 vs observed 93.0 (cm-c9726df7085f438d). (3) The survivors-per-z bound yields no CAPP algorithm, since the cost is still 2^k times the count. (4) The derandomised z* of Lemma D needs E over z of N(z) for a fixed threshold vector, which this lemma does not give. Open: a threshold-independent (deterministic) bound on non-constant gates for every restriction, and an adversarial-threshold analysis.

label: S0059
statement: LEMMA (sharpened expectation and deterministic poly-time restriction). Setting: n>=2, 1<=k<n, r=n-k, m>=1, W in {+-1}^{m x n}, t in Z^m, F subset [n] with |F|=k, G=[n]\F. For z in {0,1}^G define N_F(z) = #{j : the gate y -> [W_j.(z,y) >= t_j] is non-constant in y in {0,1}^F}. Claim: (a) E_{z uniform} N_F(z) <= m k beta_r, with beta_r = C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r; (b) beta_r <= 1/sqrt(r); (c) there is a deterministic procedure, polynomial in n and m, that outputs z with N_F(z) <= E_z N_F <= m k/sqrt(r). PROOF. Fix gate j, put A_j(z) = sum_{i in G} W_ji z_i and S_j(y) = sum_{i in F} W_ji y_i. label: S0061
statement: LEMMA (shared-weight MAJ o MAJ counting). Let w in Z^n with |w_i| <= W, thresholds t_1..t_m in Z, weights v_j in Z, integer T, and C(x) = [sum_j v_j [w.x >= t_j] >= T] for x in {0,1}^n. Then #{x : C(x)=1} is computed exactly in O(n^2 W + m) arithmetic operations. Proof: s(x) = w.x ranges over an integer interval R of size at most 2nW+1. The DP dist_0 = {0:1}, dist_i = dist_{i-1} convolved with {0:1, w_i:1} gives dist_n(s) = #{x : w.x = s} exactly, in O(n * |R|) time. Since C depends on x only through s, the answer is sum over s in R with g(s) >= T of dist_n(s), where g(s) = sum_j v_j [s >= t_j] is computed for all s in R by sorting thresholds and prefix sums in O(|R| + m). Correctness follows since the DP counts x by their value of w.x. Scope: one shared weight vector, bounded integer weights. This is a restricted subclass only: it does not decide the general MAJ o MAJ CAPP obligation (G0001) and does not handle distinct bottom weight vectors.

label: S0063
statement: LEMMA (k-class DP for MAJ o MAJ, exact). Let W >= 1, k >= 1, n >= 1. Let w^(1),...,w^(k) in Z^n with |w^(c)_i| <= W. Let bottom gates g_j(x) = [w^(c_j).x >= t_j] for j = 1..m with class labels c_j in {1..k}, integer thresholds t_j, integer top weights v_j, and integer T. Let C(x) = [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T]. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : C(x) = 1} is computed exactly in time O(n k S + m S) where S <= min(2^n, (nW+1)^k) is the number of distinct states. Proof: (i) u(x) = (w^(1).x, ..., w^(k).x) in Z^k; C depends on x only through u(x), since g_j depends only on u_{c_j}(x). (ii) For each c, lo_c = sum_i min(0, w^(c)_i) and hi_c = sum_i max(0, w^(c)_i) satisfy hi_c - lo_c = sum_i |w^(c)_i| <= nW, so u_c(x) lies in an integer interval of size <= nW+1; hence the set of attainable u is contained in a box of at most (nW+1)^k points, and of size at most 2^n. (iii) The DP dist_0 = {0^k: 1}, dist_i(u) = dist_{i-1}(u) + dist_{i-1}(u - col_i), where col_i = (w^(1)_i,...,w^(k)_i), satisfies dist_n(u) = #{x : u(x) = u}; each layer has at most S states. (iv) The answer is the sum of dist_n(u) over u with sum_j v_j [u_{c_j} >= t_j] >= T. Consequence: for k <= (1-delta) n / log2(n W + 1) the count is computed exactly in time 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n) (since (nW+1)^k <= 2^{(1-delta) n}). For W = 1: k <= (1-delta) n / log2(n+1) gives 2^{(1-delta) n} poly(n), with exact output, so the error is 0 and the algorithm is deterministic. Scope: bounded integer weights per coordinate, number of DISTINCT weight vectors k at most (1-delta) n / log2(nW+1), arbitrary poly m. This is a restricted subclass. It does NOT close G0001 or G0002 (general MAJ o MAJ has k up to m = poly, so the bound becomes (nW+1)^m), and it does not establish Chen-Williams 2019 (Q-05bce643f5 still unverified).

label: S0066
statement: LEMMA (claimed, for review). Setup: W_j in {-1,+1}^n, F subset [n] with |F|=k, R=[n]\F, f=n-k, M_j = #{i in R: W_ji=-1}, delta in (0,1/2). For integer T let P_j(T) = Pr_{x uniform in {0,1}^R}[sum_{i in R} W_ji x_i >= T] and A_j = {T in Z : delta <= P_j(T) <= 1-delta}. For z in {0,1}^F let T_j(z) = t_j - sum_{i in F} W_ji z_i, and flip_j(z,z') = [T_j(z) in A_j] xor [T_j(z') in A_j]. (a) A_j is an integer interval (possibly empty). Proof: with y_i = x_i if W_ji=+1 and y_i = 1-x_i if W_ji=-1, sum_R W_ji x_i = sum_R y_i - M_j, so P_j(T) = Pr[Bin(f,1/2) >= T+M_j], nonincreasing in T; {P<=1-delta} is upward closed and {P>=delta} downward closed, so their intersection is an integer interval. (b) If flip_j(z,z') then dist(T_j(z), {min A_j, max A_j}) <= |Delta_j|, Delta_j = T_j(z') - T_j(z). Proof: write T=T_j(z), T'=T+Delta, A=[L,H]. If T in A and T' not in A then T' < L or T' > H, so T is within |Delta| of L or of H (T-L < L-... i.e. T' < L gives T-L < -Delta <= |Delta|, and T'>H gives H-T < Delta). Symmetric for T not in A, T' in A. (c) Let the thresholds t_j be independent of (z,z') with Pr[t_j = v] <= rho for all v in Z. Then E[#{j : flip_j(z,z')}] <= 2 rho m (sqrt(2k) + 1), expectation over t, z, z' independent and uniform. Proof: Delta_j = sum_{i in F} W_ji (z_i - z'_i) with e_i = z_i - z'_i independent over i, E e_i = 0, E e_i^2 = 1/2, so E Delta_j^2 = k/2 and E|Delta_j| <= sqrt(k/2) by Jensen. Given z,z', by (b) a flip requires t_j in [L - s_j - |Delta_j|, L - s_j + |Delta_j|] or the same around H, where s_j = sum_F W_ji z_i and L,H depend only on W, F (not on t, z'). Each is an integer interval of 2|Delta_j|+1 points, so Pr_t[flip_j] <= 2 rho (2|Delta_j|+1). Taking expectation over z,z' gives E flip_j <= 2 rho (2 sqrt(k/2) + 1) = 2 rho (sqrt(2k) + 1); sum over j. (d) Corollary: if t_j is uniform on 2R+1 integers around a centre, rho = 1/(2R+1); with R >= a sqrt(n) this gives E flips <= m(sqrt(2k)+1)/(a sqrt(n)) approximately, i.e. the sqrt(k/n)/a shape measured in cm-09dc3c1260e64590, now with a proof (for this z-vs-z' event, not for the full-vs-restriction comparison used there, whose binomial parameters differ).

label: S0069
statement: LEMMA (pm1 derandomisation, fixed A). Setup: F of size f with weights w in {+1,-1}^F, A of size k with weights u in {+1,-1}^A, thresholds t_1..t_m integers. Gate j on (z,x) in {0,1}^F x {0,1}^A is [sum_F w_i z_i + sum_A u_i x_i >= t_j]. Let N(z) = number of gates nonconstant in x after fixing z. Claim: a deterministic procedure running in O(m f^3) arithmetic operations on integers of at most f bits outputs z* with N(z*) <= m k / sqrt(f). PROOF. Let L = sum_A min(0,u_i), U = sum_A max(0,u_i), so U-L = k. Step 1 (window): S = sum_F w_i z_i. Over x, the A-sum takes every integer in [L,U] since each u_i = +-1 moves it by one; so gate j is nonconstant iff t_j - S in {L+1..U}, i.e. S in [t_j-U, t_j-L-1], an interval of exactly k integers. Step 2 (Erdos-Sperner): replacing z_i by 1-z_i when w_i = -1 gives positive weights with the same count of solutions per sum, and subsets with equal sums form an antichain, so #{z: S(z)=s} <= C(f, floor(f/2)) <= 2^f/sqrt(f). Hence Pr_z[j nonconstant] <= k 2^f/sqrt(f)/2^f = k/sqrt(f), and E_z[N] <= m k/sqrt(f). Step 3 (exact conditional expectations): for a prefix pi of length i, let a = sum_{l<i} w_l pi_l, p = #{l>=i: w_l=+1}, q = #{l>=i: w_l=-1}. The unfixed sum Y = alpha - beta with alpha ~ Bin(p,1/2), beta ~ Bin(q,1/2) independent. So Pr[j nonconstant | pi] = 2^-(p+q) sum over (x,y) with lo <= x-y <= hi of C(p,x) C(q,y), where lo = t_j-U-a, hi = t_j-L-1-a. This is exact and costs O(f^2) per gate. Let E(pi) = sum_j Pr[j nonconstant | pi]. Then E(pi) = (E(pi0)+E(pi1))/2, so the child with smaller E has E no larger. Greedy over i = 1..f gives z* with E(z*) = N(z*) <= E(empty) = E_z[N] <= m k/sqrt(f). Cost: f levels, 2 children, m gates, O(f^2) each: O(m f^3). SCOPE: +-1 weights only, A fixed in advance (not adaptive), no bound on survivors in time beyond the poly count. Integer weights break Step 3 (Y is no longer binomial). CONSEQUENCE for G0012(i): time poly(m,f) is below 2^k times the bound mk/sqrt(f) whenever 2^k >= C m f^3, i.e. k >= c log(mf). It does NOT yet give G0012(ii) or (iii), and does not cover adaptive A (G0016). This supersedes the S0031 review record marked REFUTED: the claim 'poly-time deterministic z*' is TRUE for +-1 weights, because conditional sums reduce to binomial convolutions, not to 2^f enumeration. The earlier claim that no poly-time method exists was wrong.

statement: LEMMA R3 (repair of S0017 scope: gates with f_j = 0 handled by an indicator). Setting as in S0017: F = set of free variables with f = |F| >= 1, A = restricted variables with |A| = k, w_ji integers with |w_ji| >= 1 on F, real offsets; for gate j let f_j = #{i in F : w_ji != 0}, L_j = sum_A min(0,w_ji), U_j = sum_A max(0,w_ji), S_j(z) = sum_{i in F} w_ji z_i for z uniform on {0,1}^F, and N(A,z) = #{j : gate j non-constant on {0,1}^A}. CLAIM: E_z[N(A,z)] <= D0 + sum_{j: f_j>=1} (U_j - L_j)/sqrt(f_j), where D0 = #{j : f_j = 0 and gate j non-constant on {0,1}^A}, a z-independent integer. PROOF. (1) If f_j = 0 then S_j = 0 for all z, so the indicator of non-constancy is the same for all z; it contributes exactly the z-independent term to N, summing to D0. (2) If f_j >= 1: by the window identity (S0006(a), valid for w in {-1,+1} and for integer |w|>=1 since the A-part value set is all integers in [L_j,U_j] when weights are +-1; for general integer weights the A-part is contained in [L_j,U_j] and the non-constancy event is contained in S_j in a set W_j of at most U_j-L_j integers) gate j non-constant implies S_j(z) in W_j, |W_j| <= U_j - L_j. (3) Erdos 1945: for |w_ji| >= 1 and any open interval I of length 2, #{T subset of F_j : sum_{i in T} w_ji in I} <= C(f_j, floor(f_j/2)). Each integer c lies in the open interval (c-1,c+1), so Pr_z[S_j = c] <= C(f_j,floor(f_j/2))/2^{f_j}. (4) C(f,floor(f/2))/2^f <= 1/sqrt(f) for f >= 1 (central binomial bound binom(2r,r) <= 4^r/sqrt(pi r) for r>=1, and f=1 gives 1/2). It does not close G0001 or G0007(ii). Its status is CLAIMED: the author is claude-haiku-5-5 and an independent reviewer from another model family must check it.

label: S0001
statement:
statement: For every n≥1 and distinct u,v∈{0,1}^n, let y=u∧¬v if u∧¬v≠0; otherwise let y=v∧¬u. Exactly one of u,v is disjoint from y. Thus, if a deterministic one-pass streaming algorithm has the same state after u and v, it gives the same output on (u,y) and (v,y), although their DISJ answers differ, so it errs on at least one.
proof: If u∧¬v≠0, every 1-coordinate of y has u_i=1 and v_i=0; hence u intersects y and v is disjoint from y. Otherwise u_i≤v_i for every i. Since u≠v, some coordinate has v_i=1 and u_i=0, so y=v∧¬u is nonzero, u is disjoint from y, and v intersects y. In either case the two DISJ answers differ. Equal deterministic states after the prefixes, followed by the same suffix, produce the same final state and output.

label: S0002
statement:
statement: For every n≥1 and fixed omitted coordinate i(n)∈[n], let σ_n(x)=x with coordinate i(n) deleted. The prefixes u_n=0^n and v_n=e_{i(n)} collide under σ_n, and the common suffix y_n=e_{i(n)} gives DISJ(u_n,y_n)=1 and DISJ(v_n,y_n)=0. If i(n) is computable by a polylogtime-uniform AC0 family (in particular, if i(n)=1), these prefix and suffix families are uniformly AC0-constructible.
proof: Deleting coordinate i(n) makes u_n and v_n identical on every retained coordinate, so σ_n(u_n)=σ_n(v_n). The all-zero string is disjoint from y_n, while v_n=e_{i(n)} intersects y_n at coordinate i(n), giving opposite DISJ answers. The construction outputs zeros or the unit vector at i(n); under the stated uniformity assumption these strings are generated by the corresponding uniform AC0 family.

label: S0003
statement:
statement: Fix an integer q>=1 and a deterministic one-pass streaming machine A with at most q states. For each n>=q and j in {0,...,q}, let x_j(n)=1^j0^(n-j). Then there is a fixed pair 0<=a<b<=q such that A reaches the same state after x_a(n) and x_b(n) for infinitely many n. Each of the two prefix families is polylogtime-uniform AC0 constructible. For those infinitely many n, the suffix-separation lemma supplies a common suffix on which the two DISJ answers differ.
proof: For each n>=q, the q+1 prefixes x_0(n),...,x_q(n) lead to at most q states. Thus some pair (a_n,b_n) with a_n<b_n collides. There are only binom(q+1,2) possible pairs. If each pair collided at only finitely many n, the union of those finite sets of lengths would be finite, contradicting that a colliding pair exists for every n>=q. Hence one fixed pair (a,b) collides for infinitely many n. For fixed a, x_a(n) is generated by outputting a initial 1s followed by n-a zeros, which is a uniform AC0 family; likewise for b. At each collision length, apply the suffix-separation lemma to x_a(n),x_b(n). This proves the stated result. The pair depends on A, and this argument does not select it uniformly from A.

label: S0004
statement: statement: For integers M>q>=1, every map from an M-element set into a set of at most q states has at least binom(M-q+1,2) unordered colliding pairs. Proof: Let the nonempty fiber sizes be a_1,...,a_r, where r<=q and sum a_i=M. The number of colliding pairs is C=sum_i binom(a_i,2). If two fibers have sizes a>=b>=2, moving one item from the smaller fiber to the larger changes C by binom(a+1,2)+binom(b-1,2)-binom(a,2)-binom(b,2)=a-b+1>=1; hence a minimizing partition has at most one fiber larger than 1. Among at most q fibers this minimum is attained by q-1 singleton fibers and one fiber of size M-q+1, giving C=binom(M-q+1,2). If fewer fibers are used, merging or adding empty fibers does not lower the minimum. This is a counting strengthening of pigeonhole and does not select any colliding pair uniformly from the map.

label: S0005
statement: statement: For integers M>=1 and q>=1, the minimum number of unordered colliding pairs over maps from an M-element set into at most q states is (q-r) binom(a,2)+r binom(a+1,2), where a=floor(M/q) and r=M mod q. Proof: Regard the map as q fiber sizes including empty fibers. Its collision count is the sum of binom(a_i,2). If a_i>=a_j+2, replacing these two sizes by a_i-1 and a_j+1 changes the sum by -(a_i-a_j)+1<0. Thus a minimizing q-tuple has sizes differing by at most 1. The sum and number of fibers then force q-r sizes equal to a and r sizes equal to a+1, giving the formula. Such a partition is realized by a map, so this is the minimum. This is a finite counting lemma and does not select a colliding pair uniformly from a machine.

label: S0006
statement:
statement: For every q>=1, given as input a table of q+1 binary labels of length ceil(log2 q) representing a map f:{0,...,q}->{0,...,q-1}, a lexicographically first colliding pair can be output by a DLOGTIME-uniform AC0 circuit family of size polynomial in q and log q.
proof: For each pair i<j, compute E_ij=[f(i)=f(j)] by bitwise XNORs followed by an AND over the label bits; this has constant depth. Order the pairs lexicographically and compute S_ij=E_ij AND NOT(OR_{(a,b)<(i,j)} E_ab). These priority gates have constant depth with unbounded fan-in. Pigeonhole guarantees some E_ij=1, so exactly the first colliding pair has S_ij=1. Output each index bit by OR-ing the corresponding bits gated by S_ij. There are O(q^2) pairs, and the gates and wires are generated by regular index comparisons and bit positions, giving polynomial size and DLOGTIME uniformity. The table is an explicit input; this does not generate a streaming machine's table uniformly.

label: S0007
statement: statement: For each integer q>=1, let L=ceil(log2 q) (and L=0 when q=1). Given an explicit table of q+1 labels f(0),...,f(q) in {0,1}^L, one can compute the lexicographically first pair i<j with f(i)=f(j) by a DLOGTIME-uniform AC0 circuit family of size O(q^4+q^2 L) in the standard indexed-table encoding. Proof: For each pair i<j form E_ij as the conjunction, over the L coordinates, of equality literals for the corresponding table bits (for L=0 equality is true). Define P_ij = E_ij AND NOT(OR{E_ab : a<b and (a,b)<lex(i,j)}), with empty OR false. Since q+1 labels take only 2^L<=q values when q>=2, and for q=1 the two zero-bit labels are equal, at least one E_ij is true; exactly the lexicographically first true E_ij has P_ij true. Output each binary index bit as the OR over pairs (i,j) of P_ij gated by that pair's constant index bit. Pairwise equality uses O(L) gates per pair. Building each candidate's priority OR independently uses O(q^4) total gates/wires, so the stated bound follows. Gates and wires are indexed by O(log q)-bit pair and coordinate indices; a DLOGTIME uniformity machine determines the wiring and constants in polylog(q) time. This is an explicit-table selector only; it supplies no circuit for generating or accessing the transition table of an arbitrary streaming algorithm.

label: S0010
statement: statement: Let Q be a fixed set of q states, s0 in Q, and T0,T1:Q->Q fixed transition maps. For every fixed j>=0, the state reached after 1^j0^(n-j), for n>=j, is ultimately periodic in n with preperiod < q and period <= q. Proof: Put z=T1^j(s0). The q+1 states T0^t(z), 0<=t<=q, contain a repetition T0^a(z)=T0^b(z) with 0<=a<b<=q. Applying T0 repeatedly gives T0^(t+b-a)(z)=T0^t(z) for every t>=a. Hence the sequence is periodic from a<q with period b-a<=q. For any fixed finite collection of j values, the tuple of reached states is ultimately periodic, using the maximum of the individual preperiods and the least common multiple of their periods. Consequently, for a fixed machine, state labels on a fixed finite collection of these prefix families are computable by a uniform AC0 family whose constants may depend on the machine. This restricted result does not give a uniform selector for machine families whose transition maps or state counts vary with n.

label: S0012
statement:
statement: Lemma (collision count with DISJ separators). Let u_1,...,u_M be distinct strings in {0,1}^n, and let a deterministic streaming machine have at most q states after reading an n-bit prefix. If M>q, at least binom(M-q+1,2) unordered pairs among these prefixes reach the same state. For every such colliding pair u,v, there is a common suffix y in {0,1}^n for which exactly one of u,v is disjoint from y.
Proof. The machine partitions the M prefixes into state fibers of sizes a_1,...,a_r, with r<=q and sum a_i=M. The collision count is sum_i binom(a_i,2). This sum is minimized by q-1 singleton fibers and one fiber of size M-q+1: if two fibers have sizes a>=b>=2, moving one item from the smaller to the larger increases the sum by a-b+1, so a minimizing partition has at most one nonsingleton fiber; adding empty fibers if necessary gives the stated minimum binom(M-q+1,2). For a distinct pair u,v, if u AND NOT v is nonzero, set y=u AND NOT v; then u intersects y and v is disjoint from y. Otherwise u is coordinatewise at most v, and since u!=v, v AND NOT u is nonzero; set y=v AND NOT u, so v intersects y and u is disjoint from y. Thus every colliding pair has a common suffix distinguishing their DISJ answers. Equal deterministic states followed by the same suffix produce the same output, so the machine errs on at least one of the two inputs. This lemma does not uniformly select a colliding pair for an arbitrary machine.

statement: CLAIMED, kind ALGORITHM (boundary result, does NOT close G0001). Statement: let W in Z^{m x n}, t, v in Z^m, T in Z, and suppose the supports S_1..S_m of the rows of W are pairwise disjoint, |S_j| = k_j. Let c_j = #{y in {0,1}^{S_j} : sum_{i in S_j} W[j,i] y_i >= t_j}. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : sum_j v_j [W_j.x >= t_j] >= T} = 2^f * sum_{e >= T} [z^e] prod_j ((2^{k_j} - c_j) + c_j z^{v_j}), with f = n - sum_j k_j. Proof: under uniform x, the events E_j = [W_j.x_{S_j} >= t_j] depend only on disjoint blocks, hence are independent with P[E_j] = c_j/2^{k_j}. Counting patterns (E_j) gives weight 2^f prod_j (c_j if E_j else 2^{k_j} - c_j); summing over patterns with sum_j v_j E_j >= T gives the generating-function formula. Running time: O(sum_j 2^{k_j}) to compute the c_j, plus m block updates on a polynomial of at most m*V+1 coefficients (V = max |v_j|). Scope: exact for every instance with pairwise disjoint supports; no assumption on weights or thresholds. Evidence: cm-07270f02ad1441eb (60 random disjoint-block instances, n in {8,10,12}, 0 mismatches vs brute force, EXPLORATORY_COMPUTATION). Caveat: the identity is elementary (independence of disjoint blocks); its value is that it is an exact polynomial-time procedure on a subclass, not a step toward overlapping supports.

label: S0008
statement: CLAIMED, kind ALGORITHM (sub-case, does NOT close G0001). Statement: let f(x) = [sum_j v_j [W_j . x >= t_j] >= T] on {0,1}^n with integer W, t, v, T and m rows, and let U = union of supp(W_j) over all j with |U| = s. Then #{x in {0,1}^n : f(x)=1} = 2^(n-s) * #{y in {0,1}^U : f(y)=1}, and the right-hand count is computed in time O(2^s * m * s) by enumerating y in {0,1}^U and evaluating each gate. Proof: for each j, W_j . x = W_j|_U . x_U because W_j has zero entries outside U, so f(x) depends only on x_U; the n-s coordinates outside U are free, giving the factor 2^(n-s). The enumeration evaluates m gates of support <= s at each of the 2^s points. Scope: exact for every instance, no assumption on weights, thresholds, or v. Running time 2^(n-s) * 2^s * m * s = 2^n m s is not improved; the saving is 2^s * poly(m, n) when s <= (1-delta) n, i.e. 2^{(1-delta) n} poly. Caveat: this is the junta condition (f depends on at most s variables), a bookkeeping-level fact, not progress towards the general case. For the target size m = n^1.5 with full-support gates, U = [n] and the bound gives 2^n poly, so G0001 is not closed.

label: S0023
statement: LEMMA-ARR (CLAIMED, scope: m bottom gates, any n). For integer W in Z^{m x n}, t in Z^m, the number of distinct patterns P(x) = ([W_j.x >= t_j])_j over x in {0,1}^n is at most sum_{i=0}^{n} C(m,i) <= (e m / n)^n. Proof: [W_j.x >= t_j] iff W_j.x > t_j - 1/2 for integer x, so P(x) is the sign vector of x with respect to the m affine hyperplanes H_j = {y : W_j.y = t_j - 1/2} in R^n. A sign vector with x not on any H_j determines an open cell of the arrangement, and a cell is determined by its sign vector (cells are convex), so distinct patterns <= number of cells. Buck (1943) / Cover (1965): an arrangement of m hyperplanes in R^n has at most sum_{i<=n} C(m,i) regions. Consequence: for m <= n/4, patterns <= (e/4)^n <= 2^{0.56 n}, i.e. delta = 0.44. Scope: this is a known bound (Buck/Cover) applied to the bottom layer; it is not new. It does NOT close G0001: for m = n^alpha with alpha > 1 the bound is at least 2^n, and no algorithm enumerating the realised patterns in 2^{(1-delta)n} time is given.

statement: Lemma statement recorded. Next: prove the exactness (counting identity) and bound K_clip. The identity holds because for fixed x_A, the condition W_j·x ≥ t_j is equivalent to W^B_j·x_B ≥ t_j - W^A_j·x_A. Since W^B_j·x_B ∈ [lo_j, hi_j], values below lo_j are always true (so clip to lo_j), values above hi_j are always false (so clip to hi_j+1 as an impossible threshold). Thus the condition depends on x_A only through c(x_A). Summing over c gives the exact count. The bound on K_clip follows because each c_j takes at most |supp_B(j)| + 2 values.

structure.lemma: Clipped-State DP for THR∘THR #SAT. Let C be a THR∘THR circuit on n variables with m = n^α bottom gates (α > 0). Split variables into X_A (first a = ⌊n/2⌋) and X_B (rest). For each bottom gate j, let W^A_j, W^B_j be its weights on X_A, X_B; threshold t_j. Define lo_j = min_{x_B} W^B_j·x_B, hi_j = max_{x_B} W^B_j·x_B. For x_A ∈ {0,1}^a, the clipped vector c(x_A) ∈ ℤ^m has entries c_j = clip(t_j - W^A_j·x_A, lo_j, hi_j + 1). Then #SAT(C) = Σ_{c ∈ C} |{x_A : c(x_A) = c}| · R(c), where R(c) = |{x_B : (W^B_j·x_B ≥ c_j for all j) is satisfied and the top threshold holds}|. The number of distinct clip vectors K_clip ≤ Π_j (|{W^B_j·x_B : x_B ∈ {0,1}^b}| + 2).

statement: CLAIMED LEMMA (kind LEMMA, does NOT close G0007): Let M_k(x) = [sum_{i in S} x_i >= t], |S| = k, t = floor((k+1)/2), and let a random restriction keep each variable free independently with probability p, fixing each other variable to a uniform bit. Then Pr[M_k nonconstant] = sum_{f=1}^{k} P(Bin(k,p)=f) * P(t-f <= Bin(k-f,1/2) <= t-1). Since the window {t-f,...,t-1} has f points and max_j P(Bin(m,1/2)=j) <= sqrt(2/(pi m))(1+o(1)), we get Pr <= E[f] sqrt(2/(pi(k-f))) = sqrt(2/pi) p sqrt(k) (1+o(1)) + tail, where the tail is controlled by Chernoff for f > k/2. Asymptotic sharpness: as p sqrt(k) -> 0, Pr / (p sqrt(k)) -> sqrt(2/pi) (only f = 1 contributes at first order). Scope: unit-weight majority only; the general-weight case needs a Littlewood-Offord anti-concentration bound and is open. The proof of the tail term is sketched, not written out, so this is CLAIMED until a second session checks it.

statement: CLAIMED LEMMA (kind LEMMA; closes only the tail gap G0051(i), not G0007). Setting: k >= 4, S a set of k variables, t = floor((k+1)/2), M(x) = [sum_{i in S} x_i >= t]. A random restriction keeps each variable of S free independently with probability p in [0,1] and fixes the others to uniform bits. Claim: Pr[M|rho nonconstant] <= (2/sqrt(pi)) sqrt(k/(k-2)) p sqrt(k) + (4p)^{k/2}. PROOF. Let F ~ Bin(k,p) be the number of free variables in S. Given F = f, the fixed part has m = k-f variables and sum s ~ Bin(m,1/2). M|rho is nonconstant iff s <= t-1 and s+f >= t, i.e. s in the window [t-f, t-1], which has f integers. So W_f := Pr[nonconstant | F=f] <= f * max_j P(Bin(m,1/2)=j). (a) Max-pmf bound: for m >= 2, max_j P(Bin(m,1/2)=j) <= sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))). Proof: C(2r,r)/4^r <= 1/sqrt(pi r) for r >= 1 (standard). If m = 2r, the max is C(2r,r)/4^r <= sqrt(2/(pi m)) <= sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))). If m = 2r+1, the max is C(2r,r)/4^r * (2r+1)/(2r+2) <= 1/sqrt(pi r) = sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))). (b) Part f <= k/2: then m >= k/2 >= 2 and m-1 >= (k-2)/2, so W_f <= 2f/sqrt(pi(k-2)). Summing with E[F] = kp gives sum_{f<=k/2} P(F=f) W_f <= 2kp/sqrt(pi(k-2)) = (2/sqrt(pi)) sqrt(k/(k-2)) p sqrt(k). (c) Part f > k/2: sum_{f>k/2} P(F=f) W_f <= P(F >= k/2). Chernoff with e^lambda = (1-p)/p (p in (0,1); p = 0, 1 are trivial) gives P(F >= k/2) <= e^{-lambda k/2} (1-p+p e^lambda)^k = (2 sqrt(p(1-p)))^k <= (4p)^{k/2}. Adding (b) and (c) gives the claim. CHECK: for p sqrt(k) -> c as k -> infinity the true value is ~ sqrt(2/pi) c (only f = 1 contributes at first order), so the constant 2/sqrt(pi) loses a factor sqrt(2). structure.proved_step: CLAIMED LEMMA (kind LEMMA; closes only the tail gap G0051(i), not G0007). Setting: k >= 4, S a set of k variables, t = floor((k+1)/2), M(x) = [sum_{i in S} x_i >= t]. Claim: Pr[M|rho nonconstant] <= (2/sqrt(pi)) sqrt(k/(k-2)) p sqrt(k) + (4p)^{k/2}. PROOF. Let F ~ Bin(k,p) be the number of free variables in S. Given F = f, the fixed part has m = k-f variables and sum s ~ Bin(m,1/2). M|rho is nonconstant iff s <= t-1 and s+f >= t, i.e. s in the window [t-f, t-1], which has f integers. So W_f := Pr[nonconstant | F=f] <= f * max_j P(Bin(m,1/2)=j). (a) Max-pmf bound: for m >= 2, max_j P(Bin(m,1/2)=j) <= sqrt(2/(pi(m-1))). Proof: C(2r,r)/4^r <= 1/sqrt(pi r) for r >= 1 (standard). label: S0092
statement: Proof. (1) Write c = sum over free i with W_ji nonzero of W_ji x_i, and U = W_j restricted to F, lo = sum min(U_i, 0), hi = sum max(U_i, 0). The gate is non-constant iff t_j - hi <= c < t_j - lo, i.e. c lies in a set of L = hi - lo consecutive integers, with L <= sum over F of |W_ji| <= Bk. (2) Erdos (1945, Sperner): for reals a_i with |a_i| >= 1, any open interval of length 2 contains at most C(r, floor(r/2)) of the 2^r subset sums. Apply it to the open interval (s-1, s+1) with s an integer: Pr[c = s] <= C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r. (The earlier version used a window of length 2 with integer weights, which is false: a=(1,1), window (0.5,2.5). The point bound is correct.) (3) Union over the L integer values gives Pr[non-constant | F] <= L C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r. (4) C(r, floor(r/2))/2^r <= 1/sqrt(r) for all r >= 1 (standard central-binomial estimate). Hence the bound. QED. Exact checks: cm-11329b5046ac4967 (old window-2 version: 24 violations, refuted) and cm-0fc2b38402284a21 (point version: 0 violations in 300 instances, worst ratio 1.0).

structure.gap: Scope and limits. (a) This is a per-gate bound for a fixed F. It is not a running-time bound: a branching or enumeration algorithm still pays for every leaf, and the bound says nothing about how many leaves or distinct residual functions occur. (b) The bound is vacuous unless B k < sqrt(r). For poly-bounded weights (B = n^c) it only helps when k = o(n^{1/2 - c}), which leaves few free variables and does not reduce the 2^n count. (c) The G0007 obligation (a restriction that shrinks the whole circuit at a scale that gives 2^(1-delta) n) is still open. Repair needed: a leaf-count or residual-function bound that combines this per-gate estimate over all m gates, plus a treatment of large weights.
structure.lemma: Per-gate restriction lemma (repair of the R0948 step). Let W_j in Z^n with max |W_ji| <= B, threshold t_j in Z, and g_j(x) = [W_j.x >= t_j]. Fix a set F of k variables and draw the other variables uniformly. Let r = |supp(W_j) minus F| >= 1. Then Pr[g_j non-constant | F] <= (sum over i in F of |W_ji|) * C(r, floor(r/2)) / 2^r <= B k / sqrt(r).

label: S0098
statement: Degree-counting lemma (scope of the bounded-overlap route). Let C = top ∘ (g_1..g_m) with g_j = [W_j·x ≥ t_j], W_j in Z^n. After deleting constant gates (always-firing gates folded into T, never-firing gates dropped), m' remaining gates each have nonempty support N_j. With d_i = #{j : i in N_j}: sum_i d_i = sum_j |N_j| ≥ m'. Hence if every d_i ≤ c then m' ≤ c·n; for m' = n^α with α > 1 some variable lies in at least n^(α-1) gates.

Any repair for α > 1 must handle variable degree growing like n^(α-1), e.g. a pathwidth or DP argument with unbounded incidence degree. Open: whether a pathwidth bound of order (1-δ)n holds for such incidence graphs, and whether the DP state count stays below 2^((1-δ)n) for them. label: S0114
statement: LEMMA IS-COVER (bounded fan-in, bounded co-occurrence). SETTING: x in {0,1}^n; bottom gates g_j(x) = [w_j . x_{S_j} >= t_j] with integer w_j, t_j, |S_j| <= k; top gate [sum_j v_j g_j(x) >= T] with integer v_j, T. Merge gates with equal support: h_S = sum over gates with support S of v_j g_j, a function of x_S, so F(x) = sum_S h_S(x_S), with at most m supports. Co-occurrence graph G on [n]: u~v iff u,v lie in a common support S. Assume max degree Delta(G) = Delta. V := sum_S max|h_S| (polynomial if weights are polynomial). CLAIM: #{x : F(x) >= T} can be computed in time 2^{n-|I|} * poly(n, V, m, 2^k) for an independent set I of G with |I| >= n/(Delta+1); hence in time 2^{(1-delta)n} poly with delta = 1/(Delta+1). PROOF. (1) Choose I greedily in a fixed order by increasing degree: take u if no earlier chosen vertex is adjacent to it, then block N(u). Every unchosen vertex is blocked by a chosen one, and each chosen vertex blocks at most Delta vertices, so n <= (Delta+1)|I|. (2) Let C = [n] minus I. Fix x_C (2^{|C|} choices). Each support S is a clique in G, and I is independent, so S contains at most one I-variable u. Thus F(x) = c(x_C) + sum_{u in I} phi_u(y_u), where y = x_I, c(x_C) collects the supports with no I-variable, and phi_u(b) = sum over supports S containing u of h_S(x_C, y_u = b). The y_u are independent given x_C. (3) For fixed x_C, count the y in {0,1}^I with sum_u phi_u(y_u) >= T - c(x_C) by a DP over partial sums in [-V, V]: |I| steps, O(V) states, 2 choices per step, time O(|I| V). (4) Sum over the 2^{|C|} assignments x_C: total time 2^{n-|I|} * O(n V + m 2^k) per assignment. Since |I| >= n/(Delta+1), the exponent is at most (1 - 1/(Delta+1)) n. QED. SCOPE: fan-in <= k (constant), co-occurrence degree <= Delta (constant), any number m of bottom gates (m may be n^alpha), polynomial integer weights. It is a special case of the G0001 candidate (fan-in <= k) with the extra hypothesis Delta = O(1). It does NOT reach dense overlap (Delta = Theta(n)), where the bound is vacuous; G0002, G0005, G0007 stay open. CAVEATS: (a) the argument is the standard independent-set conditioning / bounded-degree counting, so a reviewer may judge it trivial, which would mean it does not count as progress under the owner's criterion; (b) it gives no new bound for general THR o THR; (c) it does not use S0010 or any other CLAIMED step. EVIDENCE: cm-b7e4eddda7d84b56 (300 random window instances, n in 6..12, k in {2,3}, 0 count mismatches vs brute force, 0 independent-set failures, 0 one-I-variable-per-support failures, 0 greedy-bound failures, max observed Delta 7, min |I|/(n/(Delta+1)) = 1.0).

label: S0121
statement:
LEMMA-RES-OVERLAP (CLAIMED): Let C be a THR o THR circuit with m = n^alpha bottom gates (alpha > 1), weights bounded by B = poly(n), and variable-gate incidence graph of maximum degree Delta (each variable participates in at most Delta bottom gates). Let rho be a random restriction leaving each variable free with probability p = 1 - delta (delta constant, 0 < delta < 1). Then with probability at least 1 - exp(-Omega(delta n / Delta)) over rho, at least (1 - exp(-Omega(delta))) fraction of bottom gates become constant (output fixed to 0 or 1).

Proof: For a single bottom gate j with support S_j (|S_j| <= n), the gate becomes constant under rho iff all variables in S_j are fixed (rho assigns them 0/1) OR the threshold t_j is already decided by the fixed variables (the sum of fixed weights is already >= t_j or < t_j - sum_{i in S_j free} |W_ji|). Since |S_j| <= Delta * (number of variables in support?) - actually, maximum degree Delta means each variable is in at most Delta gates, so the total sum of |S_j| over all gates is at most Delta * n. For a fixed gate j, the number of its inputs left free is Binomial(|S_j|, p). By Chernoff, Pr[|S_j free| > (1 + eps) p |S_j|] <= exp(-eps^2 p |S_j| / 3). If |S_j free| = 0, the gate is constant. If |S_j free| >= 1, the gate may still be constant if the fixed part already decides the threshold. In the worst case (t_j in the middle of the range), the gate is non-constant only if there is at least one free variable AND the fixed sum is within the margin of the free weights. But the union bound over all m gates: expected number of non-constant gates <= sum_j Pr[gate j non-constant]. For each gate, Pr[non-constant] <= Pr[|S_j free| >= 1] <= p |S_j|. Sum over j: p * sum_j |S_j| <= p * Delta * n. So at most p * Delta * n gates are non-constant in expectation. By Markov, Pr[non-constant gates > 2 p Delta n] <= 1/2. This is not the bound claimed. Need a stronger argument.

REPAIR: The lemma as stated is not yet proved. The correct statement is weaker: for Delta = O(1) (bounded overlap), a random restriction leaving p = 1 - delta variables free makes at least (1 - exp(-Omega(delta))) fraction of gates constant with high probability, provided the bottom gates have linear-size support. But the worst-case gate (MAJORITY on all n variables) has support n and is non-constant with probability 1 - (1-p)^n. For Delta = 1 (disjoint supports), the bound works. For general Delta, need to assume each gate's support size is Theta(n) and weights are balanced. This lemma needs a more careful proof; recording the gap.

structure.evidence: Analytic attempt; the proof has a gap in the union bound step. The correct scope is Delta = O(1) and bottom gates with Omega(n) support and balanced weights. Open: prove the constant-fraction bound for this subclass.

label: S0143
statement: LEMMA-TOPFANIN (bookkeeping, not progress under the owner criterion; CLAIMED, unreviewed): for a THR o THR function f(x) = [sum_j v_j [w_j . x >= t_j] >= T] with k bottom gates, integer weights |w_ji| <= B, n variables, the exact count #f is computed by a DP over the variables in index order whose state is the vector of residuals r_j = t_j - (partial sum of gate j) after fixing x_1..x_i. Gate j is decided-true iff r_j <= -B(n-i), decided-false iff r_j > B(n-i); otherwise r_j lies in (-B(n-i), B(n-i)], giving 2B(n-i) values. Per gate there are at most 2Bn+2 states (undecided values plus the two constant states), so the time is poly(n,k) * (2Bn+2)^k. This corrects the (Bn+1)^k bound in the earlier note. It is the r = k instance of the partial-sum DP of S0027, so it adds no new mechanism.

label: S0175
statement: LEMMA-RO (random-order frontier DP, Las Vegas). Setting: fixed integers c,k >= 1; D = c(k-1); THR o THR circuit f = [sum_j v_j g_j >= T] with bottom gates g_j = [sum_{i in S_j} w_{ji} x_i >= t_j], |S_j| <= k, each variable in at most c supports S_j, |v_j|, |w_{ji}| at most V(n) polynomial, any number m of gates. Let beta_D = (D/(D+1)) (D+1)^{-1/D} < 1. Claim: for every eps > 0 there is a Las Vegas algorithm computing #f exactly with expected time poly(n,m,V) 2^{(beta_D+eps) n}. Proof: (1) Fix an ordering pi of variables, pos(i) its position. Gate j completes at ct_j = max pos over S_j. K_t = {i : pos(i) <= t and some gate containing i completes after t}. A DP over x restricted to K_t plus the partial sum (range at most 2mV+1 values) is exact, because variables outside K_t are no longer read by any unfinished gate. State count at most 2^{|K_t|}(2mV+1). (2) i is in K_t iff pos(i) <= t and some u in N(i) has pos(u) > t, where N(i) is the union of S_j minus i over gates containing i; |N(i)| <= D. With s = |N(i)|+1 <= D+1 and tau = t/n: P(i in K_t) = P(pos(i) <= t) - P(all of {i} union N(i) in the prefix) <= tau - C(t,s)/C(n,s) <= tau - tau^{D+1} + O(D^2/n). Maximising over tau gives E|K_t| <= beta_D n + O(D^2). (3) A transposition of two positions changes the membership of at most 2(D+1) variables, so |K_t| is 2(D+1)-Lipschitz for transpositions. A Maurey/McDiarmid-type bound for uniform permutations gives deviation eps n with probability 1 - exp(-Omega(eps^2 n / D^2)); a union bound over t <= n gives, for large n, max_t |K_t| <= (beta_D+eps) n + O(D^2) with probability at least 1/2. (4) Algorithm: sample pi, compute max_t |K_t| exactly (poly time), accept if below the threshold, otherwise resample. Expected at most 2 trials; then run the DP. The output is exact; only the running time is random. Consequence: for fixed c,k, the subclass admits a counting algorithm with running time 2^{(beta_D+eps) n} poly(n,m,V), which is a strict 2^{(1-delta)n} saving with delta = 1 - beta_D - eps > 0 for any number of gates m, including m = n^alpha. The non-literal part has at most cn/2 gates by LEMMA-OVL.

structure.gap: Scope: fixed overlap c and fan-in k only. Novelty: random-order vertex separation plus standard frontier DP; probably known in folklore, to be checked.

State count at most 2^{|K_t|}(2mV+1). (2) i is in K_t iff pos(i) <= t and some u in N(i) has pos(u) > t, where N(i) is the union of S_j minus i over gates containing i; |N(i)| <= D. With s = |N(i)|+1 <= D+1 and tau = t/n: P(i in K_t) = P(pos(i) <= t) - P(all of {i} union N(i) in the prefix) <= tau - C(t,s)/C(n,s) <= tau - tau^{D+1} + O(D^2/n). Maximising over tau gives E|K_t| <= beta_D n + O(D^2). (3) A transposition of two positions changes the membership of at most 2(D+1) variables, so |K_t| is 2(D+1)-Lipschitz for transpositions. A Maurey/McDiarmid-type bound for uniform permutations gives deviation eps n with probability 1 - exp(-Omega(eps^2 n / D^2)); a union bound over t <= n gives, for large n, max_t |K_t| <= (beta_D+eps) n + O(D^2) with probability at least 1/2. (4) Algorithm: sample pi, compute max_t |K_t| exactly (poly time), accept if below the threshold, otherwise resample. Expected at most 2 trials; then run the DP. The output is exact; only the running time is random. Consequence: for fixed c,k, the subclass admits a counting algorithm with running time 2^{(beta_D+eps) n} poly(n,m,V), which is a strict 2^{(1-delta)n} saving with delta = 1 - beta_D - eps > 0 for any number of gates m, including m = n^alpha. The non-literal part has at most cn/2 gates by LEMMA-OVL.
