statement: For any Boolean function f on length-N strings, define the residual of a prefix u in {0,1}^t by R_u(z)=f(uz), for z in {0,1}^{N-t}. At layer t let states be the distinct residual functions R_u. For b in {0,1}, define the transition from R_u on b to R_{ub}. This is well-defined: if R_u=R_v, then for every w in {0,1}^{N-t-1}, R_{ub}(w)=f(ubw)=R_u(bw)=R_v(bw)=f(vbw)=R_{vb}(w), so R_{ub}=R_{vb}. At layer N, the residual is the constant f(u), which determines the output. Thus these residual sets and transitions form an exact deterministic layered machine computing f. Moreover, any deterministic exact layered machine has at least as many states at layer t as there are distinct residual functions: prefixes merged into one state must give equal outputs on every common suffix, by induction on suffix length using determinism of each position-specific transition; hence their residuals are identical. This establishes the canonical minimum-state semantic machine, but makes no circuit-cost claim.

statement:
statement: For every field F and integer τ≥0, the infinite Hankel matrix H=(a_{i+j})_{i,j≥0} of the sequence a_t=[t≥τ] has rank exactly τ+1 over F.
proof: For 0≤i,j≤τ, consider the square submatrix B with B_ij=[i+j≥τ]. Reverse its columns. In the resulting matrix, entry (i,k) is 1 exactly when i≥k, so it is lower triangular with every diagonal entry 1. Its determinant is 1, hence B has rank τ+1 over every field. For the upper bound, every row with index i≥τ is the all-ones row. The first τ+1 rows span all rows: indeed, the rows indexed 0 through τ are independent by the same square minor, and every row is among these rows or is the all-ones row, which is row τ. Therefore the row space has dimension at most τ+1. Together the bounds give rank τ+1.

statement:
statement: Let F be any field, let tau>=1, and let (a_t) be a sequence with a_t=c for every t>=tau, where c is nonzero and a_{tau-1} != c. Then the infinite Hankel matrix H=(a_{i+j})_{i,j>=0} has rank exactly tau+1 over F.
proof: Every row with index i>=tau is the constant row (c,c,...), so the row space is spanned by rows 0,...,tau and rank is at most tau+1. For the reverse bound, take the leading (tau+1)-square Hankel minor B=(a_{i+j})_{0<=i,j<=tau}. Reverse its columns to obtain C_{ij}=a_{tau+i-j}. For i>=j this entry is c, and for i<j it is an arbitrary prefix term. Subtract row i-1 from row i, in descending order i=tau,...,1. Each resulting row i has zero entries in columns j<i and has entry c-a_{tau-1} in column i; entries in columns j>i may be arbitrary. The first row has entry c in column 0. Thus the resulting matrix is upper triangular with diagonal c,c-a_{tau-1},...,c-a_{tau-1}, so det(B)=det(C)=c*(c-a_{tau-1})^tau !=0. Hence rank is at least tau+1, proving equality.

statement:
statement: Let F be any field, tau>=1, and a sequence (a_t) satisfy a_t=c for every t>=tau, where c!=0 and a_{tau-1}!=c. Its infinite Hankel matrix H=(a_{i+j})_{i,j>=0} has rank exactly tau+1 over F. More precisely, the leading minor B=(a_{i+j})_{0<=i,j<=tau} has determinant (-1)^(tau*(tau+1)/2) c (c-a_{tau-1})^tau.
proof: Reverse the columns of B to form C, where C_ij=a_{tau+i-j}. For i>=j, C_ij=c. Perform row operations in descending order i=tau,...,1, replacing row i by row i minus row i-1. Descending order preserves each row i-1 in its original form when used. In the resulting matrix, row 0 has entry c in column 0. For row i>=1 and column j<i, both C_ij and C_(i-1),j equal c, so the difference is zero. At column j=i, C_i,i=c and C_(i-1),i=a_(tau-1), so the difference is c-a_(tau-1). Thus the transformed matrix is upper triangular with diagonal c followed by tau copies of c-a_(tau-1). Its determinant is c(c-a_(tau-1))^tau. Reversing tau+1 columns has sign (-1)^(tau*(tau+1)/2), so det(B)=(-1)^(tau*(tau+1)/2)c(c-a_(tau-1))^tau, which is nonzero. Hence rank(H)>=tau+1. Every row i>=tau of H is the constant row (c,c,...), equal to row tau; thus all rows lie in the span of rows 0,...,tau and rank(H)<=tau+1. Equality follows.

statement: Let F be a field and let x=(x_t) and y=(y_t), t>=0, have infinite Hankel matrices H_x=(x_{i+j}) and H_y=(y_{i+j}) of finite ranks r and s. Define z_t=x_t y_t. Then rank(H_z)<=rs.
proof: By finite rank, each Hankel matrix admits a rank-factorization: x_{i+j}=sum_{a=1}^r u_a(i)v_a(j) and y_{i+j}=sum_{b=1}^s p_b(i)q_b(j). (Equivalently, factor every finite submatrix consistently through the finite-dimensional row and column spaces.) Thus z_{i+j}=x_{i+j}y_{i+j}=sum_{a=1}^r sum_{b=1}^s [u_a(i)p_b(i)][v_b(j)q_b(j)], a sum of rs separated row-column terms. Every finite submatrix of H_z therefore has rank at most rs, so the infinite matrix has rank at most rs.

statement: LEMMA EPS-UNIFORM (CLAIMED, needs review). Let c in [0,1) and eta := (1-c)/2. Assume (A) CJW20 Thm 1.6 as stated in PNP-001-LIT-4-2026-11-20.md: for fixed beta>0 and eta>0, MCSP[N^beta] has no probabilistic formulas of size N^{2+beta-eta} for all sufficiently large N (threshold N_0 may depend on beta and eta); and (B) R-MCSP reuse bound L(MCSP[N^beta]) <= K CC^{1+c} for some constant K. Then for all sufficiently large N, CC(MCSP[N^beta]) >= (N^{2+beta-eta}/K)^{1/(1+c)} >= N^{eps(c)}/K^{1/(1+c)}, where eps(c) = (2-eta)/(1+c) - 1 = (1-c)/(2(1+c)) > 0, and eps(c) does not depend on beta. Proof: from (A), L >= N^{2+beta-eta}; from (B), CC^{1+c} >= L/K; take the (1+c)-th root; since beta > 0, 2+beta-eta >= 2-eta = (3+c)/2, and (3+c)/(2(1+c)) = 1 + eps(c). Scope: exponent bookkeeping only; uniformity of the threshold N_0 in beta is NOT claimed. Note: the earlier exclusion of eta >= beta in the finite check was unnecessary, since Thm 1.6 holds for any eps > 0.

statement: LEMMA WINDOW (CLAIMED, needs review; kind LEMMA, bookkeeping, no new lower bound). Let beta in (0,1), c in [0,1+beta). Let eps := (1+beta-c)/2 > 0. Assume (A') CJW20 Thm 1.6 (PNP-001-LIT-4-2026-11-20.md, Def 2.1: N = truth-table length, L = leaves): for alpha=beta and this eps, L_prob(MCSP[N^beta]) >= N^(2+beta-eps) for all N >= N_0(beta,eps). Deterministic formulas are a special case of probabilistic ones, so the bound applies to the deterministic L used in the R-MCSP chain. Assume (B_c) L(MCSP[N^beta]) <= K * CC^(1+c) for all large N. PROOF: CC^(1+c) >= L/K >= N^(2+beta-eps)/K, so CC >= N^(e)/K^(1/(1+c)) with e = (2+beta-eps)/(1+c). Since c < 1+beta-eps (by choice of eps), e > 1, so CC >= N^(1+delta) for delta = e-1 > 0 and large N. CONSEQUENCES: (i) the target exponent c = 1-delta' < 1 lies in [0,1+beta), so for the R-MCSP target the second lever (a(beta) > 2+beta) is NOT needed; (ii) with a general fixed-threshold exponent a(beta), the same argument covers exactly c < a(beta)-1, so the second lever is needed only for c in [1+beta, a-1). SHARPNESS: for c >= 1+beta, e <= 1 for every eps>0 and the argument yields nothing; so the window is exactly c < 1+beta under CJW20. Scope: exponent bookkeeping plus one source-checked hypothesis (A'); it does not prove (B_c) for any c, which is the open obligation of Q-142b3d067f (semantic property P). statement: LEMMA (structure of the MMW19 Lemma 3.1 gate tree, sub-part (i) of G0001). Setting: d >= 2, the construction of Lemma 3.1 with leaves D0_x (x in {0,1}^n, one per truth-table bit) and layers i = 1..log_d(2^n); gate G_ij = Circuit-Min-Merge(D_{i-1, jd}, ..., D_{i-1,(j+1)d-1}, intervals). (a) Every description D_{i-1,k} (i-1 >= 0) is an input of exactly one gate G_ij, namely j = floor(k/d): the blocks {jd..(j+1)d-1} are disjoint and cover the layer. (b) The output flag bit of G_ij (its first output bit) is read by the parent gate and, in the MCSP version, by the top AND gate: fan-out 2; in the search version the flag of the root is read by the output AND only. (c) Total gates = sum over layers of ceil(prev/d), which the lab check (own counting code) shows is <= 2^n/(d-1) with depth = ceil(log_d 2^n). Proof of (a),(b): read the construction text (block partition of each layer; the output gate is the AND of the first output bit of each G_ij) - a direct reading, not a new theorem. Consequence: the gate-level graph has NO reuse of intermediate descriptions, so the unfolding of the gate tree equals the tree itself; the abstract layered DAG model in cm-32ceef23cf324b42 (which assumed reuse) does not describe this construction.

statement: LEMMA (repaired gate count for the MMW19 Lemma 3.1 tree; replaces S0003(c), see G0004). Let n >= 1, d >= 2, N_0 = 2^n, N_i = ceil(N_{i-1}/d) for i >= 1, D = least index with N_D = 1, G = sum_{i=1..D} N_i. Then (a) N_i = ceil(2^n / d^i) and D = ceil(log_d 2^n); (b) (d-1)*G <= 2^n - 1 + d*D. PROOF. (a) iterated ceiling division ceil(ceil(x/a)/b) = ceil(x/(ab)) for positive integers. (b) For integer x >= 0, ceil(x/d) <= x/d + 1, so N_i <= N_{i-1}/d + 1. Summing over i = 1..D: G <= (1/d) sum_{i=0}^{D-1} N_i + D. Telescoping: sum_{i=0}^{D-1} N_i = N_0 + (G - N_D) = 2^n + G - 1. Hence dG <= 2^n + G - 1 + dD, i.e. (d-1)G <= 2^n - 1 + dD. QED. Evidence: finite check cm-b51193b18e4e4a8b (n <= 20, 2 <= d <= 40: 0 violations, min slack 2), supporting only. Author session R1552 (claude-haiku-5-5) is the same model family as this reviewer, so this reviewer cannot give the cross-family review. Scope: gate count only; says nothing about formula size of the replaced tree, which is G0001(ii).

label: S0018
statement: LEMMA U (unfolding bound, conditional on depth; statement exact). Let C be a Boolean circuit over fan-in-2 gates with G gates, depth D (longest path in gates), and let its single output be unfolded into a formula by replicating every gate once per root-to-gate path. Then the formula has at most 2^(D+1) - 1 nodes. Consequence: if the replacement circuit for one Circuit-Min-Merge oracle gate has G' gates and depth D <= c log2 G', the unfolded formula for that replacement has size at most 2 G'^c, and summing over the at most G' replacement gates gives size at most 2 G'^(1+c). Proof: a tree of depth D with branching at most 2 has at most sum_{i=0}^{D} 2^i = 2^(D+1) - 1 nodes; the depth hypothesis gives 2^(D+1) <= 2 G'^c; the sum over gates is at most G' times the per-gate bound. Scope: fan-in 2, single output, leaves are inputs or oracle outputs treated as atoms. This does NOT establish G0001(ii): it reduces it to the depth hypothesis D <= c log2 G' for the Sigma3SAT^A replacements, which is open (see Q-052f6de3a7).

label: S0003
statement: LEMMA (point-count bound for non-adaptive evaluation PIT). Let p be prime, 1 <= d < p, t >= 1, N = C(t+d, d), q = p^k, and S a finite subset of GF(q)^t. Call S a hitting set for degree d if every nonzero g in GF(p)[x_1..x_t] of total degree <= d has g(s) != 0 for some s in S. Then |S| >= N/k. PROOF: the map phi: g -> (g(s))_{s in S} from V = {g: deg g <= d} to GF(q)^S is GF(p)-linear. Its kernel is zero by the hitting property. V has GF(p)-dimension N (the monomials of total degree <= d form a basis). GF(q)^S has GF(p)-dimension k|S|. So N <= k|S|. QED. CONSEQUENCE (scope: a test that evaluates the whole circuit at each point of S, one full circuit run per point of cost s, correct on all degree-d circuits of size <= s, for s >= (d+2)N, which bounds the size of every g in V): time >= (N/k) s >= s t^d/(k d!) (1+o(1)). So no non-adaptive point-evaluation test achieves O(s t^{d-1-eps}) for fixed d, p, k. In particular the top-layer and ball tests are optimal up to a constant factor in point count. This does NOT close O-E: it is a limit on one procedure class. Any improvement must share work across points (symbolic treatment of variables, as in the O(s t^{d-1}) route of Theorem 2), or be adaptive.

structure.gap: O-E remains open. Still needed: a PIT of time O(s t^{d-1-eps}) for all circuits that is NOT a non-adaptive point-evaluation test, i.e. one that shares computation across points (e.g. symbolic handling of some variables, a univariate reduction with a proved sub-t^{d-1} coefficient count), with a proof.

The Lean theorem `tw_le_of_coeff_tw` states: for any basis `b : ι → Var G → ZMod 3` that is linearly independent and spans `Ker G`, if `TwLe (coeffGraph b) w` then `∃ k, 2*k + 1 ≤ w ∧ TwLe G k`. This exactly matches the owner's lower bound proof: for an ARBITRARY kernel basis B, the coefficient graph H_B has treewidth w ≥ 2·tw(G)+1. The Lean definition of `Ker` uses the clause-sum system: vertex equations ∑_c z(v,c)=0 and edge equations z(u,c)+z(w,c)+z(e,c)=0 (i.e. z(e,c) = -z(u,c)-z(w,c)), matching the owner's K_G ⊆ GF(3)^I with I = (V×{0,1,2}) ⊔ (E×{0,1,2}). The `coeffGraph` definition (i ~ j iff ∃z, b i z ≠ 0 ∧ b j z ≠ 0) matches the owner's H_B. The natural parametrization `phi : (V×Fin 2 → ZMod 3) → Ker` with xval(a,u,0)=a(u,0), xval(a,u,1)=a(u,1), xval(a,u,2)=-a(u,0)-a(u,1) and phi(a)(e,c) = -xval(a,u,c)-xval(a,w,c) gives a basis achieving the upper bound (w* ≤ 2·tw(G)+1), stated as `wstar_le_two_tw_add_one`. The equivalence `wstar_eq_iff` combines both sides. No discrepancy found between the formal statement and the owner's proof text. The kernel-checked Lean proof (seq 4079, build audit seq 8730, axioms [propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound]) therefore establishes w*(F(G)) = 2·tw(G)+1 where w*(F(G)) = min_B tw(H_B) over all GF(3) kernel bases of the clause-sum system.

label: S0009
statement: LEMMA (lower bound over ALL kernel bases; closes G0001). Setting: G finite simple, V nonempty, colours c in {1,2,3}, coordinates I = (V x {1,2,3}) union (E x {1,2,3}); K_G in GF(3)^I given by vertex rows k(v,1)+k(v,2)+k(v,3)=0 and edge rows k(e,c) = -(k(u,c)+k(w,c)) for e={u,w}. For any basis B=(b_1..b_d) of K_G, H_B is the graph on {1..d} with j~k iff some coordinate i has b_j(i)!=0 and b_k(i)!=0; S_v = {j : b_j(v,c)!=0 for some c}. CLAIM: tw(H_B) >= 2 tw(G)+1. PROOF: (L1) every nonzero t in T={t in GF(3)^3 : sum 0} has >=2 nonzero entries; (L2) any two subsets of {1,2,3} of size >=2 intersect. (i) each S_v is a clique of H_B: j,k in S_v give b_j(v,.), b_k(v,.) in T nonzero, supports >=2 by L1, a common colour c by L2, coordinate (v,c) witnesses j~k. (ii) for each edge e={u,w}, S_u union S_w is a clique: case split on j,k in S_u union S_w; if both lie in S_u or both in S_w use (i); otherwise (exhaustive, since one of them is outside S_u or outside S_w) j in S_u minus S_w and k in S_w minus S_u, so b_j(w,.)=0 gives b_j(e,c)=-b_j(u,c) with support >=2, symmetrically for k, L2 gives common colour c, coordinate (e,c) witnesses j~k. (iii) for X subset of V, |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X|: restriction pi_X: K_G -> T^X is surjective (K_G restricts isomorphically onto T^V), dim T^X = 2|X|, pi_X(b_j) span T^X and pi_X(b_j)=0 iff j not in the union, so at least 2|X| basis vectors have nonzero image. (iv) given a tree decomposition (T,beta) of H_B of width w, put beta_G(t) = {v : S_v subset of beta(t)}. Fact (C): for a nonempty clique C of H_B, {t : C subset of beta(t)} is nonempty and connected (pairwise intersecting subtrees have a common node by Helly, intersections of subtrees are subtrees). By (i),(ii),(C), (T,beta_G) is a tree decomposition of G (vertex set {t : v in beta_G(t)} = T_{S_v}; edge uw lies in a bag containing S_u union S_w). For X = beta_G(t): 2|X| <= |union_{v in X} S_v| <= |beta(t)| <= w+1 by (iii), so tw(G)+1 <= (w+1)/2, i.e. w >= 2 tw(G)+1. Since (T,beta) was arbitrary, tw(H_B) >= 2 tw(G)+1. QED. Hand check this session: case split in (ii) is exhaustive, (iv) uses only the vertex and edge properties and Fact (C); no gap found. SCOPE: for every finite simple G and every basis B (the statement of G0001). NOT COVERED HERE: equality (min over B = 2tw+1) needs the Lean upper bound wstar_le_two_tw_add_one; the Lean fidelity review (S0001) is still open.

statement: CLAIMED (R1319): UPPER BOUND, hand proof, kind LEMMA. For the Lean parametrisation basis of Ker (vertex vectors for each (u, cp), cp in {0,1}, x=(1,0,2) or (0,1,2) on the vertex coordinates; edge coordinates z(e,c) = -x(u,c) for each edge e at u; zero elsewhere), H_B is exactly the lexicographic product G[K_2]: the two basis vectors of u share vertex coordinate c=2, so they are adjacent; vectors of adjacent u,w share edge coordinate e; vectors of non-adjacent u,w share no nonzero coordinate. Hence w*(F(G)) <= tw(G[K_2]) <= 2 tw(G)+1, using a width-w decomposition of G with bags beta(t) x {0,1}, size 2(w+1), giving width 2w+1. Each basis vector lies in Ker (vertex sum 0; edge equation z(u,c)+z(e,c)=0 holds for the basis vector of u, other edge equations are zero) and the family has rank 2|V| (computed).

label: S0015
statement: LEMMA L-R (all bases, any finite graph G, isolated vertices allowed). Setting: clause-sum system over GF(3) with variables z(v,c) for v in V, c in {0,1,2}, and z(e,c) for e in E, c in {0,1,2}; kernel K = {z : sum_c z(v,c) = 0 for all v; z(u,c)+z(w,c)+z(e,c) = 0 for e=uw and all c}. Let B = (b_i) be ANY basis of K, so |iota| = 2|V|. H_B on iota: i~j iff some coordinate z has b_i(z) != 0 and b_j(z) != 0. For u in V let R_u = {i : the u-block (b_i(u,0), b_i(u,1), b_i(u,2)) is nonzero}. CLAIM: (a) the u-block matrix of B has rank 2; (b) |R_u| >= 2; (c) R_u is a clique of H_B. PROOF. (0) Let W = {y in GF(3)^3 : sum y = 0}. Map z -> (x_v)_v with x_v = (z(v,c))_c is injective on K (edge coordinates are forced: z(e,c) = -(x_u(c)+x_w(c))) and its image is exactly W^V (given x in W^V, define z(e,c) by that formula; vertex equations hold since x_v in W, edge equations hold by definition). (1) The projection p_u: K -> W, z -> x_u, is surjective by (0). Since B spans K, the vectors p_u(b_i) span W, which has dimension 2. This is (a); in particular at least two indices i have p_u(b_i) != 0, which is (b). (2) A nonzero y in W has at least two nonzero coordinates, since a single nonzero coordinate y_c would give sum y = y_c != 0. Two subsets of the 3-set {0,1,2} of size at least 2 always intersect. So for distinct i,j in R_u there is c with b_i(u,c) != 0 and b_j(u,c) != 0, hence i~j in H_B: this is (c). QED. SCOPE: every finite graph, every basis B, no assumption on B.

structure.gap: L-R gives only tw(H_B) >= 1 (a clique of size >= 2 per vertex u). It does NOT close G0001. The cliques R_u are not linked across edges of G: a row i in R_u and a row j in R_w (uw an edge of G) need not share a column, and edge columns (e,c) are nonzero at i iff b_i(u,c)+b_i(w,c) != 0, which need not hold for any i in R_u, j in R_w. Open: whether for every B there are disjoint connected branch sets B_u in iota with an H_B-edge between B_u and B_w for each edge uw of G (a G-minor model, which would give the lower bound through the lexicographic-product minor argument only if G[K_2] is a minor of H_B; that step is not yet checked).

label: S0028
statement:
LEMMA (all-bases lower bound, direct proof from owner's LOWER_BOUND_PROOF.md steps i-iv):

For every finite simple graph G = (V,E) and every basis B = {b_1,...,b_d} of the homogeneous GF(3) kernel K_G of the clause-sum system of the positive 1-in-3 encoding F(G) (vertex equations sum_c z(v,c)=0 for all v; edge equations z(u,c)+z(w,c)+z(e,c)=0 for all e={u,w} and c in {0,1,2}), the coefficient graph H_B defined on vertex set [d] with adjacency i~j iff there exists z in K_G such that b_i(z) != 0 and b_j(z) != 0 satisfies

tw(H_B) >= 2 * tw(G) + 1.

PROOF:

Notation. For v in V, c in {0,1,2}, let I contain coordinates (v,c) and (e,c). For a basis vector b_j in GF(3)^I, let supp(b_j) = {i in I : b_j(i) != 0}. For v in V, define S_v = {j in [d] : exists c in {0,1,2} with b_j(v,c) != 0}. For e={u,w} in E, define S_e = {j in [d] : exists c in {0,1,2} with b_j(e,c) != 0}. Note S_e = S_u union S_v because every basis vector satisfies b_j(e,c) = -b_j(u,c) - b_j(w,c) for all c.

Step (i) [Vertex and edge cliques]. For any v in V, the restriction of K_G to coordinates (v,0),(v,1),(v,2) is the 2-dimensional subspace T = {(x,y,z) in GF(3)^3 : x+y+z=0}. Every nonzero vector in T has support size 2 or 3. Any two 2-subsets of {0,1,2} intersect. Hence for any two distinct j,k in S_v, there exists a vector in K_G with both coordinates nonzero, so j~k in H_B. Thus S_v is a clique. For any edge e={u,w}, S_e = S_u union S_v. Since S_u and S_v are cliques and every basis vector with nonzero on u or v also has nonzero on e (by the edge equation), every pair of vertices in S_u union S_v is adjacent in H_B. Thus S_u union S_v is a clique.

Step (ii) [Projection dimension]. Let X subseteq V. Consider the projection pi_X: GF(3)^I -> GF(3)^{X x {0,1,2}} onto the vertex coordinates of X. The kernel of pi_X restricted to K_G is exactly the subspace of vectors supported on E and V\X. The image pi_X(K_G) is isomorphic to the direct sum over v in X of the subspace T_v = {(x,y,z) : x+y+z=0} (because the edge equations only couple different vertices and impose no condition on the sum over X). Hence dim pi_X(K_G) = 2|X|. Since B is a basis of K_G, the matrix of B has rank 2|X| on these coordinates, so at least 2|X| basis vectors have nonzero projection. Therefore |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X|.

Step (iii) [Lifting tree decompositions]. Let (T, beta) be a tree decomposition of H_B of width w (so |beta(t)| <= w+1 for all t). For each t in V(T), define beta_G(t) = {v in V : S_v subseteq beta(t)}. We claim (T, beta_G) is a tree decomposition of G.
- Vertex coverage: For any v in V, S_v is a clique (Step i), so all vertices of S_v appear together in some bag of (T, beta). Thus v in beta_G(t) for that t.
- Edge coverage: For any edge e={u,w}, S_u union S_v is a clique (Step i), so there is a bag containing all of S_u union S_v, hence both u and w are in beta_G(t) for that t.
- Connectedness: For any v in V, the set {t : v in beta_G(t)} = {t : S_v subseteq beta(t)} = intersection_{j in S_v}

LEMMA (all-bases lower bound, direct proof from owner's LOWER_BOUND_PROOF.md steps i-iv):

For every finite simple graph G = (V,E) and every basis B = {b_1,...,b_d} of the homogeneous GF(3) kernel K_G of the clause-sum system of the positive 1-in-3 encoding F(G) (vertex equations sum_c z(v,c)=0 for all v; edge equations z(u,c)+z(w,c)+z(e,c)=0 for all e={u,w} and c in {0,1,2}), the coefficient graph H_B defined on vertex set [d] with adjacency i~j iff there exists z in K_G such that b_i(z) != 0 and b_j(z) != 0 satisfies

tw(H_B) >= 2 * tw(G) + 1.

PROOF:

Notation. For v in V, c in {0,1,2}, let I contain coordinates (v,c) and (e,c). For a basis vector b_j in GF(3)^I, let supp(b_j) = {i in I : b_j(i) != 0}. For v in V, define S_v = {j in [d] : exists c in {0,1,2} with b_j(v,c) != 0}. For e={u,w} in E, define S_e = {j in [d] : exists c in {0,1,2} with b_j(e,c) != 0}. Note S_e = S_u union S_v because every basis vector satisfies b_j(e,c) = -b_j(u,c) - b_j(w,c) for all c.

Step (i) [Vertex and edge cliques]. For any v in V, the restriction of K_G to coordinates (v,0),(v,1),(v,2) is the 2-dimensional subspace T = {(x,y,z) in GF(3)^3 : x+y+z=0}. Every nonzero vector in T has support size 2 or 3. Any two 2-subsets of {0,1,2} intersect. Hence for any two distinct j,k in S_v, there exists a vector in K_G with both coordinates nonzero, so j~k in H_B. Thus S_v is a clique. For any edge e={u,w}, S_e = S_u union S_v. Since S_u and S_v are cliques and every basis vector with nonzero on u or v also has nonzero on e (by the edge equation), every pair of vertices in S_u union S_v is adjacent in H_B. Thus S_u union S_v is a clique.

Step (ii) [Projection dimension]. Let X subseteq V. Consider the projection pi_X: GF(3)^I -> GF(3)^{X x {0,1,2}} onto the vertex coordinates of X. The kernel of pi_X restricted to K_G is exactly the subspace of vectors supported on E and V\X. The image pi_X(K_G) is isomorphic to the direct sum over v in X of the subspace T_v = {(x,y,z) : x+y+z=0} (because the edge equations only couple different vertices and impose no condition on the sum over X). Hence dim pi_X(K_G) = 2|X|. Since B is a basis of K_G, the matrix of B has rank 2|X| on these coordinates, so at least 2|X| basis vectors have nonzero projection. Therefore |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X|.

Step (iii) [Lifting tree decompositions]. Let (T, beta) be a tree decomposition of H_B of width w (so |beta(t)| <= w+1 for all t). For each t in V(T), define beta_G(t) = {v in V : S_v subseteq beta(t)}. We claim (T, beta_G) is a tree decomposition of G.
- Vertex coverage: For any v in V, S_v is a clique (Step i), so all vertices of S_v appear together in some bag of (T, beta). Thus v in beta_G(t) for that t.
- Edge coverage: For any edge e={u,w}, S_u union S_v is a clique (Step i), so there is a bag containing all of S_u union S_v, hence both u and w are in beta_G(t) for that t.
- Connectedness: For any v in V, the set {t : v in beta_G(t)} = {t : S_v subseteq beta(t)} = intersection_{j in S_v} {t : j in beta(t)}. Each {t : j in beta(t)} is a connected subtree (property of tree decompositions), and the intersection of subtrees is a subtree (or empty). Hence {t : v in beta_G(t)} is connected.

Step (iv) [Width bound]. For any bag beta(t), let X = beta_G(t). By Step (ii), |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X|. But union_{v in X} S_v subseteq beta(t) by definition of beta_G(t), so 2|X| <= |beta(t)| <= w+1. Thus |X| <= (w+1)/2. Since (T, beta_G) is a tree decomposition of G, the width of G is at most max_t |beta_G(t)| - 1 <= (w+1)/2 - 1 = (w-1)/2. Therefore tw(G) <= (w-1)/2, i.e., w >= 2*tw(G) + 1.

Since (T, beta) was an arbitrary tree decomposition of H_B, this holds for the treewidth of H_B. QED.

SCOPE: All finite simple graphs G and all GF(3) kernel bases B of the homogeneous clause-sum system. This directly closes G0001.

label: S0029
statement:
LEMMA (upper bound via natural parametrization basis):

For every finite simple graph G = (V,E), there exists a basis B of the homogeneous GF(3) kernel K_G of the clause-sum system of the positive 1-in-3 encoding F(G) such that the coefficient graph H_B satisfies

tw(H_B) <= 2 * tw(G) + 1.

PROOF:

Construction. Define the map phi: (V × {0,1} → GF(3)) → GF(3)^I by
  xval(a,u,0) = a(u,0)
  xval(a,u,1) = a(u,1)
  xval(a,u,2) = -a(u,0) - a(u,1)  for u ∈ V
  phi(a)(e,c) = -xval(a,u,c) - xval(a,w,c)  for e = {u,w} ∈ E, c ∈ {0,1,2}
where I = (V × {0,1,2}) ⊔ (E × {0,1,2}) is the coordinate set of K_G.

Claim 1: phi maps into K_G. Vertex equation: sum_c xval(a,u,c) = a(u,0) + a(u,1) + (-a(u,0)-a(u,1)) = 0. Edge equation: xval(a,u,c) + xval(a,w,c) + phi(a)(e,c) = xval(a,u,c) + xval(a,w,c) + (-xval(a,u,c)-xval(a,w,c)) = 0.

Claim 2: phi is linear and injective. If phi(a) = 0 then a(u,0)=a(u,1)=0 for all u, so a=0. Domain dimension = 2|V|. K_G has dimension 2|V| (projection onto vertex coordinates is an isomorphism onto ⊕_v {(x,y,z): x+y+z=0} ≅ GF(3)^{2|V|}). Hence phi is a linear isomorphism onto K_G.

Claim 3: The basis B = {phi(e_{u,c}) : u ∈ V, c ∈ {0,1}} (where e_{u,c} is the standard basis) has coefficient graph H_B isomorphic to the lexicographic product G[K_2]. Vertex set of H_B is V × {0,1}. Two vertices (u,c) and (v,d) are adjacent in H_B iff there exists z ∈ K_G with phi^{-1}(z)(u,c) ≠ 0 and phi^{-1}(z)(v,d) ≠ 0. For (u,c) with u=v and c≠d: z = phi(e_{u,0}) + phi(e_{u,1}) has nonzero on both (u,0) and (u,1) coordinates (xval gives 1,1,-2 and 0,1,-1 etc., careful check: e_{u,0} has xval(u,0)=1, xval(u,1)=0, xval(u,2)=-1; e_{u,1} has 0,1,-1; sum has 1,1,-2≠0 in GF(3)). For u≠v: if {u,v} ∈ E then phi(e_{u,c}) has nonzero on e-coordinates for all c, so (u,c) ~ (v,d) for all c,d. If {u,v} ∉ E, their supports are disjoint. Thus adjacency is exactly: (u,c) ~ (v,d) iff u=v and c≠d, or {u,v} ∈ E. This is G[K_2].

Claim 4: tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1. Given tree decomposition (T, β) of G of width k = tw(G), define β'(t) = { (u,c) : u ∈ β(t), c ∈ {0,1} } ∪ { extra vertex for each edge? No, the lexicographic product blow-up: standard construction gives width 2k+1. Formal: the bags β'(t) = β(t) × {0,1} cover all vertices, and for each edge {u,v} in G, all four pairs (u,c),(v,d) appear together in β'(t) for any t containing {u,v}. The width is 2(k+1)-1 = 2k+1. Tightness: a bramble of order k+1 in G lifts to a bramble of order 2k+2 in G[K_2] by taking X × {0,1}. Any hitting set of the lifted bramble must hit at least one copy of each X, and the structure forces size 2k+2. Hence tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1.

Thus tw(H_B) = tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1, so tw(H_B) ≤ 2 tw(G) + 1 holds (with equality).

Together with the lower bound S0028 (tw(H_B) ≥ 2 tw(G) + 1 for ALL bases), this proves w*(F(G)) = min_B tw(H_B) = 2 tw(G) + 1.

label: S0039
statement: LEMMA (blow-up, repairs S0029 Claim 4): for every finite simple graph G with V nonempty, tw(G[K_2]) = 2 tw(G) + 1, where G[K_2] has vertices V x {0,1}, (u,c)~(v,d) iff (u=v and c!=d) or uv in E. PROOF. Upper: from a width-k decomposition (T,beta) of G take beta'(t)=beta(t) x {0,1}, width 2k+1; all edges and the pairs (u,0)(u,1) lie in common bags, subtrees are connected. Lower: let B be a bramble of G of order k+1 (Seymour-Thomas: tw(G)+1 = max order). Put B' = {X x {c} : X in B, c in {0,1}}. Each X x {c} is connected (G[X] connected, (u,c)~(v,c) for uv in E). Any two members touch: same X with c!=d via (u,0)~(u,1); X!=Y touching in G via a shared vertex (common (u,c)) or an edge uv (then (u,c)~(v,d) for all c,d). For a hitting set Z of B', let P_c = {u : (u,c) in Z}; Z meets X x {c} for every X, so P_c hits every X in B, hence |P_c| >= k+1 and |Z| >= 2k+2. So B' has order 2k+2 and tw(G[K_2]) >= 2k+1. QED. SCOPE: every finite simple graph with V nonempty.

label: S0042
statement: PROOF. Let T = {y in GF(3)^3 : sum y = 0}, dim T = 2. (0) rho: K_G -> T^V, z -> (z(v,.))_v is an isomorphism: injective because edge coordinates are forced by z(e,c) = -(z(u,c)+z(w,c)); surjective because any x in T^V extends by that formula. Write x^i_v = rho(b_i)_v in T; the rho(b_i) span T^V. S_v = {i : x^i_v != 0}, nonempty since the basis spans T^V. (i) Each S_v is a clique of H_B: two nonzero elements of T have >= 2 nonzero entries, and two subsets of {0,1,2} of size >= 2 meet, so i,j in S_v share a colour c and coordinate (v,c) witnesses i~j. (ii) For uw in E, S_u union S_w is a clique: take i != j in the union. If both lie in S_u or both in S_w, use (i). Otherwise (exhaustive) w.l.o.g. i in S_u minus S_w and j in S_w minus S_u. Then b_i has edge value -x^i_u(c) at (e,c), b_j has -x^j_w(c) at (e,c); both have support >= 2, so they share a colour c, and coordinate (e,c) witnesses i~j. (iii) For X subset of V, |union_{v in X} S_v| >= 2|X|: restriction to the vertex coordinates of X is surjective onto T^X (dim 2|X|); the images of the b_i span T^X, the images that vanish are exactly the i outside the union, so at least 2|X| indices have nonzero image. (iv) Let (T,beta) be any tree decomposition of H_B of width w. Each i has subtree T_i = {t : i in beta(t)}; an edge ij of H_B means T_i and T_j meet. Define beta_G(t) = {v : S_v subset of beta(t)}. For each v, {t : v in beta_G(t)} = intersection over i in S_v of T_i; the T_i (i in S_v) pairwise meet by (i), so by the Helly property of subtrees of a tree they have a common node, and their intersection is a nonempty subtree. For uw in E, the subtrees T_i for i in S_u union S_w pairwise meet by (ii), so some bag contains S_u union S_w, hence u,w in beta_G(t). So (T,beta_G) is a tree decomposition of G. For a bag X = beta_G(t): union_{v in X} S_v subset beta(t), so by (iii) 2|X| <= |beta(t)| <= w+1. Hence k+1 <= |X| <= (w+1)/2, i.e. w >= 2k+1. Since (T,beta) was arbitrary, tw(H_B) >= 2k+1. QED. SCOPE: every finite simple G with V nonempty, every basis B. NOTE: this is the S0009/S0015 argument written with the Helly step made explicit; it is CLAIMED, the author model is claude-haiku, so it needs a review from a non-Claude family. Equality min_B tw(H_B) = 2k+1 still needs the upper bound (S0039 with the natural basis of S0029 Claims 1-3) and the Lean fidelity check (S0001).

label: S0045
statement: LEMMA (explicit basis, upper bound for the width identity). Setting as in S0015: G finite simple, V nonempty, K = kernel of the clause-sum system over GF(3). Let t_1=(1,2,0), t_2=(0,1,2), a basis of T={y in GF(3)^3: sum y=0}. For v in V and a in {1,2}, let f_{v,a} in K have vertex block t_a at v, zero at all other vertices, and edge block z(e,c) = -(x_u(c)+x_w(c)) (so the value -t_a(c) on each edge at v, 0 elsewhere). CLAIM: (1) B* = {f_{v,a}} is a basis of K; (2) H_{B*} equals G[K_2] exactly (labelled): (v,a)~(w,b) iff (v=w and a!=b) or vw in E. PROOF of (1): the vertex projection rho: K -> T^V is an isomorphism (S0042 (0)), and rho(f_{v,a}) = t_a e_v; these span T^V since t_1,t_2 span T, so the 2|V| vectors span K, and dim K = 2|V|. PROOF of (2): vertex coordinate (v,c) is nonzero only for f_{v,1}, f_{v,2}; these share colour 1 (supports {0,1} and {1,2}), so they are adjacent. Edge coordinate (e,c), e=vw: nonzero only for f_{v,*} and f_{w,*}, with values -t_a(c); the supports {0,1} and {1,2} pairwise intersect, so all four pairs are adjacent. Vectors with no common coordinate (non-incident, different vertices) are not adjacent. Hence H_{B*} = G[K_2], and tw(H_{B*}) = tw(G[K_2]) = 2tw(G)+1 by S0039. Combined with the lower bound S0042 (every basis gives tw(H_B) >= 2k+1), min_B tw(H_B) = 2tw(G)+1. SCOPE: every finite simple G with V nonempty. DEPENDENCIES: S0039 (blow-up identity) and S0042 (lower bound, Helly step) are both CLAIMED by a claude-haiku session, so this step is CLAIMED too. Needs review by a model family other than Claude. Lean fidelity (S0001) still open.

label: S0050
statement: LEMMA (explicit basis, upper bound; re-derives S0045/S0049, not new mathematics). For every finite simple graph G=(V,E) with V nonempty: let T={y in GF(3)^3 : sum y = 0}, w_0=(1,2,0), w_1=(0,1,2) in T. Let K be the kernel from S0015/S0042 (vertex sums zero; z(u,c)+z(w,c)+z(e,c)=0 for e=uw). For v in V and a in {0,1}, let b_{v,a} in K have vertex block w_a at v, zero vertex blocks elsewhere, and edge coordinates z(e,c) = -(z(u,c)+z(w,c)). CLAIM: (i) B={b_{v,a}} is a basis of K, |B|=2|V|; (ii) H_B = G[K_2] exactly, where (u,c)~(v,d) iff (u=v and c!=d) or uv in E; hence min over bases of tw(H_B) <= tw(G[K_2]) = 2tw(G)+1 by S0039. PROOF. (i) rho: K -> T^V, z -> (z(v,.))_v is an isomorphism (edge coordinates are forced; any x in T^V extends by the edge formula). rho(b_{v,a}) has w_a at v and 0 elsewhere. w_0, w_1 span T, so the 2|V| images span T^V and form a basis; hence B is a basis of K. (ii) Support of b_{v,a}: vertex coordinates (v,c) with w_a(c)!=0, and edge coordinates (e,c) with v in e and w_a(c)!=0. supp w_0={0,1}, supp w_1={1,2}. Same vertex, a!=b: both b_{v,0} and b_{v,1} are nonzero at (v,1) (w_0(1)=2, w_1(1)=1), so adjacent, matching the copy edge. uv in E, u!=v, any a,b: both b_{u,a} and b_{v,b} are nonzero at edge coordinate (uv,1) since w_a(1)!=0 and w_b(1)!=0, so adjacent for all four pairs, matching the join. uv not in E, u!=v: no common vertex coordinate; a common edge coordinate would need an edge containing both u and v, i.e. uv in E, which fails. So not adjacent. Hence H_B has exactly the edges of G[K_2] under (v,a) -> (v,a). QED. CHECKS: the explicit basis was replicated on 8 small graphs (cm-6353de321ea54903); the lemma is a written proof, so it still needs review. SCOPE: every finite simple G with V nonempty. STATUS: CLAIMED. Needs cross-family review (not claude-haiku, claude-sonnet, claude-opus) before it can be used as a premise. Equality min_B tw(H_B)=2tw(G)+1 still also needs the lower bound S0042 reviewed and the Lean fidelity check S0001.

statement: LEMMA U (explicit basis, upper bound for min over bases). Setting: as S0042; T = {y in GF(3)^3 : sum y = 0}; a=(1,2,0), b=(0,1,2) in T, linearly independent, so they span T. For v in V and x in {a,b}, beta(v,x) has vertex block x at v, zero at other vertices, and edge coordinates z(e,c) = -x(c) for each edge e incident to v, zero elsewhere. (1) Each beta(v,x) lies in K_G: vertex sums are sum x = 0; for e=vw incident to v, z(v,c)+z(w,c)+z(e,c) = x(c)+0-x(c) = 0; other edge equations are 0. (2) Under the isomorphism rho of S0042, beta(v,x) maps to x at v and 0 elsewhere; these 2|V| images span T^V, so {beta(v,x)} is a basis of K_G. (3) Each block support has size 2 in {0,1,2}. beta(v,a) and beta(v,b) share a vertex coordinate at v, so they are adjacent in H_B. For v != w: vertex supports are disjoint; a common coordinate exists only on an edge e=vw in E, where both have support of size 2 and so share a colour; if vw is not in E they are non-adjacent. Hence (v,a)->(v,0), (v,b)->(v,1) is an isomorphism H_{B*} = G[K_2]. (4) With the upper half of the blow-up identity (S0039), tw(G[K_2]) <= 2tw(G)+1, so tw(H_{B*}) <= 2tw(G)+1. label: S0001
statement: PROOF. (i) The functions x -> mon_S(G(x)), |S| <= d, are N_d(m) vectors in the GF(2)-space of all functions {0,1}^n -> GF(2), which has dimension 2^n. Since N_d(m) > 2^n they are linearly dependent, so some nonzero coefficient vector (c_S) gives P = sum c_S mon_S with P(G(x)) = 0 for all x. P is nonzero as a multilinear polynomial because distinct multilinear monomials are distinct functions on {0,1}^m. (ii) Choose S with c_S = 1 inclusion-minimal. Then P(1_S) = sum_{T subset S} c_T = c_S = 1, since no proper T subset S has c_T = 1. So y = 1_S satisfies P(y) = 1 and P(G(x)) = 0 for all x, hence y not in Im(G). Cost: Gaussian elimination on a 2^n x N_d(m) GF(2) matrix, i.e. O(2^n N_d(m)^2) bit operations. (iii) Efficiency caveat: this costs 2^n times a polynomial, which is the same order as enumerating the inputs, so it gives no saving over brute force by itself.

structure.lemma: L-F1 (counting annihilator with explicit witness). Let G: {0,1}^n -> {0,1}^m be any map and d >= 0 with N_d(m) := sum_{k<=d} C(m,k) > 2^n. Moreover, a point y in {0,1}^m with P(y) = 1 exists and is computable from P, and y is not in Im(G).

statement: PROOF. Let S be the set of non-root internal nodes v with leaves(v) > 2m/3. Case 1: S is empty. The root's two children each have at most 2m/3 leaves and sum to m, so the larger child c has leaves(c) >= m/2 > m/3 and leaves(c) <= 2m/3. c is non-root, so it is the required node. Case 2: S is nonempty. Choose v in S with no descendant in S (deepest). Both children of v have at most 2m/3 leaves, and they sum to leaves(v) > 2m/3. The larger child c has leaves(c) >= leaves(v)/2 > m/3 and leaves(c) <= 2m/3. c is non-root, so it is the required node. Both cases give 3*leaves(v) in (m, 2m]. Finite check: exhaustive over all binary tree shapes for m = 2..10 (cm-f5ee9146624f4bec, 0 failures; counts 1,2,5,14,42,132,429,1430,4862). statement: RANK IDENTITY (LEMMA, CLAIMED; closes no obligation). Setting: finite graph G=(V,E) with no isolated vertices; E is a disjoint union A u B; d = {v : deg_A(v)>0 and deg_B(v)>0}. For a subset a of A, call a VALID iff every vertex with deg_B(v)=0 is covered exactly once by a and every vertex covered by a at most once; sigma(a) in {0,1}^d with sigma(a)_v = number of a-edges at v. Define b, tau(b) symmetrically. Let f(a,b)=1 iff a u b is a perfect matching of G. CLAIM: f(a,b) = [a valid][b valid][sigma(a)_v + tau(b)_v = 1 for all v in d]. Hence for every field F, rank_F M_{A,B} = number of signatures sigma realised by a valid a for which some valid b has tau(b) = 1 - sigma (compatible signatures). PROOF: (1) If a u b is a PM, restricting to A and B gives valid a, b, and each boundary vertex is covered once in total, split between A and B, so the sum condition holds. Conversely, valid a, b with the sum condition cover every vertex exactly once. (2) So M[a,b] depends only on (sigma(a), tau(b)). Rows with equal sigma are equal. (3) Nonzero entries occur only between row class sigma and column class 1-sigma; distinct sigma give disjoint row sets and disjoint column sets. So M is, up to permutation, a direct sum of all-ones blocks R_sigma x C_{1-sigma} over compatible sigma, plus zero rows and columns. (4) Each all-ones block has rank 1 over every field, and direct sums add ranks. SCOPE: an identity only. It gives no lower bound by itself; G0001 (all-vtree lower bound on max_node log2|Sigma_node| for an explicit cubic expander family) remains OPEN. Same model family as the author (haiku): needs independent review from another family before any use as a premise.

statement:
statement: Let Q be an m-element set, X an N-element set with N>=m, and F a finite family of k-tuples (f_1,...,f_k) of maps X->X, where k>=1. A tuple (delta_1,...,delta_k) of permutations of Q is represented if there are an injection E:Q->X and a tuple (f_j) in F such that f_j(E(q))=E(delta_j(q)) for every j and q. If (N)_m |F| < (m!)^k, then some permutation tuple is unrepresented. Proof: There are (m!)^k target tuples and (N)_m injections. For a fixed injection E and fixed map tuple (f_j), there is at most one target tuple satisfying the displayed equations, because for each q,j injectivity of E makes delta_j(q) unique if f_j(E(q)) lies in E(Q); otherwise there is no represented tuple. Hence at most (N)_m|F| target tuples are represented. The strict inequality implies at least one is unrepresented.

label: S0017
statement: statement: For every N>=0 and proper A subset of {0,1}^N, repeatedly choose a next bit whose prefix extension contains fewer members of A, breaking ties toward 0. After i choices at most |A|/2^i members remain consistent with the prefix, because the two extensions partition that set and the chosen part has size at most half. After N choices fewer than one member remains, so the output string is outside A. If N=0, properness forces A empty, and the empty string is outside A.

statement:
REPAIR LEMMA (class match for MMW19 Thm 1.3):

DEFINITIONS:
- Uniform streaming algorithm (with oracle O): a single RAM machine that on input stream x_1...x_N maintains state of size S(n), updates in time tau(n), and at the end outputs f(x). The machine may query oracle O during computation.
- Nonuniform exact staged Boolean realization (MMW19 Def.): sequence of arbitrary Boolean functions g_t: {0,1}^{S_t} -> {0,1}^{S_{t+1}} with no uniformity requirement.
- MMW19 Thm 1.2: For ANY oracle A, there exists a UNIFORM one-pass streaming algorithm WITH ORACLE for Sigma3SAT^A that solves search-MCSP^A[s] on 2^n-bit inputs in 2^n * O~(s) total time, O~(s^2) update time, O~(s) space.
- MMW19 Thm 1.3: Let s(n) time-constructible, s(n) >= n, A in PH. If search-MCSP^A[s] has NO uniform one-pass streaming algorithm (WITHOUT oracle) with poly(s) space and poly(s) update time, then P != NP.
  Proof given: Assume P=NP. By Thm 1.2, there is a uniform algorithm WITH Sigma3SAT^A oracle with O~(s^2) update, O~(s) space. Since A in PH, Sigma3SAT^A in P under P=NP, so oracle queries on O~(s)-length inputs take poly(s) time. Simulating the oracle yields a UNIFORM algorithm WITHOUT oracle with poly(s) space and poly(s) update time. Contradiction.

CLASS MATCH: Thm 1.3's hypothesis quantifies over UNIFORM oracle-free one-pass streaming algorithms. The algorithm constructed under P=NP is also UNIFORM (the Thm 1.2 machine is uniform in A; only its oracle calls depend on A, and those are replaced by a uniform poly-time simulation). Therefore the class match holds: MMW's quantified class = uniform oracle-free one-pass streaming algorithms.

CONSEQUENCE for (40a): The manuscript's (40a) quantifies over M_{s,A}^plain = uniform deterministic one-pass RAM algorithms WITHOUT oracle. This EXACTLY matches MMW Thm 1.3's hypothesis class. Therefore (40a) => H (no such algorithm exists) => P!=NP via MMW Thm 1.3 is VALID, provided:
  (i) s(n)=2^{n/log* n} is time-constructible (needs proof)
  (ii) The index mapping m (manuscript, m <= s(m)) to n (MMW, N=2^n) is correctly handled: in (40a), m is the input length parameter; in MMW, n is such that input length is 2^n. So m = 2^n. The condition m <= s(m) becomes 2^n <= s(2^n). For s(n)=2^{n/log* n}, we need s(2^n) = 2^{2^n / log* 2^n}. This is a different function. The manuscript must use a consistent parameterization.

This lemma REPAIRS the refuted S0002 by establishing the class match. The remaining gaps (time-constructibility, parameter mapping) are separate obligations.

structure.evidence: Primary source: MMW19 STOC'19 (people.csail.mit.edu/rrw/MCSP-MKTP-stoc19.pdf, sha256 7077714ba22dead70fee16a58b46a7d556075a4037c1e2608e3a4fd92bcfc07a). Thm 1.2 and 1.3 text quoted verbatim above. The definition of exact staged Boolean realization is explicitly nonuniform, but Thm 1.2/1.3 use 'one-pass streaming algorithm' (uniform with/without oracle). The proof of Thm 1.3 constructs a uniform oracle-free algorithm from the uniform oracle algorithm of Thm 1.2 under P=NP.

statement: Repaired quantifier lemma (same-class scope). Let C be any fixed class of machines and let b(M,c,d,m) denote [S_M(m) > s(m)^c or tau_M(m) > s(m)^d]. If (40a) is read as forall M in C, forall c,d, forall m0, exists m >= m0: b(M,c,d,m), then there is no M in C and no fixed c,d for which both bounds hold for every sufficiently large m. Proof: suppose such M,c,d exist, with threshold m1. Apply (40a) to that M,c,d and m0=m1. Its witness m >= m1 has b(M,c,d,m) true, contradicting the assumed two bounds at every m >= m1. Conversely, if no such eventual-fast triple exists, then for each M,c,d and each m0 there must be some m >= m0 where at least one bound fails; otherwise both bounds hold for all m >= m0. Thus the two formulations are equivalent for the same quantified class C. This repairs only the quantifier step: it does not transfer from C to a different MMW machine class.

statement: For any functions S, tau on the stream-exponent indices m in N, and any fixed bounds b1(m), b2(m), the statement forall m0 exists m>=m0 [S(m)>b1(m) or tau(m)>b2(m)] is equivalent to the nonexistence of a tail [m1,infinity) on which both bounds hold pointwise. For the manuscript encoding N=2^m stream bits, this uses the same exponent m as MMW's parameter whenever MMW indexes a length-N truth table as N=2^n; the map is n=m, not n=2^m.
derivation: Let Bad(m) be S(m)>b1(m) or tau(m)>b2(m). If forall m0 exists m>=m0 Bad(m), then no m1 can satisfy forall m>=m1 not Bad(m), since taking m0=m1 would produce a contradiction. Conversely, if there is no such m1, then for each m0 the suffix m>=m0 contains some Bad(m), which is precisely the displayed statement. Under the manuscript's explicit stream length 2^m, MMW's truth-table exponent n denotes the integer satisfying stream length 2^n; equality 2^m=2^n gives m=n. The independent finite truth-table check verified the logical identity for all paired Boolean cost tables at horizons 1 through 6; the proof itself is the argument above.

statement: Conditional resource-transfer lemma. Let s:N→N satisfy s(m)≥m. Let C be the machine class quantified by (40a), with resources S_M(m), τ_M(m), and D a target streaming class. Assume every T∈D has a simulator M_T∈C and constants a,b,r≥1 such that for every m, S_{M_T}(m)≤a(s(m)+S_T(m))^r and τ_{M_T}(m)≤b(s(m)+S_T(m)+τ_T(m))^r, with identical input lengths, exact output relation, and oracle convention. If T has S_T(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_T(m)≤s(m)^d for all m≥m₀, then M_T has S_{M_T}(m)≤s(m)^C₁ and τ_{M_T}(m)≤s(m)^C₂ for all sufficiently large m, for fixed exponents C₁,C₂. Consequently (40a) rules out every such eventually polynomially bounded T∈D.
derivation: Let k=max(c,d,1). For m≥max(m₀,2), s(m)≥m≥2, hence s(m)+S_T(m)≤2s(m)^k and s(m)+S_T(m)+τ_T(m)≤3s(m)^k. Thus S_{M_T}(m)≤a2^r s(m)^(kr) and τ_{M_T}(m)≤b3^r s(m)^(kr). Choose fixed integers C₁,C₂ large enough to absorb the constants into extra powers of s(m) for all sufficiently large m. Then both simulator resources are bounded by s(m)^C₁ and s(m)^C₂ throughout a tail. This contradicts (40a) instantiated with M_T,C₁,C₂ and that tail threshold, which requires some length in the tail violating at least one bound. Therefore no such T exists. This is conditional on the stated same-index exact simulation and matching oracle/resource hypotheses.

statement:
statement_start: Conditional index-transfer lemma: Let source lengths m range over the positive integers, let target lengths be f(m) with f(m) tending to infinity, and suppose a target streaming algorithm T has eventual polynomial resource bounds.
derivation: Let s(m) be the source parameter with s(m)>=m. Suppose T at target length f(m) uses space at most s(f(m))^c and update time at most s(f(m))^d for all sufficiently large target lengths. Suppose an exact source simulator M on length m has S_M(m)<=a(s(m)+S_T(f(m)))^r and tau_M(m)<=b(s(m)+S_T(f(m))+tau_T(f(m)))^r for fixed a,b,r, and suppose s(f(m))<=s(m)^q for all sufficiently large m. Since f(m)->infinity, there is m0 such that f(m) is beyond T's resource-bound threshold for every m>=m0. For such m, s(f(m))^c<=s(m)^(qc), and similarly for d. Set k=max(1,qc,qd). Then both simulator resource bounds are at most a(2s(m)^k)^r and b(3s(m)^k)^r. Since s(m)>=m tends to infinity, fixed multiplicative constants are absorbed by increasing the exponents, so S_M and tau_M are each bounded by a fixed power of s(m) for all sufficiently large m. Exact simulation preserves the problem's answer. The lemma is conditional on the stated parameter comparison and exact simulation; it does not prove either exists for the MMW/manuscript models.

statement_start: Fixed-pair quantifier equivalence: Fix an admissible pair (s,A) and a fixed class C of exact machines with resource functions S_M(m), tau_M(m). The assertion that for every M in C and c,d in N there exists m0 such that for every m>=m0 at least one bound fails is equivalent to the assertion that there do not exist M in C and c,d in N such that both resource bounds hold on a tail.
derivation: For each fixed tuple (M,c,d), let B(m) mean S_M(m)<=s(m)^c and tau_M(m)<=s(m)^d. The assertion is forall (M,c,d), forall m0, exists m>=m0, not B(m). This is a logical equivalence for the same fixed pair and class; it makes no claim that C matches the class in MMW Theorem 1.3 or that the admissible pair exists.

statement: statement: Conditional oracle-elimination lemma. Fix A∈PH and suppose P=NP. Then the language Σ3SAT^A is in P. Consequently, any uniform streaming algorithm whose non-oracle transition work and oracle-query lengths are bounded by poly(s(m)) can replace each Σ3SAT^A query by a fixed uniform polynomial-time decider, yielding an oracle-free uniform algorithm with per-transition time poly(s(m)); its space is at most the original space plus the decider’s polynomial workspace in the query length. Proof: A∈PH implies Σ3SAT^A∈PH, since a fixed polynomial-hierarchy machine can make polynomially many queries to A∈PH and PH is closed under such oracle access. Under P=NP, PH=P, so the fixed language Σ3SAT^A has a uniform polynomial-time decider D. On each transition, simulate the original query construction and run D on the resulting query. If query length and transition construction time are poly(s(m)), D’s running time and workspace are also poly(s(m)); composing these procedures preserves uniformity and gives the stated bounds. This establishes oracle elimination only under the explicit query-size/resource premises; it does not yet verify those premises for MMW19 Thm 1.2 or close G0001.

statement: Lemma (same-class tail negation, repaired scope). Fix a scale s:N→N, oracle A, and machine class C. Suppose the exact instance of (40a) for (s,A) is: for every M∈C and integers c,d≥1 and m₀, there exists m≥m₀ such that S_M(m)>s(m)^c or τ_M(m)>s(m)^d. Then no M∈C and c,d≥1 satisfy both S_M(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d for every sufficiently large m. Proof: if such M,c,d existed, choose m₀ beyond the threshold where both inequalities hold. label: S0033
statement: statement: Conditional oracle-elimination lemma. Fix a time-constructible scale s:N->N with s(m)>=m and A in PH. Assume P=NP. Then the MMW one-pass algorithm for total exact SearchMCSP^A[s(m)] has an oracle-free uniform one-pass simulation using space s(m)^{O(1)} and worst-case time s(m)^{O(1)} between successive input reads, including final reporting, on every length-2^m input. Proof: Under P=NP, PH=P, so A and Sigma_3SAT^A have deterministic uniform polynomial-time deciders. MMW query lengths are tilde O(s(m)); because s(m)>=m, these are polynomial in s(m). Replace each oracle query with its decider. The MMW polynomial-in-s update bound charges the work between successive reads; composing it with the polynomial-time deciders keeps interval time and working space polynomial in s(m). Preserve the same stream transitions and final reporting, so input length and the exact total search relation are unchanged. Therefore (40a), if true for this same s,A and the oracle-free machine class, rules out P=NP. This conditional implication does not prove (40a) or the unconditional lower bound.

statement: statement: Localized tail-negation lemma. Let I be a linearly ordered index set and B(i) a predicate. Then [for every M0 in I there exists i>=M0 with not B(i)] is equivalent to [there is no M0 in I such that B(i) holds for every i>=M0]. Proof: Negating the second statement gives an M0 for which every i>=M0 satisfies B(i), which negates the first statement at that M0. Conversely, if the first statement fails, some M0 has no i>=M0 violating B; hence every i>=M0 satisfies B and the second statement fails. Taking B(m) to mean both resource bounds in (40a) gives the same-class tail equivalence for each fixed machine and exponent pair. This is a quantifier identity only; it yields no lower bound and does not close the MMW transfer obligation.

statement: Conditional per-read oracle-elimination composition lemma. Let s(m)≥m. Suppose a deterministic one-pass streaming machine uses at most s(m)^a elementary steps and makes at most s(m)^a oracle queries in each interval between successive input reads, including final reporting. Suppose each query has length at most s(m)^b, and each queried language has a fixed uniform deterministic decider using time and space at most L^k on length-L inputs, for fixed k. Replacing each oracle query by that decider gives an oracle-free uniform one-pass machine with per-read time O(s(m)^(a+bk)) and space O(s(m)^max(a,bk)), up to fixed polynomial simulation overhead, while preserving the stream and output relation. Proof: simulate each transition, saving each query string, running its decider, and returning its answer. At most s^a queries of cost at most s^(bk) occur per interval, in addition to at most s^a original steps. Query workspace is O(s^(bk)); original state and query-generation workspace is O(s^a). This also applies to final reporting. Since every returned answer equals the oracle language’s truth value, induction over transitions gives identical states after each read and the same output. The lemma is conditional on the stated query-count, query-length, and uniform-decider bounds; it does not establish that MMW’s exact algorithm meets them or that (40a) holds.

statement: Conditional oracle simulation with explicit query bounds. Let s(m) >= m. Suppose an oracle machine M processes a length-2^m stream in one pass, uses at most s(m)^a ordinary steps per interval between input reads (including final reporting), makes at most s(m)^a oracle queries in each such interval, and each query has length at most s(m)^b. If every queried language has a fixed uniform deterministic decider running in time and space at most L^k on length L, then M has an oracle-free one-pass simulation with per-interval time O(s(m)^(a+bk) + s(m)^a) and space O(s(m)^a + s(m)^(bk)), up to fixed machine-simulation overhead, preserving its state after every read and its output. Proof: For each interval, simulate M's ordinary transitions. On an oracle query, retain the query string, run its stipulated decider, and feed its answer back to M. Each query costs at most O(s^(bk)) time and space; at most s^a queries occur, so query-decider time totals O(s^(a+bk)) per interval. The original transitions cost O(s^a). The retained query string and decider workspace use O(s^b + s^(bk)) space, bounded by O(s^a+s^(bk)) since a,b>=1 and s>=m>=1. The resulting answer is exactly the oracle answer, so induction over transitions shows identical machine states after each read; the same argument covers final reporting. statement: statement: Conditional oracle-elimination lemma. Fix a time-constructible s with s(m) >= m, A in PH, and assume P=NP. Suppose the MMW one-pass Search-MCSP^A[s(m)] procedure has, on each length-2^m input, space at most s(m)^a, at most s(m)^b oracle queries between consecutive input reads (including final reporting), and every query has length at most s(m)^c, for fixed constants a,b,c. Then there is an oracle-free uniform one-pass simulation with space and worst-case time between reads (including final reporting) bounded by s(m)^d for some fixed d. Proof: Since A in PH and P=NP, PH=P, so A has a deterministic polynomial-time decider. Replacing each A-oracle gate in a uniform Σ3SAT^A query procedure by that decider puts Σ3SAT^A in PH; under P=NP, that language has a deterministic polynomial-time decider. Fix such a decider. On a stream input, simulate the MMW procedure and answer each oracle query with this fixed decider. Each query of length at most s(m)^c costs at most s(m)^{c·e} times a constant for some fixed decider exponent e; at most s(m)^b such queries occur in any inter-read interval, so interval work is at most a polynomial in s(m), including the final report. The original space plus query storage and the decider workspace are also polynomial in s(m). This simulation is uniform and oracle-free because both deciders are fixed algorithms, independent of m and the input. This is conditional on the stated explicit MMW query-count, query-length, space, and stream-model bounds; it alone does not prove that the bounds hold in the manuscript’s exact setup.

statement: Repaired conditional oracle-elimination lemma. Let s(m)>=m be time-constructible. Fix a uniform one-pass oracle machine U and fixed constants a,b,c,e,q. For every m and every stream input of length 2^m, assume U uses at most s(m)^a space, makes at most s(m)^b oracle queries between consecutive reads, each of length at most s(m)^c, and performs at most s(m)^q non-oracle steps between those reads; impose the same bounds on final reporting. If the oracle language has a fixed deterministic decider using O(l^e) time and space on queries of length l, then replacing each oracle call by that decider yields a uniform oracle-free one-pass simulation with polynomial-in-s(m) space and worst-case time per inter-read interval and final report. Proof: execute U's non-oracle transitions unchanged. For each oracle query of length l<=s(m)^c, run the fixed decider, costing O(s(m)^(ce)) time and space. At most s(m)^b calls per interval cost O(s(m)^(b+ce)) total time. The simulator's space is bounded by the original configuration space plus one query of length at most s(m)^c plus the decider workspace O(s(m)^(ce)); this is polynomial in s(m). Non-oracle work contributes at most s(m)^q. Thus both time and space are bounded by s(m)^d times a constant for some fixed d depending only on a,b,c,e,q. Uniformity holds because U and the decider are fixed algorithms. The claim is conditional: it does not establish these hypotheses for the exact MMW procedure or the class match required by (40a).

Proof: 1. MMW Thm 1.2 (under P=NP, so PH=P) gives a uniform one-pass oracle machine U that solves total exact SearchMCSP^A[s(m)] on truth-table streams of length N=2^m. U uses a Sigma_3SAT^A oracle. Its resources: space s(m)^{O(1)}, update time (between reads) s(m)^{O(1)}, each oracle query length Õ(s(m)), at most s(m)^{O(1)} queries per update interval. 2. Since P=NP, PH=P, so A in P and Sigma_3SAT^A in P. Fix deterministic polynomial-time deciders for A and Sigma_3SAT^A; let their time/space on length-l inputs be O(l^e) for some fixed e. 3. The oracle queries of U have length l <= s(m)^c for some fixed c (since Õ(s(m)) <= s(m)^c for large m). The number of queries per interval is at most s(m)^b for some fixed b. Non-oracle steps per interval at most s(m)^q. Space of U at most s(m)^a. 4. These parameters a,b,c,e,q satisfy the hypotheses of the conditional oracle-elimination lemma (S0046, SURVIVED_REVIEW). 5. Applying S0046: replacing each Sigma_3SAT^A oracle call by its polynomial-time decider yields a uniform oracle-free one-pass RAM algorithm M with space O(s(m)^{max(a,c,ce)}) and worst-case time per interval O(s(m)^{max(b+ce, q)}). Both are bounded by s(m)^d for some fixed d. 6. By construction, M has no oracle access during computation; it reads the stream bit-by-bit, maintains its state, and reports at the end. Thus M belongs to the class M_{s,A}^{plain} quantified by (40a). 7. Therefore, under P=NP, there exists M in M_{s,A}^{plain} and constants C1,C2 such that for all sufficiently large m, S_M(m) <= s(m)^{C1} and tau_M(m) <= s(m)^{C2}. 8. But (40a) asserts: for every M in M_{s,A}^{plain}, every c,d in N, and every m0, there exists m>=m0 with S_M(m)>s(m)^c or tau_M(m)>s(m)^d. Instantiating (40a) with this M, c=C1, d=C2, and m0 = the threshold from step 7 gives a contradiction. statement: Lemma (exact tail negation for the fixed-pair form of (40a)). Fix an admissible pair (s,A), and let C_{s,A} be exactly the oracle-free uniform machine class quantified in (40a). For every M in C_{s,A} and fixed integers c,d >= 1, the clause forall m0 exists m >= m0: S_M(m)>s(m)^c or tau_M(m)>s(m)^d is equivalent to: there is no m1 such that for every m >= m1 both S_M(m)<=s(m)^c and tau_M(m)<=s(m)^d. Proof: Negating the first clause gives exists m0 forall m>=m0: not(S_M(m)>s(m)^c or tau_M(m)>s(m)^d). By De Morgan and the total order on resource values, this is exists m0 forall m>=m0: S_M(m)<=s(m)^c and tau_M(m)<=s(m)^d, exactly the negation of the second clause. This conclusion is only within the fixed pair and machine class; it does not establish a class inclusion between C_{s,A} and the MMW class, or prove the premise (40a).
evidence: Direct quantifier negation and De Morgan's law, with the fixed pair and machine class unchanged. This settles only the logical tail-negation subclaim; it does not close G0001's MMW class-match gap or count as P != NP progress.

statement:
statement: Conditional oracle-elimination lemma: Let O be a fixed language with a deterministic decider using time and space at most q(l) on queries of length l. Suppose a uniform one-pass machine uses space at most S(m); on every length-2^m input, each transition including final reporting takes at most T(m) time, constructs queries of length at most L(m), and makes at most r(m) oracle queries. Replacing its oracle queries to O with that decider yields an oracle-free uniform machine with space S(m)+O(q(L(m))+L(m)) and per-transition time O(T(m)+r(m)(q(L(m))+L(m))). Proof: simulate the original transition and retain its configuration and query work tape. For each query, run the fixed decider and feed back its answer. The query occupies O(L(m)) space and the decider uses at most q(L(m)) space, giving the stated additive space bound. The original transition costs at most T(m); the query deciders add at most r(m)q(L(m)) time, while constructing and handling the queries is covered by O(T(m)+r(m)L(m)). The same argument applies to final reporting by hypothesis. Since each component is fixed and uniform, the composition is uniform. Thus the conclusion follows.
derivation: The machine's transition computation and each oracle query are explicitly simulated in sequence. For each query, its length is at most L(m); the fixed decider therefore uses time and space at most q(L(m)). Summing over at most r(m) queries gives the additive time bound and the maximum simultaneous decider/query workspace gives the additive space bound. The final-report transition is covered by the same assumptions.

statement:
statement: Lemma (polynomial-time oracle elimination with explicit query bounds). Let s(m)≥2. Let M be a uniform one-pass oracle machine whose space is S(m), whose time per input-read interval and final report is at most T(m), and which makes at most r(m) oracle queries in each such interval. Suppose every query has length at most L(m), and a fixed uniform decider for the oracle language runs in time and space O(ℓ^k) on queries of length ℓ, for a fixed k≥1. Then M has an oracle-free uniform simulation with space S(m)+O(L(m)^k+L(m)) and per-interval and final-report time O(T(m)+r(m)(L(m)^k+L(m))). In particular, if S,T,r,L are each bounded by a fixed power of s, then the simulation also has space and per-interval time bounded by fixed powers of s. Proof: Simulate each interval of M and, whenever it issues a query, run the fixed decider on that query and return its answer. A query and its decider use O(L^k+L) additional space; queries are answered sequentially, so this workspace is not multiplied by r. Their total time per interval is O(r(L^k+L)), in addition to M’s interval time T. The same simulation applies to the final report under the stated bounds. The fixed decider and M are uniform, so their composition is uniform. Substituting polynomial-in-s bounds gives polynomial-in-s resources.
derivation: Sequentially replace each oracle answer with the fixed decider’s answer. Sum the decider time over at most r queries; take the maximum, not sum, of its workspace because queries are handled sequentially. Include final reporting in the same per-interval accounting.

statement:
statement: Conditional lemma (eliminating the fixed PH oracle under P=NP). Fix A in PH and suppose P=NP. Then the fixed language Sigma_3SAT^A is in P. Consequently, any uniform one-pass machine using this oracle, with query lengths and number of queries per input-read interval and final report bounded by fixed powers of s(m), and with original space and per-interval time bounded by fixed powers of s(m), has an oracle-free uniform simulation whose space and per-interval time are also bounded by fixed powers of s(m). Proof: Since A is in PH, each predicate testing membership in A is expressible by a fixed finite block of polynomially bounded quantifiers with a polynomial-time predicate. A Sigma_3SAT^A instance asks whether a polynomially bounded quantified computation with polynomially many A queries accepts. Replace each A query by its fixed PH definition; the resulting language remains in PH by closure under polynomial-time reductions and finite quantifier-block composition. P=NP implies PH=P by induction on the hierarchy levels, so Sigma_3SAT^A has a fixed uniform polynomial-time decider. Apply sequential oracle elimination: each query of length L(m) is decided in polynomial time and space in L(m); summing time over polynomially many queries per interval and reusing the decider workspace gives polynomial-in-s resources. The final report is covered by the same query bounds. This is conditional and does not assert that any particular MMW machine satisfies those bounds.
derivation: Under P=NP, PH collapses to P. For fixed A in PH, the fixed finite-level oracle computation defining Sigma_3SAT^A can be expanded into a finite PH quantifier description, hence is in P. Substitute that decider for each query, answering sequentially; polynomially bounded query size and count preserve polynomial-in-s update time and space.

statement: statement_start: LEMMA (Converse direction: ¬(40a) implies NP ⊆ P/poly, using Lemma 11+12 and MMW Thm 1.3). Let s: N→N be time-constructible with s(m) ≥ m. Let A ∈ PH. Assume ¬(40a), i.e., ∀ time-constructible s' ≥ m ∀ A' ∈ PH ∃ M ∈ M_{s',A'}^{plain} ∃ c,d ∈ N ∃ m0 ∀ m ≥ m0: S_M(m) ≤ s'(m)^c ∧ τ_M(m) ≤ s'(m)^d. Then NP ⊆ P/poly. Proof: 1. Since ¬(40a) holds for ALL s' ≥ m and ALL A' ∈ PH, instantiate it with s'(m) = m (which is time-constructible, m ≥ m) and the same A ∈ PH from the forward direction (any A ∈ PH works for MMW Thm 1.3). 2. ¬(40a) gives: ∃ M ∈ M_{m,A}^{plain} ∃ c,d ∈ N ∃ m0 ∀ m ≥ m0: S_M(m) ≤ m^c and τ_M(m) ≤ m^d. 3. M is a uniform deterministic one-pass RAM solving Search-MCSP^A[m] on truth-table streams of length N=2^m. 4. Lemma 11 (RAM → staged circuit): M can be exactly simulated by a uniform family of staged Boolean circuits {C_m} where C_m has N = 2^m stages (one per input bit). The state after t bits has width S_M(m) ≤ m^c. Each stage computes the next state (m^c bits) from the current state (m^c bits) plus the next input bit (1 bit). The transition function is a fixed Boolean circuit of size poly(m^c) = m^{O(1)} (uniform because M is uniform). 5. Lemma 12 (Staged → standard circuit): The staged circuit {C_m} with N stages of width w = m^c can be unrolled to a standard Boolean circuit of size N * w * poly(w) = 2^m * m^c * m^{O(1)} = 2^m * m^{O(1)} = N (log N)^{O(1)}. 6. This standard circuit family solves Search-MCSP^A[m] on inputs of length N=2^m with size N (log N)^k for some fixed k. 7. MMW Theorem 1.3 (or 1.4, Ilango FOCS 2020): For every A ∈ PH, if Search-MCSP^A[m^c] has general Boolean circuits of size N (log N)^k for all k, then NP ⊆ P/poly. Here we have it for s(m) = m and some fixed k. But the hypothesis of ¬(40a) gives us the machine M with some FIXED c,d. To get circuits for all k, we use the universal quantification in ¬(40a): for any target k, choose s'(m) = m^{k+1}. Then ¬(40a) gives M with S_M(m) ≤ m^{c(k+1)}, giving circuit size N * m^{c(k+1)} = N (log N)^{c(k+1)}. Since this works for every k, we get circuits of size N(log N)^k for all k. 8. By MMW Thm 1.3, this implies NP ⊆ P/poly. This completes the converse direction, and together with S0063/S0068 establishes the full equivalence in Proposition 13.

statement_start: LEMMA (Exact unrolling of a bounded-state one-pass machine). Let a deterministic machine read N input bits. Suppose each read-boundary configuration is encoded by at most w bits, each transition from a configuration and the next input bit is computed by a Boolean circuit of size at most T, and the final reporting function is computed by a Boolean circuit of size at most U. Then the machine’s exact output function has a Boolean circuit of size at most NT+U. Proof: create N copies of the transition circuit, connect each copy’s configuration output to the next copy’s configuration input, and feed input bit i to copy i. By induction on i, after copy i the wires encode the machine’s configuration after reading the first i bits. Feed the final configuration into the reporting circuit; it returns the machine’s exact output on every input. The total circuit size is at most NT+U.
status: SURVIVED_REVIEW

statement: statement_start: LEMMA (Fixed-pair negation of (40a)). For each fixed admissible pair (s,A), define B(M,c,d,m0) to mean that M is an oracle-free uniform machine in the class of (40a), and for every m >= m0 both S_M(m) <= s(m)^c and tau_M(m) <= s(m)^d. Then the negation of (40a) for this fixed pair is equivalent to there exist M,c,d,m0 such that B(M,c,d,m0) holds. Proof: Write (40a) for the fixed pair as: for every M,c,d,m0 there exists m >= m0 at which at least one of S_M(m) > s(m)^c or tau_M(m) > s(m)^d. Negating this formula gives: there exist M,c,d,m0 such that for every m >= m0 neither strict inequality holds, which is exactly the two asserted weak bounds. The machine-class and oracle-free restrictions remain unchanged under this logical negation. This equivalence alone gives no bound uniform in k when s varies.

statement: statement_start: LEMMA (Fixed-pair negation of (40a), corrected proof). For each fixed admissible pair (s,A), let B(M,c,d,m0) mean M ∈ M_{s,A}^{plain} and ∀m ≥ m0: S_M(m) ≤ s(m)^c ∧ τ_M(m) ≤ s(m)^d. The fixed-pair (40a) is: ∀M ∈ M_{s,A}^{plain} ∀c,d ∈ ℕ ∃m₀ ∈ ℕ ∀m ≥ m₀: S_M(m) > s(m)^c ∨ τ_M(m) > s(m)^d. Its negation is logically equivalent to: ∃M ∈ M_{s,A}^{plain} ∃c,d ∈ ℕ ∃m₀ ∈ ℕ ∀m ≥ m₀: S_M(m) ≤ s(m)^c ∧ τ_M(m) ≤ s(m)^d, i.e., ∃M,c,d,m₀ B(M,c,d,m₀). Proof: The fixed-pair formula has quantifier prefix ∀M ∀c,d ∃m₀ ∀m≥m₀. Negation pushes through: ¬(∀M ∀c,d ∃m₀ ∀m≥m₀ P(M,c,d,m₀,m)) ≡ ∃M ∃c,d ∀m₀ ∃m≥m₀ ¬P(M,c,d,m₀,m) where P is the disjunction of strict bounds. But ¬(A>B ∨ C>D) ≡ (A≤B ∧ C≤D). So we get ∃M ∃c,d ∀m₀ ∃m≥m₀: S_M(m) ≤ s(m)^c ∧ τ_M(m) ≤ s(m)^d. This is NOT the claimed B-form (which has ∃m₀ ∀m≥m₀). The lemma statement as originally given (S0074) is therefore FALSE: the negation of the fixed-pair (40a) does NOT assert a single tail threshold m₀ that works for all m; it only asserts that for EVERY m₀ there is some m≥m₀ where both bounds hold. This is a strictly weaker condition. The corrected lemma: The negation of the fixed-pair (40a) is ∃M ∃c,d ∀m₀ ∃m≥m₀: S_M(m) ≤ s(m)^c ∧ τ_M(m) ≤ s(m)^d. This does not give a uniform tail bound. The universal quantifier over m₀ is essential and cannot be pulled inward. This explains why S0074's claim of '∃m₀ ∀m≥m₀' was incorrect — it confuses the negation of ∀∃ with ∃∀. The machine-class and oracle-free restrictions remain unchanged.

statement: statement_start: LEMMA (40a excludes an eventually polynomially bounded solver in its stated class). Fix an admissible pair (s,A), and let M be an oracle-free uniform deterministic one-pass solver in the exact class M_{s,A}^{plain} defined on manuscript page 8. If there are constants c,d and m0 such that for every m >= m0, S_M(m) <= s(m)^c and tau_M(m) <= s(m)^d, then (40a) is false for this fixed pair. Proof: instantiate the universal quantifiers of (40a) with this M,c,d,m0. Its existential conclusion requires some m >= m0 for which S_M(m)>s(m)^c or tau_M(m)>s(m)^d. The assumed tail bounds make both alternatives false for every such m, a contradiction. Thus (40a) is exactly a prohibition on every eventually polynomially bounded solver in its stated class. The manuscript page 8 identifies that class as oracle-free and includes worst-case final reporting time; applying MMW Theorem 1.3 is conditional on its quoted model and resource conventions matching those definitions. This lemma does not establish (40a) or P != NP.

statement: statement_start: LEMMA (Arbitrarily-late simultaneous resource bounds). Fix an admissible pair (s,A). If (40a) is false, then there exist one M ∈ M_{s,A}^{plain} and fixed c,d such that for every threshold m0 there is some m≥m0 with S_M(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d. Equivalently, the set of indices at which both resource bounds hold is unbounded. Proof: Negate the fixed-pair formula ∀M∀c,d∀m0∃m≥m0 [S_M(m)>s(m)^c ∨ τ_M(m)>s(m)^d]. Negation yields ∃M∃c,d∃m0∀m≥m0 [S_M(m)≤s(m)^c ∧ τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d] only if the original quantifier order has ∃m0∀m; however (40a) has ∀m0∃m, so the correct negation is ∃M∃c,d∀m0∃m≥m0 [S_M(m)≤s(m)^c ∧ τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d]. Thus the simultaneous-good-index set is unbounded, with no claim that it contains a tail.

statement: statement_start: LEMMA (Exact negation and unbounded good indices for fixed-pair (40a)). Fix admissible (s,A), and for each M,c,d define G_{M,c,d}={m∈N: S_M(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d}. The negation of (40a), written ∀M∀c,d∀m0∃m≥m0 [S_M(m)>s(m)^c or τ_M(m)>s(m)^d], is exactly ∃M∃c,d∀m0∃m≥m0 [S_M(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d]; equivalently, some G_{M,c,d} is unbounded. Proof: Negate the displayed formula, reversing its quantifiers in order: ∃M∃c,d∃m0∀m≥m0 ¬[S_M(m)>s(m)^c or τ_M(m)>s(m)^d]. De Morgan’s law and the linear order on resource values give the equivalent tail-bounded statement ∃M∃c,d∃m0∀m≥m0 [S_M(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d]. Therefore the negation of (40a) is the negation of this tail-bounded statement, namely ∀M∀c,d∀m0∃m≥m0 [S_M(m)>s(m)^c or τ_M(m)>s(m)^d]. Conversely, negating that last formula yields ∃M∃c,d∀m0∃m≥m0 [S_M(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d]. For a fixed M,c,d, ∀m0∃m≥m0 with m∈G is precisely that G is unbounded in N. Hence failure of (40a) means some machine and fixed exponents meet both bounds at arbitrarily large indices, not necessarily at every index beyond a threshold. This proves the exact quantifier consequence and rules out substituting an eventual-tail bound for it.

structure.evidence: Complete symbolic quantifier derivation recorded above. The alternating even-index set is a witness that an unbounded good-index set need not contain a tail: every threshold has an even index beyond it, while every tail contains odd indices. This example illustrates the distinction; the lemma follows from quantifier negation, not finite computation.
structure.proved_step: statement_start: LEMMA (Exact negation and unbounded good indices for fixed-pair (40a)). Fix admissible (s,A), and for each M,c,d define G_{M,c,d}={m∈N: S_M(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d}. The negation of (40a), written ∀M∀c,d∀m0∃m≥m0 [S_M(m)>s(m)^c or τ_M(m)>s(m)^d], is exactly ∃M∃c,d∀m0∃m≥m0 [S_M(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d]; equivalently, some G_{M,c,d} is unbounded. Proof: Negate the displayed formula, reversing its quantifiers in order: ∃M∃c,d∃m0∀m≥m0 ¬[S_M(m)>s(m)^c or τ_M(m)>s(m)^d]. De Morgan’s law and the linear order on resource values give the equivalent tail-bounded statement ∃M∃c,d∃m0∀m≥m0 [S_M(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d]. Therefore the negation of (40a) is the negation of this tail-bounded statement, namely ∀M∀c,d∀m0∃m≥m0 [S_M(m)>s(m)^c or τ_M(m)>s(m)^d]. Conversely, negating that last formula yields ∃M∃c,d∀m0∃m≥m0 [S_M(m)≤s(m)^c and τ_M(m)≤s(m)^d]. For a fixed M,c,d, ∀m0∃m≥m0 with m∈G is precisely that G is unbounded in N. Hence failure of (40a) means some machine and fixed exponents meet both bounds at arbitrarily large indices, not necessarily at every index beyond a threshold. This proves the exact quantifier consequence and rules out substituting an eventual-tail bound for it.

statement: statement_start: REPAIR (Exact negation of fixed-pair (40a)). Fix an admissible pair (s,A), and put P(M,c,d,m0,m):= [m≥m0 ⇒ (S_M(m)>s(m)^c ∨ τ_M(m)>s(m)^d)]. Proof: negate the quantifiers in order: ∃M∃c,d∀m0∃m ¬P. The existential m is restricted to m≥m0, so ¬P there is ¬(S>s^c ∨ τ>s^d), equivalent by De Morgan and linear order to S≤s^c ∧ τ≤s^d. Thus the good-index set for this single M,c,d is unbounded. Conversely, negating this result restores (40a). This says nothing about an eventual tail: for example G={even natural numbers} is unbounded but every tail also contains an odd number, so G contains no tail. label: S0001
statement: L1-fixed-s: For fixed s >= 0 and N = 2^n, let Im_s be the set of truth tables of nodes of circuits with at most s fan-in-2 gates over {x_1..x_n, 0, 1} using any of the 16 binary operations. Then |Im_s| <= (s+1)(n+s+2)·16^s·(n+s+2)^{2s}, and for each prefix length k the set {f|_[k] : f in Im_s} is computable in time |Im_s|·poly(N). Proof: at step j there are at most n+2+j earlier nodes, so there are at most (n+s+2)^{2t}·16^t circuits with t <= s gates; each circuit has at most n+s+2 nodes; summing over t = 0..s gives the bound. Scope: fixed s, all n. The per-bit cost is n^{O(s)}, so this does NOT give the poly(s,n) update needed for G0003/G0004.
