label: S0035
statement: LEMMA L-PAT (pattern obstruction; CLAIMED until reviewed). Let n>=1, m>=n+1, W in Z^{m x n} of rank d<=n, t in Z^m, g_j(x)=[w_j.x>=t_j]. (a) The number of distinct patterns P(x)=(g_1(x),...,g_m(x)) over x in {0,1}^n is at most N(m,d)=sum_{i=0}^{d} C(m,i). PROOF (a): factor W=PQ with Q in R^{d x n}, so w_j.x=p_j.y with y=Qx in R^d, and Y={Qx : x in {0,1}^n} is finite. Let eps>0 be smaller than every nonzero |p_j.y-t_j| (y in Y), and put h_j(y)=p_j.y-t_j+eps. Then h_j(y) is never 0 on Y and g_j(x)=[h_j(Qx)>0]. Each pattern is the sign vector of the h_j at a point of Y, so distinct patterns lie in distinct regions of the arrangement {h_j=0} in R^d. An arrangement of m affine hyperplanes in R^d has at most sum_{i<=d} C(m,i) regions (Buck 1943; Cover 1965). (b) For d=n: N(m,n) > 2^n. PROOF (b): if m=n+1 then N=2^{n+1}-1 > 2^n since n>=1. If n+2<=m<=2n-1 then floor(m/2)<=n, and by symmetry of binomial coefficients sum_{i<=floor(m/2)} C(m,i) >= 2^{m-1} >= 2^{n+1} > 2^n. If m>=2n then N >= C(m,n)+1 >= C(2n,n)+1 > 2^n, using monotonicity of C(m,n) in m, C(2n,n)=2 (n=1), 6 (n=2), and for n>=3 C(2n,n) >= 4^n/(2n+1) >= 2^n because 2^n >= 2n+1. (c) For d<n: N(m,d) >= C(m,d) >= (m/d)^d, so N(m,d) < 2^{(1-delta)n} forces d*log2(m/d) < (1-delta)n. For m=n^{1.5} this forces d=O(n/log n), consistent with G0006. SCOPE: exact, every n>=1, m>=n+1, every integer W and t. This is a LIMIT on the class of procedures whose state is the realised bottom pattern. It is not an algorithm, and it does not close G0001.

label: S0040
statement: lemma,RestrictedTopSupportAlgorithm,Let f(x) = [∑_{j=1}^m v_j [W_j·x ≥ t_j] ≥ T] be a THR o THR circuit on n variables with m bottom gates. Suppose: (1) the top gate has at most k nonzero weights: |{j : v_j ≠ 0}| ≤ k; (2) the bottom weights are bounded integers: |W_j[i]| ≤ B for all j, i. Then #SAT(f) can be computed in time O(n k (2Bn+1)^k · poly(m)).,Proof: Let S = {j : v_j ≠ 0}, |S| = k. The function f depends on x only through the k bottom gate outputs g_S(x) = ([W_j·x ≥ t_j])_{j∈S}. For each fixed s ∈ {0,1}^k, the top gate evaluates to a constant c(s) = [∑_{j∈S} v_j s_j ≥ T]. The number of x with g_S(x) = s is the number of solutions to the system of k threshold inequalities: for j∈S, W_j·x ≥ t_j if s_j = 1, and W_j·x ≤ t_j − 1 if s_j = 0. Each linear form W_j·x takes values in [−Bn, Bn] (since |W_j[i]| ≤ B and x_i ∈ {0,1}), so at most 2Bn+1 integer values. A dynamic program over the n variables counts solutions: state = (c_1,…,c_k) ∈ [−Bn,Bn]^k, representing the current values of the k linear forms. Start with count 1 at (0,…,0). For each variable x_i = 0,1, update the counts by adding W_j[i] to c_j. The number of states is at most (2Bn+1)^k. Each update takes O(k (2Bn+1)^k) time. After n variables, for each s ∈ {0,1}^k with c(s)=1, sum the counts of states satisfying c_j ≥ t_j (s_j=1) or c_j ≤ t_j−1 (s_j=0). Total time O(n k (2Bn+1)^k + 2^k poly(k)) = O(n k (2Bn+1)^k · poly(m)). This is a proved running time for the stated restricted subclass.,kind,ALGORITHM,closes,G0011

structure.lemma: Decision-from-search via zero-marker. Let f: {0,1}^N -> {0,1} be a truth table, s >= 1, and S: {0,1}^N -> {0,1}^L a search circuit for search-MCSP[s] of size g and depth d. Assume (E1) if some circuit of size <= s computes f then S(f) != 0^L; (E2) otherwise S(f) = 0^L. Define D(f) = OR_{i<=L} S(f)_i. Then D decides MCSP[s] on f, and D has size <= g + L and depth <= d + ceil(log2 L) (fan-in 2).

label: S0002
statement: Verifier decision lemma. Fix n, N=2^n, s>=1, f in {0,1}^N. Let V(f,C)=1 iff C is a fan-in-2 circuit on n inputs of size <= s computing f. Let decode map an L-bit string to a circuit or to reject. Define Dec(f)=V(f, decode(S(f))). If S is correct on members (f has a size-<=s circuit implies S(f) encodes one), then Dec(f)=MCSP[s](f) for all f. Proof: member case: S(f) encodes a valid circuit, so V=1. Non-member case: no size-<=s circuit computes f, so V=0 for every string, hence Dec=0. E2 is not used. OPEN (gap): the size of V must be N*(log N)^{O(1)} to be harmless against the N(log N)^k target; only poly(N,s) overhead is shown.

label: S0003
statement: Sized verifier lemma. Fix n, N=2^n, s>=1. Encode a fan-in-2 circuit C on n inputs with s gates as L = O(s log(n+s)) bits: each gate stores two operand indices in [0, n+s) plus a gate-type bit. Let V(f,y) be the circuit with inputs f in {0,1}^N and y in {0,1}^L that outputs 1 iff y is well-formed, decodes to a circuit C of size <= s on n inputs, and C(a)=f(a) for all a in {0,1}^n. Claim: V has size O(N*s*max(n,s)). Proof: (i) Well-formedness and decoding of y cost O(L log L) gates, which is negligible. (ii) For each of the N points a, evaluate C(a) with a universal evaluator. Keep a value bank of n+s wires (the n inputs, hard-wired as constants for a, plus the s gate outputs). Gate t computes its two operands by multiplexers over the n+s bank wires, costing O(n+s) gates per operand, then one gate. One point costs O(s*(n+s)) gates. (iii) Compare C(a) with f(a): O(1) per point. Total O(N*(s*(n+s)+1)) = O(N*s*max(n,s)). With n = log N and s <= (log N)^c for a fixed c >= 1, this is O(N*(log N)^{2c}) = N*(log N)^{O(1)}. Consequence: if a search circuit S of size N(log N)^k outputs encodings of size-<=s circuits, then Dec(f)=V(f,S(f)) is a decision circuit of size N(log N)^{k'} with k' = max(k,2c)+O(1). By S0002, Dec = MCSP[s] (E2 not used). Contrapositive: no size-N(log N)^{k'} circuit family for decision MCSP[(log N)^c] implies none for search-MCSP at size N(log N)^k. This is the direction the H1 transfer needs.

label: S0001
statement:
statement: For any De Morgan formula with L input-variable leaf occurrences, under a restriction in which each input variable is left live with marginal probability p, the expected number of live input-variable leaf occurrences is pL. Repeated occurrences of a variable are counted separately.
proof: For each leaf occurrence i, let I_i be 1 when its input variable is left live and 0 otherwise. The number of live input leaves is sum_{i=1}^L I_i. By linearity of expectation, its expectation is sum_i E[I_i] = sum_i p = pL. This uses only the marginal survival probability and therefore also holds under pairwise-independent restrictions.

label: S0002
statement:
statement: Let Phi be a De Morgan formula with L input-variable leaf occurrences and gate-leaf occurrences grouped by gate g, with f_g occurrences of g. Under any restriction distribution where each input variable is live with marginal p and each gate g is nonconstant with probability q_g, the expected number of surviving leaf occurrences is pL + sum_g f_g q_g.
proof: For every input-leaf occurrence i, define indicator I_i that its variable remains live. For every gate-leaf occurrence j of gate g, define indicator J_j that g remains nonconstant. The surviving occurrence count is sum_i I_i + sum_g sum_{j=1}^{f_g} J_j. By linearity of expectation its expectation is sum_i p + sum_g sum_j q_g = pL + sum_g f_g q_g. No independence is needed.

label: S0003
statement:
statement: For a finite formula with L input-leaf occurrences, let d_v be the number of occurrences of variable v. Under independent restrictions leaving each variable live with probability p, the surviving input-leaf count X satisfies E[X]=pL and Var(X)=p(1-p) sum_v d_v^2. Consequently, if every d_v<=D, Var(X)<=p(1-p)DL.
proof: Write X=sum_v d_v I_v, where I_v is the Bernoulli-p indicator that v remains live. Then E[X]=sum_v d_v p=pL. Independence gives Var(X)=sum_v d_v^2 Var(I_v)=p(1-p)sum_v d_v^2. Since d_v^2<=D d_v, summing gives sum_v d_v^2<=DL and the stated bound.

label: S0006
statement:
statement: Let F be a finite CNF on n Boolean variables, with clauses indexed by a finite set C. For each clause C_i, let A_i be the set of assignments falsifying C_i. For S subseteq C, let N(S)=|intersection_{i in S} A_i|, with N(empty)=2^n. Then #F = sum_{S subseteq C} (-1)^|S| N(S). If each clause is a disjunction of literals, then N(S)=2^(n-|V(S)|) when the falsification requirements of all clauses in S are consistent, and N(S)=0 otherwise; here V(S) is the set of variables appearing in clauses of S.
proof: An assignment x satisfies F exactly when it lies in none of the events A_i. For each assignment x, the indicator that x lies in none of the A_i equals product_{i in C}(1-1_{A_i}(x)). Expanding the finite product gives sum_{S subseteq C}(-1)^|S| 1_{intersection_{i in S} A_i}(x). Sum over all 2^n assignments and interchange the two finite sums to obtain #F=sum_{S subseteq C}(-1)^|S|N(S). For the stated clause formula, falsifying each literal fixes its variable to one Boolean value. If two such requirements conflict on a variable then the intersection is empty. Otherwise each variable in V(S) is fixed uniquely and every variable outside V(S) is free, so the intersection has exactly 2^(n-|V(S)|) assignments. This includes S=empty by convention.

label: S0007
statement:
statement: Let Phi be a finite De Morgan formula whose leaves are input-variable occurrences and gate occurrences. Under a restriction, suppose each input leaf is retained with probability p and each occurrence of gate type g is retained as nonconstant with probability q_g. Let X be the number of retained leaf occurrences before simplification, and let size(Phi|rho) count leaves after restriction followed by constant folding only. If constant folding does not increase leaf count, then E[size(Phi|rho)] <= pL + sum_g f_g q_g, where L is the number of input leaves and f_g the number of occurrences of type g. Consequently, for every t>0, Pr(size(Phi|rho)>=t) <= (pL+sum_g f_g q_g)/t.
proof: Express X as the sum of indicator variables, one for each leaf occurrence. The input indicators have expectation p and each gate occurrence of type g has expectation q_g. Linearity of expectation gives E[X]=pL+sum_g f_g q_g, with no independence assumption. By the stated constant-folding hypothesis, size(Phi|rho)<=X pointwise, so E[size(Phi|rho)]<=E[X]. Since the residual size is nonnegative, Markov's inequality gives the tail bound.

label: S0008
statement:
statement: Let Phi be a binary De Morgan formula with L input-leaf occurrences, each variable appearing at most once. Independently leave each variable live with probability p in [0,1], substitute constants for the other variables, and simplify constant and identity gates. Define size as leaves plus internal gates, with a constant formula of size 1. Then E[size(Phi|rho)] <= 2pL+1.
proof: Let X be the number of surviving input leaves. After simplification, either the residual is constant, of size 1, or it is a binary formula with k<=X leaves. A binary tree with k>=1 leaves has k-1 internal gates, so its size is 2k-1<=2X. Thus in either case size(Phi|rho)<=2X+1. By linearity of expectation, E[X]=pL, hence E[size(Phi|rho)]<=2pL+1.

label: S0009
statement:
statement: Let T be any finite rooted full binary tree with at least one leaf, and let X be its number of leaves. If size(T) counts leaves plus internal vertices, then size(T)=2X-1. Consequently, if a restriction/simplification procedure returns either a constant of size 1 or a nonconstant full binary formula R, and X is defined as the number of leaves of R (not the pre-simplification surviving-leaf count), then size(R)=1 when R is constant and size(R)=2X-1 when R is nonconstant.
proof: Let I be the number of internal vertices. Every internal vertex has exactly two children, so the number of edges is 2I. Every finite tree with I+X vertices has I+X-1 edges. Hence 2I=I+X-1, giving I=X-1 and size(T)=I+X=2X-1. The constant case follows from the stipulated size convention.

label: S0010
statement: statement: Residual-leaf charging lemma. Let Phi be a finite binary De Morgan formula tree whose leaves are input-variable occurrences and designated gate-leaf occurrences. Apply a restriction rho, substitute constants at leaves whose predicates become constant, and simplify recursively by the identities AND(0,F)=0, AND(1,F)=F, OR(1,F)=1, OR(0,F)=F. Let L be the number of input-variable leaf occurrences, and let f_g be the number of occurrences of designated gate g. If each input variable occurrence is live with marginal probability p, and each occurrence of g remains nonconstant with probability q_g, then E[L(Phi|rho)] <= p L + sum_g f_g q_g, where L(Phi|rho) is the number of leaves in the simplified residual tree. Proof: Before simplification, mark each original leaf occurrence that is still nonconstant after substitution. Every leaf of the simplified tree is an original marked leaf: constant propagation deletes subtrees or replaces a parent by one child, and never creates or duplicates a leaf. Thus pointwise L(Phi|rho) <= X(rho), where X is the number of marked original leaves. By linearity of expectation, E[X]=pL+sum_g f_g q_g; no independence is needed. Taking expectations proves the bound. The exponent-two proposal is false for Phi=x with p=N^{-a}, L=1 and no gate leaves, since its left side is p while its right side is N^{o(1)}p^2=o(p). This lemma repairs it for the exact residual-tree size, though it does not yield P2's desired shrinkage.

structure.evidence: Pointwise injection from simplified residual leaves to surviving original nonconstant leaf occurrences; linearity of expectation. The formula Phi=x at p=N^{-a} refutes the proposed p^2 input-leaf term.

label: S0011
statement: statement: Let Phi be a finite formula whose leaves are occurrences indexed by k in a finite set K. Under a random restriction, let I_k be the indicator that occurrence k remains a leaf before constant folding, and set r_k=Pr[I_k=1]. Suppose the residual-size convention counts leaves after constant folding and that this folding never increases the leaf count. Then E[|Phi|_res] <= sum_{k in K} r_k, and for every t>0, Pr(|Phi|_res >= t) <= (sum_{k in K} r_k)/t. Proof: pointwise, |Phi|_res <= sum_k I_k by the nonincrease assumption. Taking expectations and using linearity gives E|Phi|_res <= sum_k E I_k = sum_k r_k, without any independence assumption. Markov's inequality for the nonnegative random variable |Phi|_res gives the tail bound.

label: S0012
statement: statement: Let N>1, let L be the number of input-variable leaf occurrences of a De Morgan formula, and let p=p(N) satisfy p(N)=N^{-epsilon(N)} for some epsilon(N)->0. Under any restriction distribution in which each input variable is live with marginal probability p, the expected number of surviving input-variable leaf occurrences is at most N^{epsilon(N)} p^2 L. Proof: For each occurrence i let I_i be its survival indicator and X=sum_i I_i. By linearity E[X]=pL. Since p=N^{-epsilon(N)}, pL=N^{epsilon(N)}p^2L exactly. No independence assumption is needed. Thus, on the restricted regime p=N^{-o(1)}, the input-leaf contribution to P2' is absorbed by its proposed p^2L term with an explicit subpolynomial factor; this does not control gate-leaf contributions or prove P2'.

label: S0013
statement: statement: Let T be a finite rooted binary formula tree whose leaves are partitioned into input-variable occurrences and gate occurrences. Under a restriction, each input occurrence survives as a variable with marginal probability p, and each occurrence of gate g remains nonconstant with marginal probability q_g. Define the residual tree by replacing every non-surviving leaf by a Boolean constant, evaluating constant subtrees, and suppressing unary internal nodes without duplicating subtrees; count one node for a constant. If T has L input leaves and f_g occurrences of g, then E[size(T|rho)] <= 2(pL + sum_g f_g q_g)+1. Proof: Let X count the surviving nonconstant leaves. Indicator variables and linearity of expectation give E[X]=pL+sum_g f_g q_g. If X=0, the residual is a constant of size one. If X>0, any subtree with no surviving nonconstant leaf evaluates to a constant and is collapsed, so every residual leaf descends from one of the X surviving leaves. The residual tree therefore has at most X leaves. A binary tree with t leaves has t-1 internal nodes, hence size at most 2X-1 when X>0. In either case size <=2X+1; taking expectations proves the claim. This repairs the squared-probability target to a linear-probability bound under the stated semantics; it does not establish compatibility with the dossier's intended size measure.

label: S0014
statement: statement: Let T be a finite De Morgan formula tree over literals and constants, with input-variable leaf occurrences and gate-leaf occurrences. Fix a restriction and mark as active each input occurrence whose variable remains live and each gate occurrence whose restricted gate is nonconstant; let X be the number of active occurrences. Simplify T recursively using De Morgan gates: evaluate constant gates, use x AND 1=x, x AND 0=0, x OR 0=x, x OR 1=1 and their dual/complement forms, and suppress unary nodes; never duplicate a subtree. Then the resulting formula has at most X nonconstant leaves, and its node count is at most 2X+1. Consequently, for random restrictions with marginal live probability p on each input variable occurrence and marginal nonconstant probability q_g on each occurrence of gate g, E[size(T|rho)] <= 2(pL + sum_g f_g q_g)+1. Proof: By recursive simplification, every residual subtree either is constant or computes a nonconstant function that depends on at least one active leaf below it. In a residual tree that is not constant, every leaf is nonconstant: a constant child of an AND/OR gate either makes the parent constant or is removed by the neutral-element rule, and the same holds for complemented De Morgan forms. Hence every residual leaf is descended from an active occurrence, so the residual has at most X leaves. A binary tree with t leaves has t-1 internal nodes, giving at most 2X-1 nodes when nonconstant; if constant, it has one node. Thus size <=2X+1. Indicator linearity gives E[X]=pL+sum_g f_g q_g, proving the expectation bound. This conclusion depends on full constant/neutral-element simplification; the weaker rule in S0013 that only evaluates constant subtrees is insufficient (e.g. (x AND 1) AND 1 can retain two constant leaves when x is active).

label: S0015
statement:
statement: Let Phi be a finite formula whose residual size after restriction is defined syntactically, before Boolean simplification, by counting each surviving input-variable leaf occurrence once and replacing every non-surviving input leaf by a constant. If Phi has L input-variable leaf occurrences and each underlying variable is live with marginal probability p, then E[L(Phi|rho)] = pL. Consequently, for Phi=x, p=N^{-alpha} with any fixed alpha>0, and any prefactor a(N)=N^{o(1)}, the bound E[L(Phi|rho)] <= a(N)p^2 L fails for all sufficiently large N.
proof: For each leaf occurrence i, define I_i(rho)=1 when its variable is live and 0 otherwise. By the stipulated syntactic size convention, L(Phi|rho)=sum_{i=1}^L I_i(rho). Therefore linearity of expectation gives E[L(Phi|rho)]=sum_i E[I_i]=pL; no independence is needed. For Phi=x, L=1 and p=N^{-alpha}, so the proposed right side is a(N)N^{-2alpha}, whereas the left side is N^{-alpha}. Since a(N)=N^{o(1)}, the ratio of left to right is N^{alpha-o(1)}, which tends to infinity; thus the inequality fails eventually. The single-variable restriction distribution is pairwise independent vacuously.
scope: Syntactic residual leaf count before Boolean simplification; any finite formula for the equality, and the single-leaf formula for the asymptotic counterexample. This does not address residual size after Boolean simplification.
